lyttos.t: Inland city of central Crete claiming Spartan descent, destroyed by Knossos in the Lyttian War of 220 BCE.
lyttos.o: Lyttos lay on a high plateau of central [[e:crete|Crete]], south-east of [[s:knossos|Knossos]], and was one of the oldest cities on the island; it appears in [[e:homer|Homer]]. Its people claimed to be colonists from [[s:sparta|Sparta]], and ancient writers saw its customs as close to Spartan ones.
lyttos.r: [[e:aristotle|Aristotle]] cites Lyttos as an example of the Cretan constitution with [[e:kosmoi|kosmoi]], a council of elders and common messes. It controlled harbours on the north coast, including [[s:chersonesus-taurica|Chersonesos]]. Lyttos was a staunch enemy of [[s:knossos|Knossos]] and fought it repeatedly for leadership of central [[e:crete|Crete]].
lyttos.e: In the Lyttian War of 220 BCE Knossian forces destroyed Lyttos while its army was away. The city was rebuilt and resisted [[e:rome|Rome]] until [[e:quintus-caecilius-metellus-creticus|Metellus]] took it during the conquest of 69 to 67 BCE. It continued as a Roman town.

lordship-of-sligo.t: The lordship of the O'Connor Sligo, a branch of the royal O'Connors of Connacht, who ruled northern Connacht from Sligo Castle.
lordship-of-sligo.o: The [[e:ua-conchobair-dynasty|O'Connors]] of [[s:kingdom-of-connacht|Connacht]] divided in 1384 into O'Connor Don and O'Connor Roe, while [[e:oconnor-sligo|O'Connor Sligo]], a separate branch descended from Brian Luighnech, controlled Lower Connacht, centred on the town and castle of Sligo.
lordship-of-sligo.r: [[e:oconnor-sligo|O'Connor Sligo]] ruled over lesser lords such as the O'Haras, O'Dowds and MacDonaghs, frequently contesting the area with the [[e:odonnell-dynasty|O'Donnells]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-tir-chonaill|Kingdom of Tir Chonaill]], who often claimed overlordship of Sligo. The town held a Dominican friary and was a busy harbour.
lordship-of-sligo.e: Under the [[e:composition-of-connacht|Composition of Connacht]] in 1585, Sir Donal [[e:oconnor-sligo|O'Connor Sligo]] accepted English tenure. The family's power waned, and their estates were largely lost after the 17th century wars.

lubavians.t: Small Prussian territory around Lubawa on the border with Masovia, given to the first missionary bishop of Prussia in 1216.
lubavians.o: The land of [[e:lubawa|Lubawa]] lay in the south-west of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], next to the [[e:chelmno-land|Chełmno land]] and [[e:masovia|Masovia]]. Its people were [[e:old-prussians|Prussians]], related to the neighbouring [[s:pomesanians|Pomesanians]] and Sasins, and lived in scattered settlements around strongholds.
lubavians.r: Little is recorded of them. Exposed to Polish influence, some of their leaders accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]]: in 1216 Prussian nobles granted the land of [[e:lubawa|Lubawa]] to Christian, the Cistercian missionary [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]], making it one of the first mission territories.
lubavians.e: The area passed under the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] during its conquest of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in the 1230s and was assigned to the [[s:bishopric-of-culm|Bishopric of Culm]], whose [[e:bishop|bishops]] resided at [[e:lubawa|Löbau]] (Lubawa). The Prussian population merged with German and Polish settlers.

lordship-of-beirut.t: A Crusader lordship whose Ibelin lords led the barons of Outremer against Emperor Frederick II.
lordship-of-beirut.o: Baldwin I took [[s:beirut|Beirut]] in May 1110 with Genoese and Pisan ships, and the city became a lordship of the [[s:kingdom-of-jerusalem|Kingdom of Jerusalem]], first held by Fulk of Guines and later by the Brisebarre family.
lordship-of-beirut.r: [[s:beirut|Beirut]] was lost to [[e:saladin|Saladin]] in 1187 and regained by German crusaders in 1197. Its most famous lord, [[e:john-of-ibelin-the-old-lord-of-beirut|John of Ibelin, the Old Lord of Beirut]], rebuilt the citadel and a palace whose marble and mosaics impressed visitors, and led the baronial resistance to the imperial officials of Frederick II in the 1230s. The city traded with [[e:damascus|Damascus]] and [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]], and its lords held lands on both shores.
lordship-of-beirut.e: After the [[s:lordship-of-ibelin|Ibelin]] line ended, [[s:beirut|Beirut]] passed through heiresses. Following the fall of [[e:acre|Acre]] in 1291, its garrison surrendered to the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] in July and the city was dismantled.
ru: John of Ibelin, the Old Lord of Beirut

lordship-of-jerba.t: A Catalan and Sicilian lordship over the Tunisian island of Jerba, held by Christian admirals for half a century until a local revolt.
lordship-of-jerba.o: In 1284, during the [[e:sicilian-vespers|War of the Sicilian Vespers]], the admiral [[e:roger-of-lauria|Roger of Lauria]], serving the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]] and [[e:sicily|Sicily]], seized [[e:djerba|Jerba]] from the [[s:hafsid-sultanate|Hafsid Sultanate]], together with the [[e:kerkennah-islands|Kerkennah]] islands. The pope recognised Lauria's lordship, and he fortified the island with the castle known as the Castello.
lordship-of-jerba.r: A small Christian garrison held the castle while the Ibadi Muslim islanders paid tribute and kept their own law and religion. Revolts were frequent. After the [[e:roger-of-lauria|Lauria]] heirs' rule faltered, the island passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-sicily|Kingdom of Sicily]], and the chronicler [[e:ramon-muntaner|Ramon Muntaner]] governed it from 1311 to about 1315, describing his rule in his Chronicle.
lordship-of-jerba.e: A revolt of the islanders, backed by the [[s:hafsid-sultanate|Hafsids]], overwhelmed the garrison in 1335 and restored [[e:hafsid-dynasty|Hafsid]] rule. [[e:djerba|Jerba]] remained contested between [[e:spain|Spain]], the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] and [[e:tunis|Tunis]] into the 16th century.

lutician-federation.t: A pagan Slavic alliance east of the Elbe that destroyed German rule in 983 and was governed by assemblies and the oracle of the god at Rethra.
lutician-federation.o: The Lutici, or Veleti, were West Slavic tribes between the [[e:elbe|Elbe]] and the [[e:oder-river|Oder]], among them the [[e:redarii|Redarii]], [[e:tollensians|Tollensians]], [[e:circipanians|Circipanians]] and [[e:kessinians|Kessinians]]. In 983 they rose against German rule, destroying the bishoprics of [[e:havelberg|Havelberg]] and [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] and expelling the margraves of the [[s:northern-march|Northern March]] in the [[e:great-slav-rising|Great Slav Rising]].
lutician-federation.r: The federation had no prince; decisions were taken by assemblies of the tribes, and [[e:thietmar-of-merseburg|Thietmar of Merseburg]] describes the temple of [[e:radegast|Radegast]] ([[e:svarozic|Svarożic]]) at [[e:rethra|Rethra]], whose priests consulted oracles. Remarkably, [[e:henry-ii-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Henry II]] allied with the pagan Lutici against the Christian Polish ruler Bolesław I, causing scandal among churchmen.
lutician-federation.e: Internal war among the tribes in 1057 weakened the federation, and in 1068 [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:burchard-ii-of-halberstadt|Burchard of Halberstadt]] destroyed [[e:rethra|Rethra]]. The [[e:wendish-crusade|Wendish Crusade]] of 1147 and campaigns of the [[s:duchy-of-pomerania|Duchy of Pomerania]], [[e:albert-the-bear|Albert the Bear]] and [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] absorbed the Lutician lands by the mid 12th century.

luluid-dynasty.t: The rule of Badr al-Din Lu'lu', a former slave who became master of Mosul, and of his son, ended by the Mongol sack of the city in 1262.
luluid-dynasty.o: [[e:badr-al-din-lulu|Badr al-Din Lu'lu']] was a mamluk, probably of Armenian origin, in the household of [[e:nur-al-din|Nur al-Din]] Arslan Shah of the [[s:zengid-dynasty-of-mosul|Zengid dynasty of Mosul]]. As regent for the last young [[s:zengid-dynasty|Zengids]] he held effective power from the 1210s, and in 1233 the [[e:caliphate|caliph]] recognised him as ruler of [[e:mosul|Mosul]] in his own right.
luluid-dynasty.r: [[e:badr-al-din-lulu|Lu'lu']] was a shrewd survivor, balancing between the [[e:ayyubid-empire|Ayyubids]], the [[s:abbasid-caliphate|Abbasid Caliphate]], the [[e:seljuk-empire|Seljuks]] of Rum and the [[e:mongols|Mongols]], to whom he submitted after 1243. [[e:mosul|Mosul]] under his rule was celebrated for inlaid brass metalwork and [[e:manuscript|manuscript]] painting, and he built shrines, including ones honouring Shia figures, in the city.
luluid-dynasty.e: After [[e:badr-al-din-lulu|Lu'lu']] died in 1259, his son al-[[s:salihids|Salih]] Isma'il rebelled against the [[s:ilkhanate|Ilkhanate]]. [[e:hulagu-khan|Hulagu's]] forces besieged [[e:mosul|Mosul]], which fell in 1262, and al-Salih was executed. Mosul then came under direct Ilkhanid rule.

liang-liang-shidu.t: A rebel state on the Ordos frontier founded during the collapse of Sui, which survived as a client of the Eastern Turks until 628, the last regime to resist the Tang.
liang-liang-shidu.o: [[e:liang-shidu|Liang Shidu]], a local officer in [[e:shuofang-commandery|Shuofang]] commandery on the northern bend of the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]], killed the [[e:sui-dynasty|Sui]] governor in 617 and proclaimed himself emperor of [[s:liang-li-gui|Liang]]. To survive he accepted [[e:vassal|vassal]] status and a title from the [[s:eastern-turkic-khaganate|Eastern Turkic Khaganate]], whose cavalry protected him.
liang-liang-shidu.r: Little is recorded of its administration. It held a thinly populated frontier zone of steppe and farmland and served the Turks as a base for raids into the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] heartland. Its dependence on the khaganate meant its fortunes rose and fell with Turkish power.
liang-liang-shidu.e: When the [[s:eastern-turkic-khaganate|Eastern Turkic Khaganate]] weakened in the late 620s, [[s:later-tang|Tang]] armies besieged [[e:shuofang-commandery|Shuofang]] in 628. [[e:liang-shidu|Liang Shidu]] was killed by his cousin [[s:liang-li-gui|Liang]] Luoren, who surrendered the city, completing the Tang reunification of [[e:china|China]] two years before the Turkish khaganate itself fell.

lavo-kingdom.t: A kingdom of the lower Chao Phraya centred on Lopburi, first a Dvaravati city, then a Khmer provincial seat, and a forerunner of Ayutthaya.
lavo-kingdom.o: Lavo emerged as one of the [[e:mon-people|Mon]] towns of the [[s:dvaravati|Dvaravati]] world, with Lopburi as its centre from about the 7th century. Chronicles say [[e:chamadevi|Chamadevi]] of [[s:hariphunchai|Hariphunchai]] was a Lavo princess. In the 10th and 11th centuries Lavo came under the control of the [[s:khmer-empire|Khmer Empire]].
lavo-kingdom.r: Under [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] rule from the reign of [[e:suryavarman-i|Suryavarman I]], Lopburi was a provincial capital with temples such as [[e:phra-prang-sam-yot|Phra Prang Sam Yot]] and [[e:wat-phra-si-rattana-mahathat-lopburi|Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat]] showing the Khmer style. [[e:mahayana-buddhism|Mahayana Buddhism]] and [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] cults coexisted with older [[e:theravada-buddhism|Theravada]] traditions. Lavo also sent its own missions to the [[e:song-dynasty|Song]] court in the 12th century, and to the Yuan in the late 13th, suggesting periods of independence.
lavo-kingdom.e: As [[e:khmer-empire|Khmer]] power waned in the 13th century, Lavo was linked by marriage and politics with [[s:suphannaphum|Suphannaphum]], and in 1351 [[e:ramathibodi-i|U Thong]] founded the [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya Kingdom]] on the [[e:chao-phraya-river|Chao Phraya]], combining both. Lopburi remained a secondary royal city, used by [[e:narai|King Narai]] as a residence.

lemko-rusyn-republic.t: A small Rusyn republic in the Carpathian foothills, proclaimed by the Lemkos in 1918 and suppressed by Poland in 1920.
lemko-rusyn-republic.o: After the collapse of [[e:austro-hungarian-empire|Austria-Hungary]], the [[e:lemkos|Lemkos]], an [[e:east-slavs|East Slavic]] highland people of western [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Galicia]], held a council at Florynka in December 1918. Led by pro-Russian leaders, they refused to join either [[e:poland|Poland]] or the [[s:west-ukrainian-peoples-republic|West Ukrainian People's Republic]] and proclaimed their own republic, with [[e:yaroslav-kachmarchyk|Yaroslav Kachmarchyk]] as president.
lemko-rusyn-republic.r: The republic had a small council and local administration among [[e:lemkos|Lemko]] villages but no real army or economy of its own. Its leaders hoped for union with [[e:russia|Russia]] or with the [[e:rusyns|Rusyns]] of [[s:czechoslovakia|Czechoslovakia]] and sent delegates to the [[e:paris-peace-conference-1919-1920|Paris Peace Conference]], without success.
lemko-rusyn-republic.e: Polish authorities tolerated the republic for a time but ended it in March 1920, arresting its leaders. The region became part of the [[s:second-polish-republic|Second Polish Republic]], and most [[e:lemkos|Lemkos]] were later deported during the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] and after it.

lusones.t: A Celtiberian people of the upper Tagus and Jalón, among the first to fight Rome in the Celtiberian wars of the early 2nd century BCE.
lusones.o: The Lusones lived on the high plateau around the sources of the [[e:tagus|Tagus]] and the [[e:jalon|Jalón]], between modern [[e:guadalajara-spain|Guadalajara]] and [[e:zaragoza|Zaragoza]]. Appian and [[e:strabo|Strabo]] count them among the [[s:celtiberians|Celtiberians]], and they emerged in the later [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]].
lusones.r: Little is known of their society beyond their hillfort settlements and herding economy on the cold uplands. They appear in Roman narratives mainly as a source of fighting men in the wars of the 2nd century BCE.
lusones.e: In 181 BCE they took part in the First Celtiberian War, which ended with the treaty of [[e:tiberius-sempronius-gracchus-consul-177-bc|Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus]] in 179 BCE. They were drawn into the later wars that ended with [[e:numantia|Numantia]] in 133 BCE and were then absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]].

lakz.t: A medieval Lezgian principality in southern Dagestan, known mainly from Arab geographers, that guarded the mountain hinterland of Derbent.
lakz.o: Lakz is known chiefly from Arab writers of the 10th century such as [[e:al-masudi|al-Masudi]], who describe a numerous and warlike people in the mountains west of [[e:derbent|Derbent]], generally identified with the ancestors of the [[e:lezgins|Lezgins]]. When and how it arose is not recorded; it appears as a principality by the 8th or 9th century.
lakz.r: [[e:al-masudi|Al-Masudi]] reports that the people of Lakz lived in fortified villages, some still pagan, some Muslim, under their own rulers. The land lay in the [[e:samur-river|Samur]] valley and neighbouring mountains, with farming and herding.
lakz.e: In the 11th century Lakz was drawn into the wars of the [[s:shirvanshah-state|Shirvanshahs]] and the [[s:emirate-of-derbent|Emirate of Derbent]] and then overrun by Seljuk raids. It disappears from the sources, though the [[e:lezgins|Lezgin]] communities of its valleys remained.

later-liang.t: The first of the Five Dynasties, founded by the former rebel Zhu Wen when he ended the Tang in 907, with its capital at Kaifeng.
later-liang.o: [[e:zhu-wen|Zhu Wen]], a lieutenant of [[e:huang-chao|Huang Chao]], defected to the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] in 882 and was made governor at [[e:kaifeng|Bianzhou]] (Kaifeng). Over two decades he became the strongest warlord in northern [[e:china|China]], took control of the court, killed [[e:emperor-zhaozong-of-tang|Emperor Zhaozong]] in 904 and in 907 forced the last Tang emperor to abdicate, founding the [[s:liang-dynasty|Liang dynasty]].
later-liang.r: [[s:western-liang-555-587|Later Liang]] held the central plains along the [[e:yellow-river|Yellow River]] and made [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]], at the head of the canal system, its capital, a choice later dynasties followed. Its rule rested on a professional army, but it never subdued its rival [[s:jin-five-dynasties|Jin (Five Dynasties)]] at [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]] and lost a major battle at Bochao in 911. Many regional rulers in the south accepted its titles while governing independently.
later-liang.e: [[e:zhu-wen|Zhu Wen]] was murdered by his son [[e:zhu-yougui|Zhu Yougui]] in 912, who was overthrown by his brother [[e:zhu-youzhen|Zhu Youzhen]] in 913. Jin steadily took [[e:hebei|Hebei]], and in 923 [[e:li-cunxu|Li Cunxu]], now ruler of the [[s:later-tang|Later Tang]], captured [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]]; Zhu Youzhen had himself killed.

lima-culture.t: A culture of the central coast of Peru whose adobe pyramids and irrigation canals laid the foundations of settlement in the valleys where Lima now stands.
lima-culture.o: The [[e:lima|Lima]] culture took shape around 100 CE in the [[e:chillon-river|Chillón]], [[e:rimac-river|Rímac]] and [[e:lurin-river|Lurín]] valleys of [[e:peru|Peru's]] central coast. Communities built canals that turned the desert valleys into farmland and began raising large adobe platform mounds.
lima-culture.r: Its main centre was the Maranga complex in the [[e:rimac-river|Rímac]] valley, with large mounds such as [[e:huaca-san-marcos|Huaca San Marcos]], while [[e:huaca-pucllana|Huaca Pucllana]] in modern [[e:miraflores-lima|Miraflores]] was built of small handmade adobe bricks set like books on a shelf. Society was organised around ceremonial centres led by local elites. The economy combined irrigation farming with fishing. Pottery shows an interlocking serpent and fish design. The early phase of [[e:pachacamac|Pachacamac]] in the [[e:lurin-river|Lurín]] valley also belongs to this culture.
lima-culture.e: From around 650 CE the [[e:lima|Lima]] culture declined as the [[s:wari-empire|Wari Empire]] extended its influence along the coast. [[e:pachacamac|Pachacamac]] continued as a sacred site and later became the centre of [[s:ychsma|Ychsma]]. Many Lima mounds survive among the modern city's streets.

lordship-of-ireland.t: The territory in Ireland held by English kings as lords of Ireland from Henry II's invasion of 1171 until Henry VIII took the title of king in 1542.
lordship-of-ireland.o: [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]] landed at [[e:waterford|Waterford]] in 1171 to control [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Strongbow]] and other Norman adventurers. Irish kings and [[e:bishop|bishops]] submitted to him, and the [[e:papacy|papacy]] endorsed his claim. In 1177 he made his son [[e:john-king-of-england|John]] Lord of Ireland, a title merged with the English crown when John became king.
lordship-of-ireland.r: The lordship was governed from [[e:dublin|Dublin]] by a justiciar or lord deputy, with an [[e:parliament-of-ireland|Irish Parliament]] from the 13th century, English [[e:common-law|common law]] and shires. Norman lords built castles and towns, but from the 14th century Gaelic recovery and the [[e:black-death|Black Death]] shrank English rule to the [[e:the-pale|Pale]] around Dublin, and the [[e:statutes-of-kilkenny|Statutes of Kilkenny]] of 1366 sought to stop settlers adopting Irish ways.
lordship-of-ireland.e: In 1541 the [[e:parliament-of-ireland|Irish Parliament]] declared [[e:henry-viii-of-england|Henry VIII]] King of Ireland, creating the [[s:kingdom-of-ireland|Kingdom of Ireland]] in 1542.

landgraviate-of-klettgau.t: A small landgraviate on the upper Rhine between the Black Forest and Schaffhausen, ruled by the counts of Sulz and then the Schwarzenbergs.
landgraviate-of-klettgau.o: The Klettgau, a fertile district north of the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] near [[s:canton-of-schaffhausen|Schaffhausen]], had been held as a landgraviate by the counts of [[e:habsburg-laufenburg|Habsburg-Laufenburg]]. In 1408 it passed by marriage to the counts of Sulz, who ruled it from [[e:tiengen|Tiengen]].
landgraviate-of-klettgau.r: The counts of Sulz were also hereditary judges of the imperial court at [[s:free-imperial-city-of-rottweil|Rottweil]]. Klettgau's peasants joined the [[e:german-peasants-war|Peasants' War]] of 1525 and were defeated. Losses to [[s:canton-of-zurich|Zürich]] and [[s:canton-of-schaffhausen|Schaffhausen]] reduced the territory, and when the Sulz line died out in 1687 it passed by marriage to the [[s:principality-of-schwarzenberg|Principality of Schwarzenberg]], whose princes ruled it from afar through officials. It remained Catholic.
landgraviate-of-klettgau.e: In 1806 Klettgau was mediatised and placed under the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]], which later bought out the [[e:house-of-schwarzenberg|Schwarzenbergs]]' remaining rights. The district now lies mainly in [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]], with its southern part in the Swiss canton of [[s:canton-of-schaffhausen|Schaffhausen]].

luwu-kingdom.t: The oldest Bugis kingdom in tradition, setting of the I La Galigo epic and source of the iron used for South Sulawesi's weapons.
luwu-kingdom.o: Luwu, at the head of the [[e:gulf-of-bone|Gulf of Bone]], was regarded by the [[e:bugis|Bugis]] as their senior kingdom, the [[e:bantustan|homeland]] of the heroes of the [[e:la-galigo|I La Galigo]] cycle, one of the longest epics in the world. It probably rose in the 14th century, controlling iron ore from the [[e:lake-matano|Lake Matano]] area and trade from the interior highlands.
luwu-kingdom.r: Luwu was ruled by a datu, chosen from a sacred lineage. Its nickel-rich iron was prized for weapons and sold widely in the archipelago. In 1605 its ruler [[e:la-patiware-daeng-parabung|La Patiware Daeng Parabung]] became one of the first in South [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]] to accept [[e:islam|Islam]], taught by [[e:minangkabau-people|Minangkabau]] preachers.
luwu-kingdom.e: Luwu lost ground to the [[s:bone-sultanate|Bone Sultanate]] and the [[s:gowa-sultanate|Gowa Sultanate]] from the 16th century and came under [[e:dutch|Dutch]] control after their conquest of South [[e:sulawesi|Sulawesi]] in 1905. Its datu [[e:andi-djemma|Andi Djemma]] backed the [[e:indonesia|Indonesian Republic]] in 1945 to 1946 and is now a [[e:national-hero-of-indonesia|National Hero of Indonesia]].

latin-league.t: Alliance of the Latin towns around Rome, bound by shared cults and rights, that fought and then partnered Rome until Rome dissolved it in 338 BCE.
latin-league.o: The [[e:latin|Latin]] peoples of the plain south of the [[e:tiber-river|Tiber]] shared a language, the cult of [[e:jupiter-latiaris|Jupiter Latiaris]] on the [[e:monte-cavo|Alban Mount]] and other common sanctuaries from the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]]. By the 6th century BCE they met in council at the grove of Ferentina and dedicated a federal shrine of [[e:diana-mythology|Diana]] at [[e:aricia|Aricia]], whose founding a Latin dictator, Egerius Baebius of [[s:tusculum|Tusculum]], is said to have led.
latin-league.r: The League was a loose association of towns such as [[s:tusculum|Tusculum]], [[e:aricia|Aricia]], [[e:lanuvium|Lanuvium]], [[s:tibur|Tibur]] and [[s:praeneste|Praeneste]], sometimes led by an elected dictator. Members shared rights of trade and intermarriage with each other. After [[e:rome|Rome]] defeated the [[e:latins|Latins]] at [[e:battle-of-lake-regillus|Lake Regillus]] around 496 BCE, the treaty of [[e:spurius-cassius-vecellinus|Spurius Cassius]] in 493 BCE made Rome and the League equal partners in defence, and they jointly founded colonies against the [[s:aequi|Aequi]] and [[s:volsci|Volsci]].
latin-league.e: As [[e:rome|Rome]] came to dominate the alliance, the [[e:latin|Latins]] revolted in the [[e:latin-war|Latin War]] of 340–338 BCE. Rome won, dissolved the League in 338 BCE and made separate treaties with each town. The shared 'Latin rights' survived as a legal status Rome later granted to colonies and provinces.

landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel.t: The largest of the Hessian landgraviates, known for hiring out its soldiers to Britain and for the Wilhelmshöhe palace above Kassel.
landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel.o: When Landgrave [[e:philip-i-landgrave-of-hesse|Philip the Magnanimous]] died in 1567, the [[s:landgraviate-of-hesse|Landgraviate of Hesse]] was divided among his four sons. [[e:william-iv-landgrave-of-hesse-kassel|William IV]], the eldest, received about half, with [[e:kassel|Kassel]] as capital, and [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]] later gained the northern part of Hesse-[[e:marburg|Marburg]] in 1604.
landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel.r: [[e:william-iv-landgrave-of-hesse-kassel|William IV]] was a noted astronomer, and [[e:maurice-landgrave-of-hesse-kassel|Maurice the Learned]] adopted [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]] and in 1605 built the [[e:ottoneum|Ottoneum]], the first permanent [[e:theatre|theatre]] building in [[e:germany|Germany]]. [[e:amalie-elisabeth-of-hanau-munzenberg|Landgravine Amalie Elisabeth]] held the land together in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years' War. In the 18th century the landgraves hired out troops to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], including some 17,000 [[s:chatti|Hessians]] for the [[e:american-revolutionary-war|American War of Independence]], paying for works such as the [[e:hercules-kassel|Hercules monument]] and [[e:bergpark-wilhelmshohe|Wilhelmshöhe]].
landgraviate-of-hesse-kassel.e: In 1803 Landgrave [[e:william-i-elector-of-hesse|William IX]] was made an elector, and [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]] became the Electorate of [[e:hesse|Hesse]]. [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] absorbed it into the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] in 1807; restored in 1813, the electorate was annexed by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1866.

lampsacus.t: Phocaean colony on the Hellespont, famed for its wine and the cult of Priapus, where Epicurus taught and Anaxagoras died.
lampsacus.o: Lampsacus was founded by [[s:phocaea|Phocaea]] c. 654 BCE on the Asian shore of the [[e:hellespont|Hellespont]], on a site said to have been offered by a local king. Its fertile hinterland produced wine that became the city's main export.
lampsacus.r: In the late 6th century BCE the tyrant Hippoclus and his son Aeantides ruled Lampsacus under [[e:persia|Persia]]; Aeantides married a daughter of [[e:hippias-tyrant|Hippias of Athens]]. [[e:artaxerxes-i|Artaxerxes I]] granted the exiled [[e:themistocles|Themistocles]] the city's revenues for wine. Lampsacus paid large tribute in the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. [[e:anaxagoras|Anaxagoras]] spent his last years there, and [[e:epicurus|Epicurus]] taught in the city before moving to [[s:athens|Athens]].
lampsacus.e: Lampsacus appealed to [[e:rome|Rome]] against [[e:antiochus-iii-the-great|Antiochus III]] in 196 BCE and became an ally. It passed into the Roman province of Asia in 129 BCE. The modern town of Lapseki stands on the site.

latin-archbishopric-of-patras.t: Church-ruled state in the north-western Peloponnese, where the Latin archbishops of Patras governed the city as secular lords for over 150 years.
latin-archbishopric-of-patras.o: The [[e:latin|Latin]] archbishop of [[s:barony-of-patras|Patras]] was the senior Catholic churchman of the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]]. Around 1276 the archbishops acquired the rights of the Barony of Patras, giving them lordship over the city and its land in addition to their spiritual role.
latin-archbishopric-of-patras.r: The archbishops governed with the help of canons and knights, while acting as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the princes of [[e:achaea|Achaea]] and increasingly as independent rulers under papal protection. [[s:barony-of-patras|Patras]] traded [[e:silk|silk]] and currants with [[e:italy|Italy]]. To defend themselves from the Turks and [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]], the archbishops placed the city under Venetian administration from 1408 to 1413.
latin-archbishopric-of-patras.e: In 1429 [[e:constantine-xi-palaiologos|Constantine Palaiologos]], future last Byzantine emperor, took [[s:barony-of-patras|Patras]] from Archbishop Pandolfo Malatesta's officials, and the citadel surrendered in 1430. Patras joined the [[s:despotate-of-the-morea|Despotate of the Morea]] until the Ottoman conquest of 1458.

cr.a: Original design: unknown 13th-century artist; Sketch: Gustave Schlumberger (1844–1929)

lower-yafa-sultanate.t: The sultanate of the Afifi family over the lower Yafa highlands north-east of Aden, a small British-protected state until 1967.
lower-yafa-sultanate.o: The [[e:yafa|Yafa]] tribes of the mountains north-east of [[e:aden|Aden]] threw off the authority of the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] in the early 18th century. The confederation split into an upper and a lower part, and the Afifi family established the Lower Yafa sultanate, with its seat at Al Qara.
lower-yafa-sultanate.r: The sultan was more an arbiter among tribes than a ruler with an administration. The region's terraced highlands produced [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and grain, and [[e:yafa|Yafa]]'i men were known as [[e:mercenary|mercenaries]], serving the sultans of [[s:kingdom-of-hadramawt|Hadramawt]] and the [[e:nizam-of-hyderabad|Nizam of Hyderabad]]. Lower Yafa signed a protection treaty with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and became part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]], joining the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]].
lower-yafa-sultanate.e: It was a member of the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]] until 1967, when the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over and the territory was absorbed into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

lordship-of-jever.t: A small Frisian lordship on the North Sea coast, remembered for its last native ruler, Lady Mary, and later held by Catherine the Great.
lordship-of-jever.o: Jeverland was part of the free Frisian lands of [[e:ostringen|Östringen]], [[e:rustringen|Rüstringen]] and [[e:wangerland|Wangerland]], where local chieftains (hovetlinge) rose to power in the 14th century. [[e:edo-wiemken-the-elder|Edo Wiemken the Elder]], active from about 1359, built [[e:jever|Jever]] into a lordship, and his descendants resisted the ambitions of the [[e:house-of-cirksena|Cirksena]] rulers of the [[s:county-of-east-frisia|County of East Frisia]].
lordship-of-jever.r: [[e:mary-of-jever|Mary of Jever]], who ruled from 1517 to 1575, defended her small land against [[e:east-frisia|East Frisia]] by placing it under [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] protection as a fief of [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]]. She extended the castle, granted [[e:jever|Jever]] town rights in 1536 and introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. The economy rested on [[e:cattle|cattle]] farming on the fertile coastal marshes. Childless, she bequeathed Jever to the [[s:county-of-oldenburg|County of Oldenburg]].
lordship-of-jever.e: [[e:jever|Jever]] passed to [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] in 1575, in 1667 to [[s:principality-of-anhalt-zerbst|Anhalt-Zerbst]], and in 1793 to [[e:catherine-the-great|Catherine the Great]] of [[e:russia|Russia]], a [[e:zerbst|Zerbst]] princess. After [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and French occupation it was transferred to the [[s:duchy-of-oldenburg|Duchy of Oldenburg]] in 1818. Jever's castle and brewery remain its landmarks.

later-jin-936-947.t: The third of the Five Dynasties, founded with Khitan help at the price of the Sixteen Prefectures, a loss that shaped China's northern frontier for four centuries.
later-jin-936-947.o: [[e:shi-jingtang|Shi Jingtang]], a [[e:shatuo|Shatuo]] general and son-in-law of [[e:emperor-mingzong-of-later-tang|Emperor Mingzong]] of the [[s:later-tang|Later Tang]], rebelled at [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]] in 936. He won the support of the Khitan emperor [[e:yelu-deguang|Yelü Deguang]] of the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] by promising him the [[e:sixteen-prefectures|Sixteen Prefectures]] around modern [[e:beijing|Beijing]] and [[e:datong|Datong]], and with Khitan troops overthrew the Later Tang.
later-jin-936-947.r: [[e:shi-jingtang|Shi Jingtang]] called himself 'son' of the Khitan emperor and paid annual tribute, which shamed many officials. He moved the capital to [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]]. The cession gave the [[e:liao-dynasty|Liao]] the passes through the mountains north of the plain, leaving later Chinese dynasties exposed.
later-jin-936-947.e: His nephew [[e:shi-chonggui|Shi Chonggui]], who succeeded in 942, refused to remain a [[e:vassal|vassal]]. The Khitan invaded repeatedly and took [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]] at the start of 947, deporting him to [[e:manchuria|Manchuria]]. [[e:liu-zhiyuan|Liu Zhiyuan]], governor at [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]], then founded the [[s:later-han|Later Han]].

lunavada-state.t: A Solanki Rajput state in eastern Gujarat on the Mahi river, one of the states of the Rewa Kantha Agency.
lunavada-state.o: The ruling family claimed descent from the [[s:chaulukya-dynasty|Solanki dynasty]] of [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]], and tradition dates the founding of [[e:lunavada|Lunavada]] to 1434. Little is reliably known about its early rulers.
lunavada-state.r: [[e:lunavada|Lunavada]] was a small agricultural state with forested hills and a sizeable [[e:bhils|Bhil]] population. It paid tribute to the [[e:maratha-empire|Marathas]], especially [[s:baroda-state|Baroda State]] and [[e:scindias|Sindhia]], and from the 19th century came under British supervision in the [[e:rewa-kantha-agency|Rewa Kantha Agency]].
lunavada-state.e: [[e:lunavada|Lunavada]] merged into [[e:bombay-state|Bombay State]] in 1948 and is now the headquarters of [[e:mahisagar-district|Mahisagar district]], [[e:gujarat|Gujarat]].

cr.a: Xufanc from Princely States of India

lycian-league.t: The Lycian League, a federation of Lycian cities with weighted voting, praised by Strabo and cited by the framers of the US Constitution.
lycian-league.o: After the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] freed [[s:lycian-dynasts|Lycia]] from Rhodian rule in 168 BCE, the Lycian cities, which had cooperated for some time, organised a formal federation. [[e:xanthos|Xanthos]], [[e:patara|Patara]], [[e:pinara|Pinara]], [[e:olympos-lycia|Olympos]], [[e:myra|Myra]] and [[e:tlos|Tlos]] were among its six largest members.
lycian-league.r: [[e:strabo|Strabo]] describes 23 member cities sending delegates to a common assembly, with the largest cities having three votes, middling ones two and the smallest one. A federal official, the [[e:lyciarch|Lyciarch]], presided, and the league minted common coins. Its system was later cited in the Federalist Papers.
lycian-league.e: The league kept its autonomy as a Roman ally, but after unrest [[e:claudius|Claudius]] annexed [[s:lycian-dynasts|Lycia]] in 43 CE, making it a province, later joined with [[e:pamphylia|Pamphylia]]. The league survived as a provincial council.

lordship-of-chios.t: Genoese lordship of the Zaccaria family on Chios, granted by Byzantium to defend the island against Turkish raiders and lost to a Greek rising in 1329.
lordship-of-chios.o: [[e:benedetto-zaccaria|Benedetto]] I [[e:zaccaria|Zaccaria]], a Genoese admiral and merchant who already held the rich alum mines of [[s:phocaea|Phocaea]] from the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]], occupied [[s:chios|Chios]] in 1304 to protect it from Turkish [[e:piracy|pirates]]. Emperor [[e:andronikos-ii-palaiologos|Andronikos II]], unable to defend the island himself, recognised Zaccaria rule for a fixed term, which was later renewed.
lordship-of-chios.r: The [[e:zaccaria|Zaccaria]] ruled as nominal Byzantine [[e:vassal|vassals]], but in practice as independent lords. They profited from the island's mastic, wine and [[e:silk|silk]] and from alum trade. [[e:martino-zaccaria|Martino Zaccaria]] built a fleet that fought Turkish raiders successfully, took the title King and Despot of [[e:asia-minor|Asia Minor]] from the [[e:latin|Latin]] pretenders, and struck his own coins.
lordship-of-chios.e: [[e:martino-zaccaria|Martino]]'s growing independence alarmed the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]]. In 1329 the Chiots rose against him with the support of [[e:andronikos-iii-palaiologos|Andronikos III]], who landed with a fleet; Martino was captured and [[s:chios|Chios]] returned to [[s:byzantium|Byzantium]]. The Genoese came back in 1346, creating the [[s:maona-of-chios|Maona of Chios]].

cr.a: See File history below for details.

lordship-of-galloway.t: A semi-independent Gaelic lordship in south-west Scotland, whose lords acted almost as kings until the line ended in 1234.
lordship-of-galloway.o: Galloway takes its name from the [[e:norse-gaels|Gall-Gaidheil]], the 'foreign [[e:gaels|Gaels]]' of mixed Norse and Gaelic descent who settled the region in the 9th and 10th centuries. In the early 12th century [[e:fergus-of-galloway|Fergus of Galloway]] emerged as its ruler, styled king in some sources, and married an illegitimate daughter of Henry I of [[e:england|England]].
lordship-of-galloway.r: The lords of Galloway ruled a land of [[e:cattle|cattle]] and sea-power with its own laws, while founding monasteries such as [[e:dundrennan-abbey|Dundrennan]] and Soulseat and reviving the bishopric of [[e:whithorn|Whithorn]]. Fergus's grandson [[e:roland-lord-of-galloway|Roland]] and great-grandson Alan were great Anglo-Scottish nobles; Alan's fleet raided Ireland and the [[s:kingdom-of-the-isles|Kingdom of the Isles]].
lordship-of-galloway.e: When Alan died in 1234 without a legitimate son, [[e:alexander-ii-of-russia|Alexander II]] divided Galloway between his daughters, crushing a revolt. The lordship became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]]; Alan's grandson was the future [[e:john-king-of-england|King John]] Balliol.

laanemaa.t: Coastal county of western Estonia, centred on Lihula, which became the mainland core of the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek.
laanemaa.o: Läänemaa, known in [[e:latin|Latin]] as Rotalia or Maritima, covered the western coast of [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]] facing the islands of [[s:saaremaa|Saaremaa]] and [[e:hiiumaa|Hiiumaa]]. Its main stronghold was at [[e:lihula|Lihula]], and the area had close ties with the islanders across the narrow straits.
laanemaa.r: Its elders led farming and fishing communities on the low coastal land. In 1220 a Swedish [[e:crusade|crusade]] under [[e:john-i-of-sweden|King John I]] occupied [[e:lihula|Lihula]], but the [[s:saaremaa|Oeselians]] attacked and wiped out the garrison, ending [[e:sweden|Sweden's]] first attempt to gain a foothold in [[s:republic-of-estonia|Estonia]].
laanemaa.e: Läänemaa was subdued by the Germans and [[e:danes|Danes]] by 1224 and became the mainland part of the [[s:bishopric-of-osel-wiek|Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek]], whose [[e:bishop|bishops]] first resided at [[e:lihula|Lihula]] and later at [[e:haapsalu|Haapsalu]] (Hapsal). The name survives in Lääne county.

ly-dynasty.t: The dynasty that founded Thang Long, today's Hanoi, built Vietnam's first lasting state institutions and turned back a Song invasion in 1077.
ly-dynasty.o: In 1009 the court official [[e:ly-thai-to|Ly Cong Uan]], raised in a Buddhist monastery, was chosen to succeed the [[s:early-le-dynasty|Early Le dynasty]] and reigned as Ly Thai To. In 1010 he moved the capital from [[e:hoa-lu|Hoa Lu]] to the site of [[e:dai-la|Dai La]], renaming it [[e:thang-long|Thang Long]], 'rising dragon'. In 1054 the state was renamed [[s:tran-dynasty|Dai Viet]].
ly-dynasty.r: Ly rulers combined Buddhist patronage with Confucian government. They built the One Pillar Pagoda, founded the Temple of Literature in 1070 and held the first civil service examination in 1075. Dikes on the [[e:red-river-asia|Red River]] and a law code strengthened the state. The general [[e:ly-thuong-kiet|Ly Thuong Kiet]] raided [[e:song-dynasty|Song China]] in 1075 and defeated a Song counter-invasion at the [[e:battle-of-nhu-nguyet-river|Nhu Nguyet]] river in 1077.
ly-dynasty.e: From the late 12th century weak rulers let regional clans gain power, and the Tran family came to dominate the court. In 1225 the young empress [[e:ly-chieu-hoang|Ly Chieu Hoang]] was married to [[e:tran-thai-tong|Tran Canh]] and abdicated in his favour, founding the [[s:tran-dynasty|Tran dynasty]].

latvian-socialist-soviet-republic.t: Bolshevik Latvia of 1918-1920, led by Pēteris Stučka, which briefly held Riga before being driven out in the Latvian War of Independence.
latvian-socialist-soviet-republic.o: After [[e:germany|Germany's]] defeat, the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] and the [[e:latvian-riflemen|Latvian Riflemen]] invaded [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]]. On 17 December 1918 a Soviet government under [[e:peteris-stucka|Pēteris Stučka]] proclaimed the Latvian Socialist Soviet Republic, and on 3 January 1919 it took Riga, forcing the national government of [[e:karlis-ulmanis|Kārlis Ulmanis]] to retreat to [[e:liepaja|Liepāja]].
latvian-socialist-soviet-republic.r: The Soviet government nationalised land, industry and housing and created revolutionary tribunals, which carried out hundreds of executions. Food requisitioning caused famine in Riga. Its army controlled most of [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]] in early 1919, and it adopted a constitution in January.
latvian-socialist-soviet-republic.e: [[e:freikorps|German Freikorps]] and the [[e:baltic-landeswehr|Baltic Landeswehr]], with Latvian national units, recaptured Riga on 22 May 1919. The Soviet government held on in [[e:latgale|Latgale]] until Latvian and Polish forces took [[e:daugavpils|Daugavpils]] in January 1920, and it was dissolved. The [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]] signed peace with [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] in August 1920.

lordship-of-ameland.t: A Wadden Sea island that remained a free lordship under the Cammingha family, neutral in the wars around it, until the Orange-Nassau family bought it.
lordship-of-ameland.o: Ameland lay outside the authority of the counts of Holland and the Frisian lands, and from the 15th century the Cammingha family, Frisian chieftains, ruled it as lords, a status the register dates to 1424. They defended its independence against the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] and later the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] provinces.
lordship-of-ameland.r: The island was small, with villages such as Hollum, Ballum and Nes, living from fishing, farming and later whaling, with many 17th-century whaling commanders. Its lords claimed neutrality, which let islanders trade during wars. Ameland accepted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and governed itself through local courts under the lord.
lordship-of-ameland.e: After the Cammingha line ended, the lordship was bought in 1704 for the [[e:house-of-orange-nassau|Orange-Nassau]] family. It lost its separate status in the Batavian period and became part of [[s:lordship-of-frisia|Friesland]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]].

langah-sultanate.t: A sultanate of the Langah tribe that ruled Multan in the southern Punjab for some eighty years in the 15th and early 16th centuries.
langah-sultanate.o: Around 1445, as the [[e:sayyid-dynasty|Sayyid]] rulers of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] lost control of the [[e:punjab|Punjab]], the people of [[e:multan|Multan]] chose a local [[e:sufism|Sufi]] family leader as ruler. Shortly afterwards Rai Sahra, chief of the Langah tribe, took power and reigned as [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Qutb al-Din, founding a dynasty based at Multan.
langah-sultanate.r: [[e:husain-shah-langah|Husain Shah Langah]], the most important ruler, reigned for about three decades, repelled attacks from [[e:bahlul-lodi|Bahlul Lodi]] of [[e:delhi|Delhi]] and expanded towards [[e:sindh|Sindh]] and the [[e:indus|Indus]] frontier. [[e:multan|Multan]] was a centre of [[e:sufism|Sufi]] shrines, notably those of [[e:bahauddin-zakariya|Bahauddin Zakariya]] and [[e:shah-rukn-e-alam|Shah Rukn-e-Alam]], and of trade between [[e:india|India]] and [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]].
langah-sultanate.e: [[e:shah-husain-arghun|Shah Husain Arghun]] of the [[s:arghun-dynasty|Arghun dynasty]], ruling [[e:sindh|Sindh]], besieged and captured [[e:multan|Multan]] around 1526, ending Langah rule. Multan soon passed to the [[s:mughal-empire|Mughal Empire]] and became the seat of a Mughal province.

latvian-self-administration.t: Latvian auxiliary administration under German occupation from 1942 to 1945, headed by General Oskars Dankers.
latvian-self-administration.o: [[e:germany|Germany]] placed occupied [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]] in the [[e:generalkommissariat-lettland|Generalkommissariat Lettland]] of [[s:reichskommissariat-ostland|Reichskommissariat Ostland]]. Latvian directors-general were appointed in 1941 to handle local affairs, and in March 1942 the structure was formalised as the Latvian Self-Administration under General [[e:oskars-dankers|Oskars Dankers]].
latvian-self-administration.r: The Self-Administration had no political independence and executed German orders on economic, educational and social matters. In 1943 the Germans used it to [[e:conscription|conscript]] Latvian men into the [[e:latvian-legion|Latvian Legion]] of the [[e:waffen-ss|Waffen-SS]]. Most of Latvia's [[e:jews|Jews]] had already been murdered in 1941, notably at [[e:rumbula-massacre|Rumbula]].
latvian-self-administration.e: The [[e:red-army|Red Army]] retook Riga in October 1944, and the administration moved to [[e:courland|Courland]] and then [[e:germany|Germany]], ending with the German surrender in May 1945. [[s:republic-of-latvia|Latvia]] was again governed as the [[s:latvian-soviet-socialist-republic|Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic]].

lordship-of-andros.t: Latin lordship on the Cycladic island of Andros, a vassal of the Duchy of the Archipelago that survived until the Ottoman takeover in 1566.
lordship-of-andros.o: Around 1207 the Venetian Marino Dandolo, a companion of [[e:marco-sanudo|Marco Sanudo]], conquered [[s:andros|Andros]] from the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] and held it as a fief under Sanudo's [[s:duchy-of-the-archipelago|Duchy of the Archipelago]]. The island was fertile and well placed on the sea route between [[e:euboea|Euboea]] and the central [[e:cyclades|Cyclades]].
lordship-of-andros.r: A small Italian elite held the castle and the best land, while Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] islanders produced [[e:silk|silk]], wine and grain. The lordship passed among Venetian families, including the Ghisi, Sanudo and Zeno, and was disputed in dynastic quarrels with the dukes of [[s:naxos|Naxos]]. Pietro Zeno held it from 1384, and from about 1440 the Sommaripa family, starting with Crusino I, ruled it for most of its remaining history.
lordship-of-andros.e: Increasing Turkish raids left [[s:andros|Andros]] dependent on Venetian protection and Ottoman tolerance. In 1566, when the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] removed the last [[e:crispo-family|Crispo]] duke of [[s:naxos|Naxos]], they also ended Sommaripa rule on Andros, which was annexed to the empire.

lordship-of-dejanovic.t: Lordship of the Dejanović brothers in eastern Macedonia and western Bulgaria, Ottoman vassals whose daughter became a Byzantine empress.
lordship-of-dejanovic.o: The sebastokrator [[e:dejan-sebastokrator|Dejan]], a [[e:magnates|magnate]] and brother-in-law of [[e:stefan-dusan|Stefan Dušan]], held lands around [[e:kumanovo|Kumanovo]] in the [[s:serbian-empire|Serbian Empire]]. After Dušan's death his sons [[e:jovan-dragas|Jovan Dragaš]] and [[e:konstantin-dragas|Konstantin Dragaš]] built an autonomous lordship stretching from Kumanovo to [[e:kyustendil|Velbazhd]] (Kyustendil) and [[e:strumica|Strumica]].
lordship-of-dejanovic.r: The brothers ruled from [[e:kyustendil|Velbazhd]] and [[e:strumica|Strumica]], taxing the trade routes between the [[e:vardar|Vardar]] and the [[e:struma|Struma]]. After the [[e:battle-of-maritsa|Maritsa]] in 1371 they became Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassals]], supplying troops. They endowed monasteries on [[s:monastic-community-of-mount-athos|Mount Athos]] and in [[e:macedonia-region|Macedonia]]. Konstantin's daughter [[e:helena-dragas|Helena]] married the Byzantine emperor [[e:manuel-ii-palaiologos|Manuel II]] and was the mother of the last emperor, [[e:constantine-xi-palaiologos|Constantine XI]].
lordship-of-dejanovic.e: Jovan died around 1378. Konstantin was killed fighting as an Ottoman [[e:vassal|vassal]] at [[e:battle-of-rovine|Rovine]] in 1395, and the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] annexed his lands.

leeward-islands-colony.t: Umbrella colony that grouped Britain's northern Lesser Antilles under one governor for nearly three centuries, from Antigua to the Virgin Islands.
leeward-islands-colony.o: In 1671 the crown separated the Leeward Caribee Islands from [[s:barbados|Barbados]] and gave them their own governor-in-chief, first [[e:charles-wheler|Sir Charles Wheler]] and then [[e:william-stapleton-1st-baronet|Sir William Stapleton]]. The group comprised [[s:colony-of-antigua|Antigua]], [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]], [[s:colony-of-nevis|Nevis]] and [[s:montserrat|Montserrat]], later joined by [[e:barbuda|Barbuda]], [[e:anguilla|Anguilla]] and the [[s:british-virgin-islands|British Virgin Islands]]. A general legislature met occasionally from the 1680s.
leeward-islands-colony.r: Each island kept its own assembly and lieutenant governor, while the governor-in-chief, usually based at [[e:st-johns-antigua-and-barbuda|St John's]] on [[s:colony-of-antigua|Antigua]], handled defence and relations with [[e:london|London]]. Between 1816 and 1833 the islands were split into two governments. In 1871 they became a formal federal colony with a single legislature, which included [[s:commonwealth-of-dominica|Dominica]] until 1940. Their economies rested on [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], and later on [[e:cotton|cotton]] and small farming.
leeward-islands-colony.e: The federal colony was dissolved in 1956, and its members joined the [[s:west-indies-federation|West Indies Federation]] in 1958, though the shared governorship lingered briefly. Its former members became [[s:antigua-and-barbuda|Antigua and Barbuda]], [[s:saint-kitts-and-nevis|Saint Kitts and Nevis]], and the territories of [[s:montserrat|Montserrat]], [[e:anguilla|Anguilla]] and the [[s:british-virgin-islands|British Virgin Islands]].

laguatan.t: A great Berber confederation of the Libyan desert that fought Byzantine Africa and survived as the Lawata tribe of Arab writers.
laguatan.o: The Laguatan (Leuathae in [[e:procopius|Procopius]], Lawata in Arabic sources) were a confederation of [[e:camel|camel]]-using [[e:berbers|Berber]] tribes that moved west from the Syrtic region and [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] in the 5th and 6th centuries, perhaps including the earlier [[s:austuriani|Austuriani]]. They first appear as a serious power in the wars of [[s:praetorian-prefecture-of-africa|Byzantine Africa]].
laguatan.r: The confederation was led by chiefs, and its leader Ierna was also priest of the god [[e:gurzil|Gurzil]], whose image was carried into battle, according to the [[e:latin|Latin]] poet [[e:corippus|Corippus]]. In 543 the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] killed Laguatan envoys at [[s:leptis-magna|Leptis Magna]], setting off a long war. The general [[e:john-troglita|John Troglita]] defeated them and their allies in 546 to 548, after which they paid tribute to the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]].
laguatan.e: The Laguatan remained powerful in the desert. When the [[e:arabs|Arabs]] arrived in the 640s, the Lawata were among the first [[e:berbers|Berbers]] they met in [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] and [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]]; many converted to [[e:islam|Islam]], later often to [[e:ibadism|Ibadism]], and Lawata groups spread across [[e:north-africa|North Africa]].

lordship-of-plauen.t: Vogtland lordship of the imperial advocates of Plauen, whose family gave the Vogtland its name and a Grand Master to the Teutonic Order.
lordship-of-plauen.o: The advocates of [[e:weida|Weida]], imperial officials whose men were all named Henry, governed lands on the upper [[e:white-elster|Elster]] and [[e:saale|Saale]] for the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] emperors. From about 1209 a branch ruled [[e:plauen|Plauen]], and the whole region came to be called the Vogtland after their title. Over time they treated the office as a hereditary lordship.
lordship-of-plauen.r: The lords ruled a hilly district of farms, forests and small towns from [[e:plauen|Plauen]]. Family members served as knights and administrators, and [[e:heinrich-von-plauen|Heinrich von Plauen]] defended [[e:malbork-castle|Marienburg]] after the [[e:battle-of-grunwald|Battle of Grunwald]] and became Grand Master of the [[s:state-of-the-teutonic-order|State of the Teutonic Order]]. The [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettins]] and Bohemian kings steadily eroded their power; in 1466 the Wettins took Plauen.
lordship-of-plauen.e: [[e:henry-iv-of-plauen|Henry IV of Plauen]], Burgrave of [[e:meissen|Meissen]] and Bohemian chancellor, recovered [[e:plauen|Plauen]] in 1547. His line died out in 1572 and the lands passed to [[e:saxony|Saxony]]. Another branch of the family survived as the princes of [[e:house-of-reuss|Reuss]], rulers in eastern [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] until 1918.

lordship-of-beaujeu.t: The barony of the Beaujolais hills between Lyon and Mâcon, whose lords founded Villefranche-sur-Saône and served the French crown before it passed to the Bourbons.
lordship-of-beaujeu.o: The lords of [[e:beaujeu|Beaujeu]] appear in the 10th century as castellans in the hills west of the [[e:saone|Saône]], between the counts of [[e:macon|Mâcon]] and [[s:county-of-forez|Forez]] and the archbishops of [[e:lyon|Lyon]]. Their castle at Beaujeu gave its name to the Beaujolais, and they gradually brought the surrounding parishes under their control.
lordship-of-beaujeu.r: The lords built a compact barony and around 1140 founded [[e:villefranche-sur-saone|Villefranche-sur-Saône]], which became its commercial centre and later capital. Vineyards and the [[e:saone|Saône]] trade underpinned its economy. Lords such as Humbert V, constable of [[e:france|France]], rose high in royal service, and the family married into the houses of [[s:county-of-forez|Forez]] and [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]].
lordship-of-beaujeu.e: In 1400 the last lord, Edward II, childless and in debt, left the Beaujolais to [[e:louis-ii-duke-of-bourbon|Louis II, Duke of Bourbon]], and it joined the [[s:duchy-of-bourbon|Duchy of Bourbon]]. After the [[s:ile-bourbon|Bourbon]] lands were confiscated in 1527, it passed through several holders before ending up in the [[e:orleans|Orléans]] family.

lordship-of-limpurg.t: Franconian-Swabian lordship of the Schenks of Limpurg, hereditary imperial cupbearers, ruled from Gaildorf until the line died out in 1713.
lordship-of-limpurg.o: The [[e:schenk-von-limpurg|Schenks of Limpurg]] were imperial ministerials who held the hereditary office of [[e:cupbearer|cupbearer]] of the Empire. Around 1230 they built Limpurg castle above [[s:free-imperial-city-of-schwabisch-hall|Schwäbisch Hall]], and they acquired lands in the [[e:kocher|Kocher]] valley and the forests of the Limpurg uplands, forming a lordship held directly from the Empire.
lordship-of-limpurg.r: The lordship was rural, with forests, farms and small towns such as [[e:gaildorf|Gaildorf]] and [[e:obersontheim|Obersontheim]]. Relations with the [[s:free-imperial-city-of-schwabisch-hall|Free Imperial City of Schwäbisch Hall]] were tense, and in 1541 the [[e:schenk-von-limpurg|Schenks]] sold Limpurg castle to the city. The family adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] and divided into branches with residences at Gaildorf and Sontheim. The imperial [[e:cupbearer|cupbearer]] title gave them a ceremonial role at coronations.
lordship-of-limpurg.e: The last male [[e:schenk-von-limpurg|Schenk]] died in 1713, and the lands were divided among female heirs and their families, with [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] claiming part of the inheritance. The fragmented Limpurg lands were mediatised and passed to Württemberg in 1806.

lordship-of-utrecht.t: The former bishops' lands around Utrecht under Habsburg rule, where the Union of Utrecht, founding act of the Dutch Republic, was signed in 1579.
lordship-of-utrecht.o: Weakened by wars with [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]] and Holland, [[e:henry-of-the-palatinate|Bishop Henry of Bavaria]] transferred the temporal power of the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-utrecht|Prince-Bishopric of Utrecht]] to [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] in 1528. The [[e:nedersticht|Nedersticht]] became the Lordship of Utrecht, one of the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Seventeen Provinces]] of the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburg]] [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]].
lordship-of-utrecht.r: [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] built the [[e:vredenburg|Vredenburg]] castle in Utrecht to control the city and governed through a stadtholder shared with Holland. The province kept its own estates, with the cathedral chapters forming an influential first estate. The [[e:bishop|bishop]] remained a purely spiritual figure, and Utrecht became an archbishopric in 1559.
lordship-of-utrecht.e: Utrecht joined the Revolt; the citizens demolished [[e:vredenburg|Vredenburg]] in 1577, and the [[e:union-of-utrecht|Union of Utrecht]] was concluded there in 1579. After the [[e:act-of-abjuration|Act of Abjuration]] in 1581 it became a province of the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]].

larissa.t: Chief city of Thessaly on the Peneios river, seat of the powerful Aleuad family and of the Thessalian League.
larissa.o: Larissa grew on a low hill by the [[e:pineios-thessaly|Peneios]] in the plain of northern [[e:thessaly|Thessaly]], inhabited since the [[e:neolithic|Neolithic]]. In the Archaic period it became the leading city of the [[s:thessalian-league|Thessalian League]] under the [[e:aleuadae|Aleuad]] family, who claimed descent from [[e:heracles|Heracles]]. [[e:aleuas-the-red|Aleuas the Red]] was credited with organising Thessaly into four districts.
larissa.r: Larissa's landed aristocracy ruled over serfs called penestai and bred horses for cavalry. The [[e:aleuadae|Aleuad]] Thorax supported [[e:xerxes-i|Xerxes]] in 480 BCE. Later Larissa welcomed the sophist [[e:gorgias|Gorgias]], and [[e:hippocrates|Hippocrates]] died there. The Aleuads invited [[e:philip-ii-of-macedon|Philip II]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-macedon|Kingdom of Macedon]] to intervene against the tyrants of [[s:tyranny-of-pherae|Pherae]].
larissa.e: From the 340s BCE Larissa was effectively under Macedonian control. After [[e:titus-quinctius-flamininus|Flamininus]] proclaimed Greek freedom in 196 BCE it became the seat of the revived [[s:thessalian-league|Thessalian League]] and passed under Roman control in 146 BCE; it is a major Greek city today.
