lithuanian-byelorussian-ssr.t: Litbel, a short-lived Soviet republic joining Lithuania and Belarus in 1919, created as a buffer against Poland and soon overrun.
lithuanian-byelorussian-ssr.o: In February 1919 [[e:moscow|Moscow]] merged the Soviet republics of [[s:republic-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] and [[e:byelorussian-ssr|Byelorussia]], including the [[s:socialist-soviet-republic-of-byelorussia|Socialist Soviet Republic of Byelorussia]], into a single Lithuanian-Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic, known as [[e:lithuanian-byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic|Litbel]]. Its capital was [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]], and [[e:vincas-mickevicius-kapsukas|Vincas Mickevicius-Kapsukas]] chaired its council of people's commissars.
lithuanian-byelorussian-ssr.r: [[e:lithuanian-byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic|Litbel]] was a Bolshevik state with nationalised land and industry, governed by the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Communist Party]] and backed by the [[e:red-army|Red Army]]. It was intended as a buffer between [[s:russian-sfsr|Soviet Russia]] and [[e:poland|Poland]], but it had little popular support among [[e:lithuanians|Lithuanians]], [[e:poles|Poles]] or [[e:belarusians|Belarusians]] and controlled only part of the territory it claimed.
lithuanian-byelorussian-ssr.e: The Polish army captured [[e:vilnius|Vilnius]] in April 1919 and [[e:minsk|Minsk]] in August, and the Lithuanian army pushed from the west. [[e:lithuanian-byelorussian-soviet-socialist-republic|Litbel]] effectively ceased to exist by the summer of 1919. The [[s:byelorussian-ssr|Byelorussian SSR]] was re-created in 1920.

lower-navarre.t: The fragment of the Kingdom of Navarre north of the Pyrenees, ruled by the Albret kings and the future Henry IV until its union with France in 1620.
lower-navarre.o: Ferdinand of Aragon conquered the [[s:kingdom-of-navarre|Kingdom of Navarre]] south of the [[e:pyrenees|Pyrenees]] in 1512. The [[e:house-of-albret|Albret]] kings kept a small Basque-speaking territory on the northern side around [[e:saint-jean-pied-de-port|Saint-Jean-Pied-de-Port]] and [[e:saint-palais-pyrenees-atlantiques|Saint-Palais]], which [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] gave up around 1530 as too hard to hold.
lower-navarre.r: The [[e:house-of-albret|Albret]] monarchs, who also ruled neighbouring [[s:viscounty-of-bearn|Béarn]], kept the royal title and [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre's]] own estates and courts, with [[e:saint-palais-pyrenees-atlantiques|Saint-Palais]] as the seat of government. [[e:jeanne-dalbret|Queen Jeanne d'Albret]] converted to [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]] and promoted it, though most [[e:basques|Basques]] stayed Catholic. Her son [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry III of Navarre]] became Henry IV of [[e:france|France]] in 1589.
lower-navarre.e: [[e:henry-iv-of-france|Henry IV]] kept [[e:kingdom-of-navarre|Navarre]] separate from [[e:france|France]]. In 1620 [[e:louis-xiii-of-france|Louis XIII]] issued an edict uniting Lower Navarre and [[s:viscounty-of-bearn|Béarn]] with the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]], and French kings were styled 'King of France and Navarre' until 1830.

lordship-of-lemnos.t: Venetian family lordship on the northern Aegean island of Lemnos after the Fourth Crusade, whose lords bore the title of megadux of the Latin Empire.
lordship-of-lemnos.o: Around 1207 the Venetian noble [[e:filocalo-navigajoso|Filocalo Navigajoso]] seized [[e:lemnos|Lemnos]] from the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] as part of the [[e:latin|Latin]] carve-up of the [[e:aegean|Aegean]] after the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]]. The Latin emperor named him megadux, grand duke, giving him a high rank in the [[s:latin-empire|Latin Empire]], and his heirs kept both title and island.
lordship-of-lemnos.r: Little is known of how the Navigajoso governed. They held the island as a hereditary fief, collecting revenues from a Greek [[e:eastern-orthodox-church|Orthodox]] population of farmers and herders, and depended on their link to [[e:venice|Venice]] and the [[s:latin-empire|Latin Empire]] for support. [[e:lemnos|Lemnos]] was valued for its grain and its position near the [[e:hellespont|Dardanelles]].
lordship-of-lemnos.e: After the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] recaptured [[e:constantinople|Constantinople]] in 1261, the island was exposed. The admiral [[e:licario|Licario]], serving [[e:michael-viii-palaiologos|Michael VIII Palaiologos]], besieged the Navigajoso and took [[e:lemnos|Lemnos]] around 1278, returning it to Byzantine rule.

libu.t: The Libyan people west of Egypt whose attacks on the Delta alarmed the pharaohs and whose name became the Greek word 'Libya'.
libu.o: The Libu (Rebu) lived along the coast of what is now eastern [[e:libya|Libya]], in [[e:cyrenaica|Cyrenaica]] and [[e:marmarica|Marmarica]]. They appear in Egyptian records from the 13th century BCE, when, together with the [[s:meshwesh|Meshwesh]] and seafaring peoples, they tried to move into the fertile western Delta.
libu.r: Little is known of their internal organisation beyond rule by chiefs. Around 1208 BCE their chief [[e:meryey|Meryey]], son of Did, led a coalition including [[e:sea-peoples|Sea Peoples]] against [[e:merneptah|Merneptah]], who defeated it at Perire and claimed over six thousand [[e:libyans|Libyans]] killed. [[e:ramesses-iii|Ramesses III]] fought them again. Like the [[s:meshwesh|Meshwesh]], many were later settled in the western Delta, where chiefs bearing the title 'Great Chief of the Libu' ruled from [[e:sais|Sais]] by the 8th century BCE.
libu.e: The Libu chieftaincy at [[e:sais|Sais]] gave rise to the [[s:twenty-fourth-dynasty-of-egypt|Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt]] and later the [[s:twenty-sixth-dynasty-of-egypt|Twenty-sixth Dynasty]]. Their name passed to the [[e:greeks|Greeks]] as '[[e:libya|Libya]]', used for all of [[e:africa|Africa]] west of [[e:egypt|Egypt]].

landgraviate-of-hesse-homburg.t: Small Hessian landgraviate in the Taunus, home of the soldier-prince of Kleist's drama and later of a celebrated spa and casino.
landgraviate-of-hesse-homburg.o: Hesse-Homburg was established in 1622 when [[e:louis-v-landgrave-of-hesse-darmstadt|Landgrave Louis V]] of [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]] granted [[e:bad-homburg-vor-der-hohe|Homburg vor der Höhe]] to his brother [[e:frederick-i-landgrave-of-hesse-homburg|Frederick I]] as an [[e:appanage|appanage]]. It remained dependent on Hesse-[[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] for most of its history rather than a fully sovereign state.
landgraviate-of-hesse-homburg.r: Frederick II, who lost a leg in Swedish service and commanded the [[e:brandenburg|Brandenburg]] cavalry at [[e:battle-of-fehrbellin|Fehrbellin]] in 1675, built the baroque palace and inspired [[e:heinrich-von-kleist|Heinrich von Kleist's]] play [[e:the-prince-of-homburg|The Prince of Homburg]]. Later landgraves welcomed [[e:huguenots|Huguenot]] and Waldensian refugees. In the 19th century Homburg grew into a fashionable spa, and its casino, opened in 1841, drew visitors from across [[e:europe|Europe]].
landgraviate-of-hesse-homburg.e: Hesse-Homburg was mediatised to [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]] in 1806 but restored as a sovereign member of the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] in 1815, gaining [[e:meisenheim|Meisenheim]]. The line died out in 1866, the lands passed briefly to the Grand Duchy of [[e:hesse|Hesse]] and were then annexed by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].

lordship-of-groningen.t: The city of Groningen and its surrounding Ommelanden under Habsburg rule, a reluctant province that joined the Dutch Republic only after a siege in 1594.
lordship-of-groningen.o: [[e:groningen|Groningen]], a Hanseatic city that dominated the Frisian [[e:ommelanden|Ommelanden]] around it, resisted [[e:saxons|Saxon]] rule and placed itself under [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-guelders|Charles of Egmond]], duke of [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]], in 1515. When Guelders weakened, the city and countryside accepted [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] as lord in 1536, joining the [[s:habsburg-netherlands|Habsburg Netherlands]].
lordship-of-groningen.r: Stad en Lande, the city and the lands, was governed by its own estates in which the city and the rural [[e:ommelanden|Ommelanden]] constantly quarrelled over staple rights and taxes. The [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] ruled through a stadtholder. [[e:groningen|Groningen]] traded grain and [[e:cattle|cattle]] and kept close ties with the German [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanse]].
lordship-of-groningen.e: In 1580 the stadtholder [[e:george-van-lalaing-count-of-rennenberg|Rennenberg]] went over to the Spanish side, keeping [[e:groningen|Groningen]] royalist. [[e:maurice-prince-of-orange|Maurice of Nassau]] besieged and took the city in 1594, and it joined the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]] as a province.

lordship-of-molina.t: A semi-independent Castilian lordship on the borders of Aragon, ruled by the Lara family and governed by its own celebrated fuero.
lordship-of-molina.o: [[e:alfonso-i-of-aragon|Alfonso I of Aragon]] took [[e:molina-de-aragon|Molina]] around 1129. It was soon granted to the Castilian noble [[e:manrique-perez-de-lara|Manrique Pérez de Lara]], who held it under Castilian overlordship and in 1154 gave the town and its land a fuero, a charter of rights for settlers.
lordship-of-molina.r: [[e:molina-de-aragon|Molina]] was a frontier lordship of herders and settlers between [[s:kingdom-of-castile|Castile]] and Aragon, defended by its great castle. Its lords issued laws and raised troops with considerable autonomy. In the 13th century the heiress Mafalda married the infante [[e:alfonso-de-molina|Alfonso de Molina]], brother of [[e:ferdinand-iii-of-castile|Ferdinand III]], tying it closer to the Castilian royal family.
lordship-of-molina.e: [[e:blanca-alfonso-de-molina|Blanca Alfonso de Molina]] died childless in 1293, and the lordship passed to her half-sister [[e:maria-de-molina|María de Molina]], queen of [[e:sancho-iv-of-castile|Sancho IV]], and thus to the [[s:crown-of-castile|Crown of Castile]]. Spanish kings still bear the title Lord of [[e:molina-de-aragon|Molina]].

lordship-of-sidon.t: One of the four great baronies of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, whose lords built Sidon's Sea Castle and the fortress of Beaufort.
lordship-of-sidon.o: [[s:sidon|Sidon]] surrendered in December 1110 to Baldwin I, helped by the Norwegian king [[e:sigurd-the-crusader|Sigurd the Crusader]] and his fleet. The city was granted to [[e:eustace-grenier|Eustace Grenier]], and his descendants held it as one of the kingdom's chief lordships.
lordship-of-sidon.r: The lordship included the coast between [[s:beirut|Beirut]] and [[s:tyre|Tyre]] and inland castles such as [[e:beaufort-castle-lebanon|Beaufort]] above the [[e:litani-river|Litani]]. [[e:reynald-of-sidon|Reynald of Sidon]] spoke Arabic and was respected by [[e:saladin|Saladin]], with whom he negotiated while holding Beaufort in 1189-1190. The [[e:sidon-sea-castle|Sea Castle]] on an island in the harbour was built in 1228. [[e:sugar-plantation|Sugar]] and trade with [[e:damascus|Damascus]] supported the economy.
lordship-of-sidon.e: Lost in 1187 and recovered in the 13th century, [[s:sidon|Sidon]] was sacked by the [[e:mongols|Mongols]] in 1260, and [[e:julian-grenier|Julian Grenier]] sold it to the [[e:knights-templar|Templars]], who held it until the [[e:mamluk|Mamluks]] took it in 1291.

lesser-goguryeo.t: A remnant Goguryeo state in Liaodong under Tang suzerainty, ruled by descendants of the last Goguryeo king.
lesser-goguryeo.o: After [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] fell in 668, [[e:tang-dynasty|Tang China]] tried to govern the [[e:liaodong|Liaodong]] region through members of the former royal house. In 699 [[e:go-deokmu|Go Deokmu]], a son of King [[e:bojang-of-goguryeo|Bojang]], was appointed to govern the Goguryeo population there, and his line developed a semi-independent polity.
lesser-goguryeo.r: Known only from brief mentions in Chinese sources, Lesser [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] was a dependency of [[s:later-tang|Tang]] that sent envoys to the Chinese court in the 8th century. Nothing reliable is known of its internal organisation, and some historians question whether it was ever a distinct state.
lesser-goguryeo.e: It disappears from the records in the early 9th century and is usually thought to have been absorbed by [[s:balhae|Balhae]] under King [[e:seon-of-balhae|Seon]] around 820.

lordship-of-rhodes.t: Independent Byzantine lordship on Rhodes under the Gabalas family after the fall of Constantinople in 1204, later absorbed by the Empire of Nicaea.
lordship-of-rhodes.o: When the [[e:fourth-crusade|Fourth Crusade]] broke up the [[s:byzantine-empire|Byzantine Empire]] in 1204, the Greek official [[e:leo-gabalas|Leo Gabalas]] took control of [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] and neighbouring islands and ruled them as his own domain, styling himself Caesar and lord of [[e:rhodes|Rhodes]] and the [[e:cyclades|Cyclades]].
lordship-of-rhodes.r: [[e:leo-gabalas|Gabalas]] ruled as an independent Greek lord with a fleet that let him trade and bargain. Under pressure from [[e:john-iii-doukas-vatatzes|John III Vatatzes]] of [[e:nicaea|Nicaea]], who sent an expedition in 1233, he accepted Nicaean overlordship. In 1234 he made a treaty with [[e:venice|Venice]] granting its merchants trading rights while securing Venetian support. His brother [[e:john-gabalas|John Gabalas]] succeeded him around 1240.
lordship-of-rhodes.e: In 1248 the Genoese seized [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] in a surprise attack. [[e:nicaea|Nicaea]] recaptured the island around 1250 and ruled it directly as part of the [[s:empire-of-nicaea|Empire of Nicaea]]. In 1310 it fell to the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Knights Hospitaller]], becoming [[s:hospitaller-rhodes|Hospitaller Rhodes]].

livonian-brothers-of-the-sword.t: Crusading military order founded in Riga in 1202, which conquered Livonia and Estonia before being destroyed at Saule in 1236.
livonian-brothers-of-the-sword.o: [[e:albert-of-riga|Bishop Albert of Riga]] and the Cistercian [[e:theoderich-von-treyden|Theoderich]] founded the Brothers of the Sword in 1202 to provide a permanent army for the Livonian [[e:crusade|crusade]], modelled on the [[e:knights-templar|Templars]]. [[e:pope-innocent-iii|Pope Innocent III]] approved it in 1204, and its knights wore a white mantle with a red sword and cross.
livonian-brothers-of-the-sword.r: The Order's knight-brothers, mostly from [[e:saxony|Saxony]] and [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]], lived under a monastic rule and governed conquered land from castles such as [[e:cesis|Wenden]] (Cēsis) and [[e:viljandi|Fellin]]. The [[e:bishop|bishop]] granted them a third of conquered territory. Under masters [[e:wenno|Wenno]] and [[e:volquin|Volquin]] they subdued the [[e:livonians|Livs]], [[e:latgalians|Latgalians]] and [[e:estonians|Estonians]], often quarrelling with the bishops and with [[e:denmark|Denmark]] over the spoils.
livonian-brothers-of-the-sword.e: In 1236 a [[e:crusade|crusade]] against [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] ended in disaster at the [[e:battle-of-saule|Battle of Saule]], where [[e:samogitians|Samogitians]] and [[s:semigallians|Semigallians]] killed Master [[e:volquin|Volquin]] and about fifty brothers. The survivors were incorporated in 1237 into the [[e:teutonic-order|Teutonic Order]] as its Livonian branch, the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]].

lordship-of-oultrejordain.t: The Crusader lordship east of the Jordan, whose castles of Kerak and Montreal controlled the routes between Syria, Egypt and Arabia.
lordship-of-oultrejordain.o: Baldwin I built the castle of [[e:shobak-castle|Montreal]] at Shobak in 1115 to control the land beyond the [[s:hashemite-kingdom-of-jordan|Jordan]], and the region was organised as a lordship from around 1118. [[e:payen-the-butler|Payen the Butler]] built the great castle of [[e:al-karak|Kerak]] in 1142, which became its centre.
lordship-of-oultrejordain.r: The lordship taxed the caravans and pilgrims moving between [[e:damascus|Damascus]], [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and the [[e:hejaz|Hijaz]], and the [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] of the region. It passed to [[e:philip-of-milly|Philip of Milly]] and then, through the heiress [[e:stephanie-of-milly|Stephanie of Milly]], to [[e:raynald-of-chatillon|Raynald of Chatillon]] in 1176. Raynald raided the [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] coast in 1182-1183, threatening [[e:mecca|Mecca]] and [[e:medina|Medina]], and attacked a caravan in breach of a truce, provoking [[e:saladin|Saladin]].
lordship-of-oultrejordain.e: [[e:raynald-of-chatillon|Raynald]] was executed by [[e:saladin|Saladin]] after the battle of [[e:battle-of-hattin|Hattin]] in 1187. [[e:al-karak|Kerak]] surrendered after a long siege in 1188 and [[e:shobak-castle|Montreal]] in 1189; the castles became Ayyubid strongholds.

lebedos.t: Small Ionian city between Teos and Colophon, one of the twelve of the Ionian League, later home of the travelling Dionysiac actors.
lebedos.o: Lebedos was settled by [[e:ionia|Ionian Greeks]], traditionally under Andraemon, son of [[e:codrus|Codrus]], on the coast between [[s:teos|Teos]] and [[s:colophon|Colophon]] c. 1000 BCE. Though small, it was one of the twelve members of the [[s:ionian-league|Ionian League]].
lebedos.r: Little is known of its government. It lived from farming and fishing and had hot springs nearby. Lebedos fell to [[s:kingdom-of-lydia|Lydia]] and then to the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]], and paid tribute to [[s:athens|Athens]] as a member of the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]]. It revolted from [[e:athens|Athens]] in 412 BCE.
lebedos.e: [[e:lysimachus|Lysimachus]] moved many of its inhabitants to [[s:ephesus|Ephesus]] c. 290 BCE. The [[e:ptolemaic-kingdom|Ptolemies]] refounded it as [[s:barca|Ptolemais]], and the [[e:guild|guild]] of Dionysiac artists later settled there. Lebedos passed into Roman Asia after 133 BCE; [[e:horace|Horace]] described it as nearly deserted.

lordships-of-schonburg.t: Cluster of lordships in western Saxony held by the Schönburg family for six centuries, balanced uneasily between imperial immediacy and Saxon control.
lordships-of-schonburg.o: The [[e:house-of-schonburg|Schönburgs]] were imperial ministerials from the [[e:saale|Saale]] region near [[e:naumburg|Naumburg]]. From about 1170 they were granted lands in the [[e:pleissenland|Pleissenland]], the imperial territory around [[e:altenburg|Altenburg]], and built up lordships along the [[e:zwickauer-mulde|Zwickauer Mulde]] centred on [[e:glauchau|Glauchau]], later adding [[e:waldenburg-saxony|Waldenburg]], [[e:lichtenstein-saxony|Lichtenstein]] and [[e:hartenstein-saxony|Hartenstein]]. These were held directly from the Empire, which gave the family the standing of minor imperial lords.
lordships-of-schonburg.r: The lordships were ruled by several branches of the family from castles in [[e:glauchau|Glauchau]] and [[e:waldenburg-saxony|Waldenburg]], with small towns, farmland and later textile crafts in the valley. The family adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in the 16th century. Their position was squeezed by the neighbouring [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettin]] rulers of [[e:saxony|Saxony]], who held some Schönburg lands as fiefs and steadily claimed [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] over the rest.
lordships-of-schonburg.e: By the recesses agreed with the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]], culminating in 1740, the [[e:house-of-schonburg|Schönburgs]] accepted [[e:saxons|Saxon]] [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] while keeping special rights of administration and justice. These lingered into the 19th century, and the family remained major landowners in [[e:saxony|Saxony]] until 1945.

lordship-of-werle.t: Mecklenburg lordship of the Niklotid princes centred on Güstrow, who styled themselves princes of the Wends until the line died out in 1436.
lordship-of-werle.o: In the division of [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] among the sons of [[e:henry-borwin-ii-lord-of-mecklenburg|Henry Borwin II]] in 1229, Nicholas I received the eastern lands around [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]] and the castle of Werle. His line ruled as lords of Werle, alongside their cousins in Mecklenburg, [[s:lordship-of-rostock|Rostock]] and Parchim-Richenberg, all descended from the Obotrite prince [[e:niklot|Niklot]].
lordship-of-werle.r: The lords ruled a land of lakes, farmland and small towns such as [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]], [[e:waren-muritz|Waren]] and [[e:malchow|Malchow]], which grew with German settlement. They repeatedly split the territory among branches such as Werle-Güstrow and Werle-Goldberg. From the 15th century they used the title Prince of the [[e:wends|Wends]], recalling their Slavic ancestry, while their power slowly waned beside the [[s:lordship-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg]] dukes.
lordship-of-werle.e: The last lord, [[e:william-of-werle|William of Werle]], died in 1436 without a son, and his lands passed to the [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg|Duchy of Mecklenburg]]. The dukes adopted the title Prince of the [[e:wends|Wends]], and [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]] later became a ducal residence.

lugi.t: People of eastern Sutherland recorded by Ptolemy, whose name may honour the Celtic god Lugus.
lugi.o: The Lugi are known only from [[e:geography-ptolemy|Ptolemy's Geography]] of about 150, which places them in the far north of [[e:scotland|Scotland]], usually located on the east coast of [[e:sutherland|Sutherland]] around the [[e:dornoch-firth|Dornoch Firth]] and the [[e:brora|Brora]] area, between the [[s:decantae|Decantae]] and the [[s:cornavii-caithness|Cornavii (Caithness)]]. Their name may derive from the god [[e:lugus|Lugus]] or from a word for raven.
lugi.r: Nothing is recorded of their rulers or customs. Eastern [[e:sutherland|Sutherland]] has many brochs along its river valleys and coast, such as those of Strath [[e:brora|Brora]], suggesting communities led by local families who controlled grazing and farmland.
lugi.e: The Lugi vanish from the record after Ptolemy. Their territory later formed part of the lands of the northern [[e:picts|Picts]] and then of the Norse earldom of [[e:orkney|Orkney]] before being drawn into the Scottish kingdom.

later-liang-386-403.t: The Hexi kingdom of Lü Guang, the general who brought Kumarajiva back from Kucha and kept him at Guzang for seventeen years.
later-liang-386-403.o: [[e:lu-guang|Lü Guang]], a Di general of [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]], conquered [[s:kingdom-of-kucha|Kucha]] and the [[e:tarim-basin|Tarim]] kingdoms in 384. Returning east with the monk [[e:kumarajiva|Kumarajiva]] and the spoils, he learned of the [[e:battle-of-fei-river|Fei River]] defeat, seized [[e:wuwei|Guzang]] (Wuwei) in 386 and made himself ruler of the [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]], later taking the title Heavenly King of [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]].
later-liang-386-403.r: [[e:lu-guang|Lü Guang]] ruled harshly and was distrusted by his subjects. His state soon fragmented: [[s:southern-liang|Southern Liang]] and [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]] broke away from it, and [[s:western-liang|Western Liang]] later split from Northern [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]]. [[e:kumarajiva|Kumarajiva]] remained at [[e:wuwei|Guzang]], learning Chinese, which later made his translations possible.
later-liang-386-403.e: After [[e:lu-guang|Lü Guang's]] death in 399, his sons fought over the throne. Besieged by [[s:southern-liang|Southern Liang]] and [[s:northern-liang|Northern Liang]], [[e:lu-long|Lü Long]] surrendered to [[s:later-qin|Later Qin]] in 403, and [[e:kumarajiva|Kumarajiva]] had already gone to [[e:changan|Chang'an]].

latvian-soviet-socialist-republic.t: Soviet Latvia, annexed in 1940 and restored to independence in 1990-1991 after the mass movements of the Baltic Way era.
latvian-soviet-socialist-republic.o: After a Soviet ultimatum in June 1940, the [[e:red-army|Red Army]] occupied the [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]]. A rigged election produced a parliament that requested admission to the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], and Latvia was annexed in August 1940. German occupation followed in 1941-1944, before Soviet rule returned.
latvian-soviet-socialist-republic.r: Soviet power brought nationalisation, collectivisation and [[e:deportation|mass deportations]] in June 1941 and March 1949. Riga became a major industrial centre, producing radios, railway carriages and the RAF minibuses, which drew large numbers of Russian-speaking workers, so that [[e:latvians|Latvians]] fell to barely half the population. Communist leaders included [[e:arvids-pelse|Arvīds Pelše]] and [[e:augusts-voss|Augusts Voss]], and a 1959 purge removed national communists.
latvian-soviet-socialist-republic.e: The [[e:popular-front-of-latvia|Popular Front of Latvia]] mobilised mass support, including the [[e:baltic-way|Baltic Way]] human chain of 1989. On 4 May 1990 the [[e:supreme-council-of-the-republic-of-latvia|Supreme Council]] under [[e:anatolijs-gorbunovs|Anatolijs Gorbunovs]] declared the restoration of independence, completed on 21 August 1991, restoring the [[s:republic-of-latvia|Republic of Latvia]].

lachish.t: Lachish, a major Canaanite city of the Shephelah lowlands and Egyptian vassal in the Amarna age, later the second city of Judah.
lachish.o: Lachish, at Tel Lachish west of [[e:hebron|Hebron]], became a large fortified city in the [[e:middle-bronze-age|Middle Bronze Age]], protected by a steep glacis. It controlled the fertile [[e:shephelah|Shephelah]] between the coastal plain and the Judaean hills and the roads leading to [[e:egypt|Egypt]].
lachish.r: In the [[e:late-bronze-age|Late Bronze Age]] its kings, including Zimreddi and Shipti-Ba'lu, were [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]] and wrote to the [[e:pharaoh|pharaoh]] in the [[e:amarna-letters|Amarna letters]]. Excavations revealed a temple in the old moat, the Fosse Temple, and inscriptions in early alphabetic script.
lachish.e: The Canaanite city was destroyed and abandoned in the 12th century BCE, probably during the collapse of Egyptian rule. Rebuilt in the [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], it became a fortress of the [[s:kingdom-of-judah|Kingdom of Judah]], famously besieged by [[e:sennacherib|Sennacherib]] of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] in 701 BCE.

ladwa-state.t: A Sikh chiefship near Kurukshetra whose ruler sided with the Lahore army in the First Anglo-Sikh War and lost his state.
ladwa-state.o: [[e:gurdit-singh-of-ladwa|Gurdit Singh]], a [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] sardar, seized Ladwa and nearby territory around 1763 when the [[e:sikhs|Sikhs]] overran the Mughal province of [[e:sirhind|Sirhind]].
ladwa-state.r: Ladwa joined the [[e:cis-sutlej-states|Cis-Sutlej states]] under British protection in 1809. Its Raja [[e:ajit-singh-of-ladwa|Ajit Singh]] was among the more substantial of the smaller chiefs, but kept close ties with the [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] kingdom of [[e:lahore|Lahore]].
ladwa-state.e: In the [[e:first-anglo-sikh-war|First Anglo-Sikh War]] of 1845–46 [[e:ajit-singh-of-ladwa|Ajit Singh]] joined the [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] army and took part in the campaign around [[e:battle-of-baddowal|Buddowal]] and [[e:battle-of-aliwal|Aliwal]]. The British confiscated Ladwa in 1846, and its lands became part of a British district, now in [[e:kurukshetra|Kurukshetra]] district of [[e:haryana|Haryana]].

cr.a: Cartographers and surveyors of the British East India Company

lamuri.t: A port kingdom at the northern tip of Sumatra, the first landfall for ships from India and a forerunner of the Aceh Sultanate.
lamuri.o: Lamuri is first named as Ilamuridesam in [[e:rajendra-chola-i|Rajendra Chola]]'s inscription of 1030 among places attacked by his fleet, and Arab geographers knew it as Lamri. It lay near modern [[e:banda-aceh|Banda Aceh]], and the archaeological site of Lamreh on the coast has revealed a fortified settlement and early Muslim tombstones.
lamuri.r: As the first harbour reached after crossing the [[e:bay-of-bengal|Bay of Bengal]], Lamuri traded in [[e:camphor|camphor]], sappanwood and [[e:pepper|pepper]]. [[e:marco-polo|Marco Polo]] mentions Lambri in 1292, and Ming records show its envoys visiting [[e:china|China]] and [[e:zheng-he|Zheng He's]] fleets calling there in the early 15th century. Its rulers adopted [[e:islam|Islam]] during the 13th or 14th century.
lamuri.e: In the early 16th century Lamuri was absorbed by the rising [[s:aceh-sultanate|Aceh Sultanate]], which grew from the nearby port of [[e:aceh|Aceh]] and took over its role at the entrance to the [[e:strait-of-malacca|Strait of Malacca]].
lamuri.re: Hinduism and Buddhism, later Sunni Islam

lycian-dynasts.t: The Lycian dynasts, local rulers of Xanthos and other cities who governed Lycia under Persian overlordship and built striking tombs.
lycian-dynasts.o: In c. 540 BCE the Persian general [[e:harpagus|Harpagus]] conquered Lycia; [[e:herodotus|Herodotus]] tells that the men of [[e:xanthos|Xanthos]] killed their families and died fighting. Afterwards a dynasty at Xanthos, perhaps descended from Harpagus, and rival dynasts in other cities ruled Lycia as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]].
lycian-dynasts.r: The dynasts minted [[e:silver|silver]] coins with Lycian legends and raised pillar tombs and temple-tombs, such as the [[e:nereid-monument|Nereid Monument]] of Erbbina, now in the [[e:british-museum|British Museum]]. The Inscribed Pillar at [[e:xanthos|Xanthos]] carries the longest known Lycian text. Lycian culture blended Anatolian traditions with Greek art.
lycian-dynasts.e: In the 4th century BCE [[e:pericles|Pericles]] of [[e:limyra|Limyra]] briefly united Lycia and joined the revolt against [[e:persia|Persia]], but [[e:mausolus|Mausolus of Hecatomnid Caria]] took control c. 360 BCE. The dynasts disappeared, and Lycia later reorganised as the [[s:lycian-league|Lycian League]].

limmu-ennarea.t: An Oromo kingdom of the Gibe region, built on the lands of old Ennarea, which flourished under King Abba Bagibo as a hub of the gold and ivory trade.
limmu-ennarea.o: In the 18th century [[e:oromo|Oromo]] groups settled the former territory of the [[s:kingdom-of-ennarea|Kingdom of Ennarea]]. Around 1800 a monarchy arose there under Bofo, and his son [[e:abba-bagibo|Abba Bagibo]] (r. c. 1825 to 1861) turned [[e:limmu|Limmu]]-Ennarea into the most powerful of the [[e:gibe-river|Gibe]] kingdoms, with its capital at Saqqa.
limmu-ennarea.r: The king ruled through appointed officials and controlled the great market at Saqqa, where traders from the north exchanged cloth, salt and metal goods for gold, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], civet, [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]] and slaves. The dynasty adopted [[e:islam|Islam]], and [[e:abba-bagibo|Abba Bagibo]] married into the royal families of neighbouring states. Muslim merchants, the jabarti, played a large role in its economy.
limmu-ennarea.e: After [[e:abba-bagibo|Abba Bagibo's]] death the kingdom declined in wars with the [[s:kingdom-of-jimma|Kingdom of Jimma]] and others. It was conquered by the [[s:ethiopian-empire|Ethiopian Empire]] under [[e:menelik-ii|Menelik II]] in 1891.

lordship-of-arsuf.t: A coastal lordship of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, near which Richard the Lionheart defeated Saladin in 1191.
lordship-of-arsuf.o: [[e:arsuf|Arsuf]], the ancient Apollonia, surrendered to Baldwin I in 1101 with the help of a Genoese fleet. It became a lordship within the royal domain and was later granted to [[e:vassal|vassal]] families.
lordship-of-arsuf.r: The lordship was small, based on a fortified town and harbour on the cliffs north of [[e:jaffa|Jaffa]]. On 7 September 1191 [[e:richard-i-of-england|Richard I]] won the battle of [[e:arsuf|Arsuf]] nearby, securing the coast for the [[e:third-crusade|Third Crusade]]. In the 13th century it was held by a branch of the [[e:house-of-ibelin|Ibelin family]], including [[e:john-of-ibelin-lord-of-arsuf|John of Ibelin]], lord of Arsuf and regent of the kingdom. Debts led [[e:balian-of-arsuf|Balian of Arsuf]] to lease it to the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Hospitallers]] in 1261.
lordship-of-arsuf.e: [[e:baybars|Baybars]] besieged [[e:arsuf|Arsuf]] in 1265; after forty days the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Hospitaller]] garrison surrendered and the town was destroyed. Its ruins and castle remain at Apollonia National Park.
ru: John of Ibelin, Lord of Arsuf

lordship-of-phocaea.t: A Genoese lordship on the Aegean coast of Anatolia built on the alum mines that supplied Europe's textile industry.
lordship-of-phocaea.o: In 1275 the Byzantine emperor [[e:michael-viii-palaiologos|Michael VIII]] granted [[s:phocaea|Phocaea]] and its alum mines to the Genoese brothers Manuel and [[e:benedetto-zaccaria|Benedetto Zaccaria]]. Alum, essential for fixing dyes in cloth, made the grant extremely valuable.
lordship-of-phocaea.r: The [[e:zaccaria|Zaccaria]] built [[e:new-phocaea|New Phocaea]] to protect the mines and dominated the European alum trade, shipping it to [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]] and [[e:italy|Italy]]; [[e:benedetto-zaccaria|Benedetto]] also took [[s:chios|Chios]] in 1304. The colony employed local Greek labour and paid tribute to Turkish neighbours. The [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] retook [[s:phocaea|Phocaea]] in 1340, but Genoese families, from the 1350s within the circle of the [[s:maona-of-chios|Maona of Chios]] and the [[e:gattilusio|Gattilusio]], regained control and held it as Byzantine [[e:vassal|vassals]].
lordship-of-phocaea.e: After the Ottoman [[e:fall-of-constantinople|conquest of Constantinople]], [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] took Old and [[e:new-phocaea|New Phocaea]] in 1455, ending Genoese control of the alum trade until new mines were found at [[e:tolfa|Tolfa]] in [[e:italy|Italy]].

lan-na.t: The northern Thai kingdom of Chiang Mai, founded by Mangrai in 1292, a centre of Buddhist learning with its own Tai Tham script and culture.
lan-na.o: [[e:mangrai|Mangrai]], ruler of [[s:ngoenyang|Ngoenyang]], expanded south from [[e:chiang-rai|Chiang Rai]] and captured [[s:hariphunchai|Hariphunchai]] in 1292. In 1296 he founded [[s:kingdom-of-chiang-mai|Chiang Mai]], 'new city', with the help of his allies [[e:ngam-mueang|Ngam Mueang]] of [[e:phayao|Phayao]] and [[e:ram-khamhaeng|Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai]], and made it the capital of a kingdom called Lan Na, 'a million [[e:rice|rice]] fields'.
lan-na.r: Lan Na reached its height under [[e:tilokarat|Tilokarat]] in the 15th century, who fought [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] and hosted the Eighth Buddhist Council at [[e:wat-chet-yot|Wat Chet Yot]] in 1477. [[s:kingdom-of-chiang-mai|Chiang Mai]] monks wrote Pali chronicles and scholarly works, and the [[e:mangrai|Mangrai]] code governed society. The [[e:tai-tham-script|Tai Tham script]], [[e:rice|rice]] irrigation through muang fai weir systems and a distinct temple architecture marked Lan Na culture.
lan-na.e: [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]] of the [[s:first-toungoo-empire|First Toungoo Empire]] took [[s:kingdom-of-chiang-mai|Chiang Mai]] in 1558, and Lan Na remained mostly under Burmese rule for two centuries. In 1775 [[e:kawila|Kawila]] and [[e:rama-i|Chao Phraya Chakri]] expelled the Burmese with [[s:thonburi-kingdom|Thonburi]] support, and Lan Na's principalities passed under Siam, later forming the Kingdom of Chiang Mai.

lebou-republic.t: A self-governing state of the Lebou fishing people on the Cap-Vert peninsula, ruled by councils and elders, whose capital grew into the city of Dakar.
lebou-republic.o: The [[e:lebou-people|Lebou]], fishermen and farmers of the [[e:cap-vert|Cap-Vert]] peninsula, were long subject to the [[e:wolof|Wolof]] kingdom of [[s:cayor|Cayor]]. In the 1790s they rebelled under the Muslim leader [[e:dial-diop|Dial Diop]] and, after fighting off [[e:cayor|Cayor's]] forces, established their independence around 1795, with villages such as [[e:dakar-senegal|Ndakaaru]], Yoff and Ngor forming a single polity.
lebou-republic.r: The [[e:lebou-people|Lebou]] state had no king. Authority lay with an elected head, the Serigne [[e:dakar-senegal|Ndakaaru]], together with a council of notables and assemblies of lineage elders, an arrangement Europeans compared to a republic. [[e:islam|Islam]], spread by marabouts, gave the community cohesion, and the economy rested on fishing, farming and trade with the French post at [[s:goree|Goree]] across the bay.
lebou-republic.e: In 1857 [[e:france|France]] occupied the peninsula and founded the town of [[e:dakar-senegal|Dakar]] on [[e:lebou-people|Lebou]] land, and the Lebou were absorbed into [[s:french-senegal|French Senegal]]. They remain a recognised community in Dakar with their own traditional leadership.

lordship-of-valencia.t: The Valencian principality of Rodrigo Díaz, El Cid, who conquered the city in 1094 and held it against the Almoravids until his death.
lordship-of-valencia.o: [[e:el-cid|Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar]], a Castilian noble exiled by [[e:alfonso-vi-of-castile|Alfonso VI]], had built a [[e:mercenary|mercenary]] career serving the [[s:taifa-of-zaragoza|Taifa of Zaragoza]] and collecting tribute in the east. When the qadi [[e:ibn-jahhaf|Ibn Jahhaf]] killed [[e:yahya-al-qadir|al-Qadir]] in 1092, Rodrigo besieged [[e:valencia|Valencia]], which surrendered in June 1094.
lordship-of-valencia.r: [[e:el-cid|El Cid]] ruled as an independent lord, nominally loyal to [[e:alfonso-vi-of-castile|Alfonso VI]]. He defeated Almoravid relief armies at [[e:battle-of-cuarte|Cuarte]] in 1094 and [[e:battle-of-bairen|Bairén]] in 1097, burnt [[e:ibn-jahhaf|Ibn Jahhaf]] alive and turned the great mosque into a cathedral under [[e:bishop|Bishop]] [[e:jerome|Jerome]] of [[s:county-of-perigord|Périgord]]. Most of the Muslim population remained, paying taxes to his garrison.
lordship-of-valencia.e: [[e:el-cid|El Cid]] died in 1099. His widow [[e:jimena-diaz|Jimena]] held [[e:valencia|Valencia]] until 1102, when [[e:alfonso-vi-of-castile|Alfonso VI]] judged it indefensible, evacuated the Christians and burnt the city. The [[e:almoravid-empire|Almoravids]] entered in May 1102. The story inspired the epic [[e:cantar-de-mio-cid|Cantar de mio Cid]].

lordship-of-nikola-altomanovic.t: Short-lived lordship of the Serbian magnate Nikola Altomanović, the largest in western Serbia after the collapse of Dušan's empire.
lordship-of-nikola-altomanovic.o: [[e:nikola-altomanovic|Nikola Altomanović]], son of a nobleman in [[e:stefan-dusan|Stefan Dušan's]] service, built up lands in the 1360s as [[e:stefan-uros-v|Uroš V]]'s authority faded. By about 1371 he held a broad territory from [[e:rudnik|Rudnik]] and [[e:uzice|Užice]] to the borders of [[s:republic-of-ragusa|Ragusa]] and Hum.
lordship-of-nikola-altomanovic.r: Nikola ruled from [[e:uzice|Užice]] as an independent lord, taxing the [[e:silver|silver]] mines of [[e:rudnik|Rudnik]] and quarrelling with [[s:republic-of-ragusa|Ragusa]] over trade dues. He was aggressive towards his neighbours, plotting against [[e:lazar-of-serbia|Prince Lazar]] and [[e:tvrtko-i-of-bosnia|Tvrtko]] I of the [[s:banate-of-bosnia|Banate of Bosnia]].
lordship-of-nikola-altomanovic.e: In 1373 [[e:lazar-of-serbia|Lazar]] and [[e:tvrtko-i-of-bosnia|Tvrtko]], backed by [[e:louis-i-of-hungary|Louis I of Hungary]], defeated him; he was captured at [[e:uzice|Užice]] and blinded. His lands were divided between Lazar's [[s:moravian-serbia|Moravian Serbia]], [[e:bosnia|Bosnia]] and [[e:durad-i-balsic|Đurađ I Balšić]] of [[e:zeta-region|Zeta]].

lesser-armenia.t: Lesser Armenia, a highland kingdom on the upper Euphrates that passed between Pontus, Galatian chiefs and Roman client kings.
lesser-armenia.o: After Alexander's conquest, the mountainous land west of the upper [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] was ruled by local Armenian dynasts, separate from the [[s:kingdom-of-armenia-orontid|Kingdom of Armenia (Orontid)]]. In the late 2nd century BCE its ruler [[e:antipater|Antipater]] ceded it to [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates VI]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-pontus|Kingdom of Pontus]], who built many fortresses to store his treasures.
lesser-armenia.r: Lesser [[s:armenia|Armenia]] was a land of pastures and fortified hilltops. After [[e:pompey|Pompey]] defeated [[e:mithridates-vi-of-pontus|Mithridates]] in 66 BCE, he founded [[e:nicopolis-lesser-armenia|Nicopolis]] on the battlefield and gave the region to the Galatian king [[e:deiotarus|Deiotarus]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] later used it as a reward for loyal client kings.
lesser-armenia.e: Its last king, [[e:aristobulus-of-chalcis|Aristobulus]], a great-grandson of Herod, ruled until c. 71 CE. Vespasian annexed Lesser [[s:armenia|Armenia]] to the Roman province of [[s:kingdom-of-cappadocia|Cappadocia]] in 72 CE.

lordship-of-rimini.t: The Malatesta lordship of Rimini, home of Sigismondo Malatesta's Tempio Malatestiano and of the tragedy of Paolo and Francesca.
lordship-of-rimini.o: [[e:malatesta-da-verucchio|Malatesta da Verucchio]], leader of the [[e:house-of-welf|Guelphs]] of Rimini, drove out the Ghibelline Parcitadi family in 1295 and made himself lord of the city. His heirs ruled Rimini as papal vicars and spread through [[e:romagna|Romagna]] and the [[e:marche|Marche]].
lordship-of-rimini.r: The [[e:malatesta-family|Malatesta]] were warlords and condottieri who governed Rimini, [[e:cesena|Cesena]], [[e:fano|Fano]] and other towns. Malatesta's son [[e:giovanni-malatesta|Gianciotto]] killed his wife [[e:francesca-da-rimini|Francesca da Polenta]] and his brother [[e:paolo-malatesta|Paolo]], a story [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante]] told in the [[e:inferno-dante|Inferno]]. [[e:sigismondo-pandolfo-malatesta|Sigismondo Pandolfo Malatesta]], a brilliant and ruthless captain, had [[e:leon-battista-alberti|Leon Battista Alberti]] remodel the church of San Francesco as the [[e:tempio-malatestiano|Tempio Malatestiano]]. [[e:pope-pius-ii|Pope Pius II]] publicly condemned Sigismondo in 1462 and took most of his lands.
lordship-of-rimini.e: In 1500 [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare Borgia]] drove out [[e:pandolfo-iv-malatesta|Pandolfo IV Malatesta]]. [[e:venice|Venice]] held Rimini from 1503 to 1509, after which it passed to direct papal rule in the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].

later-pandyan-empire.t: The revived Pandya kingdom of Madurai that became the leading power of south India in the 13th century, visited by Marco Polo.
later-pandyan-empire.o: The [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandyas]], one of the ancient Tamil dynasties, had been subordinate to the [[s:chola-empire|Chola Empire]] for much of the 11th and 12th centuries. In the late 12th century they reasserted themselves around [[e:madurai|Madurai]], and under [[e:maravarman-sundara-pandya-i|Maravarman Sundara Pandya I]] in the early 13th century they defeated the [[e:chola-empire|Cholas]] and sacked their country.
later-pandyan-empire.r: [[e:jatavarman-sundara-pandya-i|Jatavarman Sundara Pandya I]] made the [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandyas]] paramount from [[e:nellore|Nellore]] to northern [[s:sri-lanka|Sri Lanka]], subduing the [[s:hoysala-empire|Hoysalas]] and the [[s:jaffna-kingdom|Kingdom of Jaffna]]. [[e:marco-polo|Marco Polo]] and [[e:wassaf|Wassaf]] described the pearl fisheries and the horse trade with [[e:arabia|Arabia]] through ports such as [[e:kayal|Kayal]]. The kings lavishly endowed the temples of [[e:madurai|Madurai]], [[e:srirangam|Srirangam]] and [[e:chidambaram|Chidambaram]], gilding the roof at Srirangam.
later-pandyan-empire.e: A succession war between Sundara [[e:pandya-dynasty|Pandya]] and Vira Pandya invited intervention by [[e:malik-kafur|Malik Kafur]] of the [[s:delhi-sultanate|Delhi Sultanate]] in 1311. [[e:madurai|Madurai]] fell under [[e:delhi|Delhi]] and then the [[s:madurai-sultanate|Madurai Sultanate]] in 1335, while Pandya princes survived in the south and later formed the [[s:tenkasi-pandyas|Tenkasi Pandyas]].

liang-li-gui.t: A brief kingdom in the Hexi Corridor, centred on Wuwei, set up as Sui collapsed and overthrown in 619 by a Sogdian family who handed it to the Tang.
liang-li-gui.o: [[e:li-gui|Li Gui]], a wealthy and respected notable of [[e:wuwei|Wuwei]] (Liangzhou), was chosen by local leaders in 617 to resist the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] of [[e:xue-ju|Xue Ju]]. He proclaimed himself Prince of Great [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]] and in 618 took the title of emperor, controlling the [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]] oasis cities.
liang-li-gui.r: The state sat astride the [[e:silk-road|Silk Road]], and Sogdian merchant families were powerful in its capital. [[e:li-gui|Li Gui]] at first exchanged friendly letters with [[e:emperor-gaozu-of-tang|Li Yuan]], founder of the [[s:tang-dynasty|Tang Dynasty]], but refused to accept a subordinate title, insisting on equal imperial status.
liang-li-gui.e: In 619 the [[s:later-tang|Tang]] envoy An Xinggui, whose Sogdian family was influential in [[e:wuwei|Wuwei]], worked with his brother An Xiuren to raise troops against [[e:li-gui|Li Gui]]. They captured him and delivered him to [[e:changan|Chang'an]], where he was executed, and the [[e:gansu-corridor|Hexi Corridor]] passed to Tang rule.

lordship-of-ainos.t: Branch lordship of the Genoese Gattilusi family at the mouth of the Maritsa, controlling trade from Thrace until Mehmed II took it in 1456.
lordship-of-ainos.o: [[s:aenus|Ainos]] (Enez), an old Greek port at the mouth of the [[e:maritsa|Hebrus]] (Maritsa), came under the control of [[e:niccolo-i-gattilusio|Niccolo Gattilusio]], brother of [[e:francesco-i-gattilusio|Francesco I Gattilusio]] of the [[s:lordship-of-lesbos|Lordship of Lesbos]], around 1384. It became a separate branch of the family's possessions in the northern [[e:aegean|Aegean]].
lordship-of-ainos.r: The lords of [[s:aenus|Ainos]] profited from salt pans, fisheries and river trade with the Thracian interior, and their realm included [[e:samothrace|Samothrace]] and at times [[e:imbros|Imbros]]. They acted as Byzantine [[e:vassal|vassals]] and later as Ottoman tributaries. [[e:palamede-gattilusio|Palamede Gattilusio]] ruled for more than forty years (1409-1455), and the family's inscriptions and fortifications survive on Samothrace and at Enez.
lordship-of-ainos.e: After the death of [[e:palamede-gattilusio|Palamede]] in 1455 a succession dispute among his heirs gave [[e:mehmed-ii|Mehmed II]] an excuse to intervene. In 1456 the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]] took [[s:aenus|Ainos]] and the lordship ended.

later-zhou.t: The last of the Five Dynasties, whose able emperor Chai Rong began the reunification of China completed by the Song.
later-zhou.o: [[e:guo-wei|Guo Wei]], a leading general of the [[s:later-han|Later Han]], was forced into rebellion when Emperor [[e:liu-chengyou|Liu Chengyou]] plotted to kill him in 950. After the emperor's death he took the throne at [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]] in 951 as founder of the [[s:wu-zhou|Zhou dynasty]], the first non-[[e:shatuo|Shatuo]] ruler of the north for decades.
later-zhou.r: [[e:guo-wei|Guo Wei]] lightened taxes and punishments. His adopted son [[e:chai-rong|Chai Rong (Emperor Shizong)]], who succeeded in 954, defeated the [[s:northern-han|Northern Han]] and Khitan at [[e:battle-of-gaoping|Gaoping]], reorganised the palace army, closed thousands of Buddhist monasteries and melted bronze images for coin. He took the lands between the Huai and [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]] from [[s:southern-tang|Southern Tang]] in 958 and recovered two of the [[e:sixteen-prefectures|Sixteen Prefectures]] from the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] in 959.
later-zhou.e: [[e:chai-rong|Chai Rong]] died in 959, leaving a child emperor. In 960 the palace army commander [[e:emperor-taizu-of-song|Zhao Kuangyin]] was proclaimed emperor by his troops at [[e:chenqiao-mutiny|Chenqiao]] and founded the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]], which built on Later Zhou's army and policies.

lusitania.t: The Roman province of western Iberia, roughly modern Portugal and Extremadura, governed from the splendid veteran colony of Emerita Augusta.
lusitania.o: Lusitania was carved out of [[s:hispania-ulterior|Hispania Ulterior]] by Augustus after the [[e:cantabrian-wars|Cantabrian Wars]], with the division under way from 27 BCE. Its capital, [[e:emerita-augusta|Emerita Augusta]] ([[e:merida-spain|Mérida]]), was founded in 25 BCE for veterans of those wars. It covered the lands of the [[s:lusitanians|Lusitanians]], [[s:vettones|Vettones]] and [[s:celtici|Celtici]] between the [[e:douro|Douro]] and the [[e:guadiana|Guadiana]].
lusitania.r: An imperial legate governed the province, among them the future emperor [[e:otho|Otho]] from 58 to 68 CE. [[e:emerita-augusta|Emerita]] grew into one of the great cities of the West, with its [[e:theatre|theatre]], amphitheatre and long bridge over the [[e:guadiana|Guadiana]]. [[e:lisbon|Olisipo]] (Lisbon) and [[e:pax-julia|Pax Iulia]] (Beja) were other centres, and the economy rested on farming, mining and fish sauce. [[e:christianity|Christianity]] spread early; [[e:eulalia-of-merida|Eulalia of Mérida]] was martyred in 304.
lusitania.e: In 409 [[e:vandals|Vandals]], [[s:alans|Alans]] and [[s:suebi|Suebi]] crossed into [[e:hispania|Hispania]], and the Alans settled in Lusitania. In 439 the Suebic king [[e:rechila|Rechila]] took [[e:emerita-augusta|Emerita]], ending effective Roman rule. The province's name later became a poetic name for Portugal.

leptis-magna.t: A Phoenician trading port on the Libyan coast that grew rich under Carthage and later became one of Rome's great African cities.
leptis-magna.o: Leptis (Lpqy in Punic) was founded by Phoenician settlers at the mouth of the Wadi Lebda, east of modern [[s:county-of-tripoli|Tripoli]], probably in the 7th century BCE. With [[e:tripoli|Oea]] and [[e:sabratha|Sabratha]] it formed the three Emporia that later gave [[s:tripolitania|Tripolitania]] its name, linking [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]] shipping with [[e:caravan-trade|caravan routes]] across the [[e:sahara|Sahara]].
leptis-magna.r: The city was governed by Punic magistrates ([[e:suffete|suffetes]]) and a council, and Carthaginian Punic remained its official language long into Roman times. As part of the [[s:punic-empire|Punic Empire]] it was so wealthy that [[e:livy|Livy]] says it paid [[e:carthage|Carthage]] a talent a day in tribute. Its farmland produced [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] and grain, and its merchants handled gold, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and slaves from the desert trade.
leptis-magna.e: [[e:masinissa|Masinissa]] of [[s:numidia|Numidia]] seized the Emporia in the 160s BCE, and Leptis later allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] against [[e:jugurtha|Jugurtha]]. Having backed [[e:juba-i|Juba I]] in [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]]'s civil war, it was fined three million pounds of [[e:olive-oil|olive oil]] a year in 46 BCE and absorbed into [[s:africa-proconsularis|Roman Africa]]. It later flourished as the birthplace of [[e:septimius-severus|Septimius Severus]].

lacetani.t: An Iberian people of inland Catalonia who resisted Rome during the Second Punic War and Cato's campaign of 195 BCE.
lacetani.o: The Lacetani lived in the interior of [[s:principality-of-catalonia|Catalonia]], roughly in the modern comarques of [[e:bages|Bages]], [[e:anoia|Anoia]] and [[e:solsones|Solsonès]], from about the 5th century BCE. They were part of the Iberian culture of the north-east and neighbours of the [[s:ilergetes|Ilergetes]] and [[s:ausetani|Ausetani]].
lacetani.r: Their society of fortified hilltop villages lived from farming and herding. Ancient writers, mainly [[e:livy|Livy]], record them only in wartime, and their name is easily confused with the coastal [[s:laietani|Laietani]], so many details are uncertain.
lacetani.e: They fought the [[e:roman-empire|Romans]] under [[e:gnaeus-cornelius-scipio-calvus|Gnaeus Scipio]] in 218 BCE and again in the north-eastern revolt of 197 to 195 BCE, when [[e:cato-the-elder|Cato]] stormed their chief town. Afterwards they were absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]] and their name faded.

lordship-of-brecknock.t: A marcher lordship in the Usk valley created by Bernard de Neufmarche's conquest of the Welsh kingdom of Brycheiniog.
lordship-of-brecknock.o: [[e:bernard-de-neufmarche|Bernard de Neufmarche]] invaded the kingdom of [[s:kingdom-of-brycheiniog|Brycheiniog]] in the late 11th century and killed [[e:rhys-ap-tewdwr|Rhys ap Tewdwr]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-deheubarth|Kingdom of Deheubarth]] near Brecon in 1093. He built [[e:brecon-castle|Brecon Castle]] and founded [[e:brecon-cathedral|Brecon Priory]], granting lands to his followers.
lordship-of-brecknock.r: [[s:kingdom-of-brycheiniog|Brecknock]] was governed as a marcher lordship with its own courts and military obligations, a Norman lowland lordship over a largely Welsh upland population. It passed by marriage to the [[e:braose-family|de Braose family]] and then to the de [[e:bohun-family|Bohuns]], earls of [[e:hereford|Hereford]], and later to the [[e:stafford|Staffords]], dukes of Buckingham.
lordship-of-brecknock.e: [[e:edward-stafford-3rd-duke-of-buckingham|Edward Stafford]], Duke of Buckingham, was executed in 1521 and the lordship came to the crown. The [[e:laws-in-wales-acts-1535-and-1542|Laws in Wales Act]] of 1536 made [[s:kingdom-of-brycheiniog|Brecknock]] a shire, which survives as part of [[s:kingdom-of-powys|Powys]].

lordship-of-mechelen.t: A small separate lordship between Brabant and Antwerp that became the judicial and court capital of the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands.
lordship-of-mechelen.o: Mechelen was long divided between the prince-[[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[s:prince-bishopric-of-liege|Liège]] and the [[e:house-of-berthout|Berthout family]], under constant pressure from [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]]. In 1333 the bishop sold his rights to [[e:louis-i-count-of-flanders|Louis of Nevers]], count of [[s:county-of-flanders|Flanders]], and after disputes with Brabant the town became a distinct lordship, one of the seventeen provinces of the [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]].
lordship-of-mechelen.r: Mechelen was a prosperous cloth town with a tall cathedral tower of [[e:st-rumbolds-cathedral|St Rumbold]]. Under the [[s:burgundian-state|Burgundian State]] it became seat of the [[e:parliament-of-mechelen|Parliament of Mechelen]] in 1473, later the Great Council, the supreme court of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]]. [[e:margaret-of-york|Margaret of York]] and then [[e:margaret-of-austria-duchess-of-savoy|Margaret of Austria]], regent for [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]], kept their courts there, making it a [[e:renaissance|Renaissance]] centre.
lordship-of-mechelen.e: In 1559 Mechelen became the seat of the new archbishop, primate of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Netherlands]]. It stayed with the [[s:spanish-netherlands|Spanish Netherlands]] and the [[s:austrian-netherlands|Austrian Netherlands]] until French annexation in 1795, and is today a city of [[s:kingdom-of-belgium|Belgium]].

later-jin-1616-1636.t: The Jurchen khanate founded by Nurhaci, who united the Jurchen tribes and challenged the Ming, the direct forerunner of the Qing Empire.
later-jin-1616-1636.o: [[e:nurhaci|Nurhaci]], a chief of the Jianzhou [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] in [[e:manchuria|Manchuria]], spent three decades uniting the Jurchen tribes and organising his followers into the [[e:eight-banners|Eight Banners]]. In 1616 he proclaimed himself khan of the [[s:later-jin-936-947|Later Jin]] (Amaga Aisin Gurun) at [[e:hetu-ala|Hetu Ala]], claiming succession from the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234).
later-jin-1616-1636.r: The [[e:eight-banners|Eight Banners]] combined military, social and administrative roles, enrolling [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]], and later Mongol and Chinese, households. [[e:nurhaci|Nurhaci]] declared war on the [[s:ming-empire|Ming Empire]] in 1618, won a great victory at [[e:battle-of-sarhu|Sarhu]] in 1619, took [[e:liaoyang|Liaoyang]] and [[e:shenyang|Shenyang]] and in 1625 made Shenyang (Mukden) his capital. A [[e:manchus|Manchu]] script based on Mongolian was created and later improved.
later-jin-1616-1636.e: [[e:nurhaci|Nurhaci]] was checked at [[e:battle-of-ningyuan|Ningyuan]] in 1626 and died that year. His son [[e:hong-taiji|Hong Taiji]] brought in Chinese officials, subdued [[e:korea|Korea]] and the [[e:chahar-mongols|Chahar Mongols]], renamed his people [[e:manchus|Manchu]] in 1635 and in 1636 proclaimed the [[s:qing-empire|Qing Empire]], which conquered [[e:china|China]] from 1644.

lusatian-league.t: An alliance of six Upper Lusatian towns, formed in 1346, that dominated the politics and trade of their province for centuries.
lusatian-league.o: In 1346 [[e:bautzen|Bautzen]], [[e:gorlitz|Görlitz]], [[e:zittau|Zittau]], [[e:kamenz|Kamenz]], [[e:lobau|Löbau]] and Lauban, towns of the [[s:margraviate-of-upper-lusatia|Margraviate of Upper Lusatia]], then a land of the [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Kingdom of Bohemia]], formed a league to suppress robber knights and protect their trade. [[e:charles-iv-duke-of-anjou|Charles IV]], as king of [[e:bohemia|Bohemia]], approved the alliance, which became a permanent political force.
lusatian-league.r: The six towns met in regular diets, kept a common treasury and troops, and formed a separate estate in the Upper Lusatian diet alongside the nobility. Their wealth came from cloth and linen weaving and from the [[e:via-regia|Via Regia]] trade road through [[e:gorlitz|Görlitz]]. They fought the [[e:hussites|Hussites]] in the 15th century and mostly turned Lutheran in the 16th.
lusatian-league.e: In 1547 Ferdinand I punished the towns for refusing aid in the [[e:schmalkaldic-war|Schmalkaldic War]], confiscating lands and privileges. [[e:upper-lusatia|Upper Lusatia]] passed to the [[s:electorate-of-saxony|Electorate of Saxony]] in 1635, and the league lingered until 1815, when [[e:gorlitz|Görlitz]] and Lauban went to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]].

lordship-of-gower.t: A marcher lordship on the Gower peninsula and around Swansea, created by Henry de Beaumont, Earl of Warwick, in the early 12th century.
lordship-of-gower.o: [[e:henry-de-beaumont-1st-earl-of-warwick|Henry de Beaumont]], Earl of Warwick, took Gower from its Welsh rulers around 1106 and built a castle at [[e:swansea|Swansea]]. English and Flemish settlers occupied the southern part of the peninsula, which developed a lasting English-speaking character.
lordship-of-gower.r: Gower was divided between an Anglicised lowland '[[e:englishry|Englishry]]' and a Welsh upland '[[e:welshry|Welshry]]'. The lords held their own courts and granted [[e:swansea|Swansea]] its first charter. The lordship passed to the [[e:braose-family|de Braose family]] and later to the Mowbrays and the Herberts, and was repeatedly fought over by the lords of [[s:lordship-of-glamorgan|Glamorgan]] and Welsh princes.
lordship-of-gower.e: The [[e:laws-in-wales-acts-1535-and-1542|Laws in Wales Act]] of 1536 attached Gower to the new county of [[s:lordship-of-glamorgan|Glamorgan]]. Its distinct dialect and Anglo-Norman churches remain, and in 1956 it became [[e:britain|Britain's]] first [[e:area-of-outstanding-natural-beauty|Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty]].

lordship-of-ravenstein.t: A small lordship on the Maas that stayed outside the Dutch Republic and became a refuge for Catholics in a Protestant land.
lordship-of-ravenstein.o: Ravenstein grew around a castle on the [[e:meuse|Maas]] in north-eastern [[s:duchy-of-brabant|Brabant]]. In the 14th century it passed to the house of [[e:kleve|Cleves]], and from 1360 it was held as a separate lordship by Cleves princes, independent of both Brabant and [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]].
lordship-of-ravenstein.r: The [[e:kleve|Cleves]] lords of Ravenstein, notably [[e:adolf-of-cleves-lord-of-ravenstein|Adolf of Cleves]] and his son Philip, were prominent at the Burgundian court. Later the lordship passed to the dukes of Jülich-Berg and the [[s:palatinate-neuburg|Palatinate-Neuburg]] family. When the surrounding lands came under the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]], Ravenstein remained a Catholic enclave, where priests and believers from the [[e:generality-lands|Generality lands]] could worship freely.
lordship-of-ravenstein.e: The lordship was absorbed into the [[s:batavian-republic|Batavian Republic]] around 1800, ending its separate status. It later became part of the province of [[e:north-brabant|North Brabant]] in the [[s:kingdom-of-the-netherlands|Kingdom of the Netherlands]].

later-tran-dynasty.t: A resistance dynasty of Tran princes who fought the Ming occupation of Vietnam from 1407 until their capture in 1414.
later-tran-dynasty.o: Soon after the Ming conquest of the [[s:ho-dynasty|Ho dynasty]] in 1407, [[e:gian-dinh-de|Tran Ngoi]], a son of the Tran emperor [[e:tran-nghe-tong|Tran Nghe Tong]], proclaimed himself emperor Gian Dinh in [[e:ninh-binh-province|Ninh Binh]] and rallied former Tran officials and generals against the occupiers.
later-tran-dynasty.r: The Later Tran had no fixed capital and operated as a mobile resistance court in the provinces of [[e:nghe-an-province|Nghe An]], [[e:thanh-hoa|Thanh Hoa]] and the south. [[e:gian-dinh-de|Gian Dinh]] won a notable victory at [[e:battle-of-bo-co|Bo Co]] in 1408 with the generals [[e:dang-tat|Dang Tat]] and [[e:nguyen-canh-chan|Nguyen Canh Chan]], but later had them killed. Their sons then backed Tran Quy Khoang, who became emperor [[e:tran-quy-khoang|Trung Quang]].
later-tran-dynasty.e: Ming forces under [[e:zhang-fu-ming-general|Zhang Fu]] gradually pushed the Later Tran south. [[e:gian-dinh-de|Gian Dinh]] was captured in 1409 and [[e:tran-quy-khoang|Trung Quang]] in 1414, ending the dynasty. Resistance revived four years later under [[e:le-loi|Le Loi]], who succeeded where they had failed.

later-le-dynasty.t: Vietnam's longest-ruling dynasty, founded by Le Loi in 1428, which conquered Champa's heartland and produced the Hong Duc legal code.
later-le-dynasty.o: [[e:le-loi|Le Loi]], a landowner from [[e:lam-son|Lam Son]] in [[e:thanh-hoa|Thanh Hoa]], led a ten-year war against [[s:jiaozhi-province-ming|Ming Jiaozhi]] Province from 1418 and proclaimed himself emperor Le Thai To at [[e:thang-long|Thang Long]] in 1428, restoring the name [[s:tran-dynasty|Dai Viet]]. Legend says he returned his magic sword to a turtle in [[e:hoan-kiem-lake|Hoan Kiem]] lake.
later-le-dynasty.r: [[e:le-thanh-tong|Le Thanh Tong]], who reigned from 1460 to 1497, built a Confucian state with examinations, provincial administration and the [[e:le-code|Hong Duc code]], notable for its protection of women's property rights. In 1471 he captured the [[e:cham|Cham]] capital [[e:vijaya-champa|Vijaya]], greatly extending [[s:tran-dynasty|Dai Viet]] south. After 1527 the Le were displaced by the [[s:mac-dynasty|Mac dynasty]], and after their restoration in 1533 real power lay with the [[s:trinh-lords|Trinh lords]] and [[s:nguyen-lords|Nguyen lords]].
later-le-dynasty.e: The Le emperors reigned as figureheads for over two centuries. When the [[e:tay-son-dynasty|Tay Son]] overthrew the Trinh in 1786, the last emperor, [[e:le-chieu-thong|Le Chieu Thong]], sought Qing help; after the Qing defeat at [[e:battle-of-ngoc-hoi-dong-da|Dong Da]] in 1789 he fled to [[e:china|China]], ending the dynasty.

lordship-of-clandeboye.t: A Gaelic lordship in Antrim and Down held by the Clann Aodha Buidhe O'Neills, who took over the lands of the collapsed Earldom of Ulster.
lordship-of-clandeboye.o: The [[e:clandeboye-oneills|Clann Aodha Buidhe]], descendants of [[e:aodh-buidhe-oneill|Aodh Buidhe O'Neill]], a 13th century king of [[e:tir-eoghain|Tir Eoghain]], moved east across the [[e:river-bann|Bann]] after the collapse of the [[s:earldom-of-ulster|Earldom of Ulster]] in 1333. By around 1350 they ruled much of south [[e:county-antrim|Antrim]] and north Down, later divided into Upper and Lower Clandeboye.
lordship-of-clandeboye.r: The lordship's seat was the castle at [[e:castlereagh|Castlereagh]] near [[e:belfast|Belfast]], and its chiefs ruled through Gaelic law, [[e:cattle|cattle]] wealth and Scottish gallowglasses. Their territory was later contested by the [[e:macdonnells-of-antrim|MacDonnells]] and by English colonisation attempts, including the [[e:walter-devereux-1st-earl-of-essex|Earl of Essex]]'s massacre of Sir [[e:brian-macphelim-oneill|Brian MacPhelim O'Neill]] and his family in 1574.
lordship-of-clandeboye.e: [[e:con-oneill-of-clandeboye|Con O'Neill]], the last lord, lost most of his lands to the Scots [[e:hugh-montgomery-1st-viscount-montgomery|Hugh Montgomery]] and [[e:james-hamilton-1st-viscount-claneboye|James Hamilton]] in 1605, opening north Down to large-scale Scottish settlement.

lordship-of-haifa.t: A small coastal lordship of the Kingdom of Jerusalem at the foot of Mount Carmel.
lordship-of-haifa.o: [[e:haifa|Haifa]] was taken in August 1100 by [[e:tancred-prince-of-galilee|Tancred]] with the help of a Venetian fleet, after a stubborn defence in which its Jewish and Muslim inhabitants fought together. It was then granted as a fief, its first known lord being [[e:geldemar-carpenel|Geldemar Carpenel]].
lordship-of-haifa.r: [[e:haifa|Haifa]] was a modest lordship with a harbour and the farmland of the [[e:mount-carmel|Carmel]] coast, and was at times attached to the [[s:principality-of-galilee|Principality of Galilee]]. It was best known for nearby Mount Carmel, where hermits gathered in the 12th century and the Carmelite order took shape in the early 13th century. Little is recorded about its administration.
lordship-of-haifa.e: [[e:saladin|Saladin]] captured [[e:haifa|Haifa]] in 1187; it was regained after the [[e:third-crusade|Third Crusade]] and refortified by [[e:louis-ix-of-france|Louis IX of France]] in 1250-1252. In 1265 the [[e:mamluk|Mamluk]] sultan [[e:baybars|Baybars]] took and destroyed it.

lordship-of-piedmont.t: The Savoy-Achaea principality in Piedmont, a cadet branch of the house of Savoy that also claimed the Frankish Principality of Achaea in Greece.
lordship-of-piedmont.o: In 1294 Count [[e:amadeus-v-count-of-savoy|Amadeus V]] of the [[s:county-of-savoy|County of Savoy]] settled his nephew Philip with the family's lands in [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]] as a dependent [[e:appanage|appanage]]. In 1301 Philip married [[e:isabella-of-villehardouin|Isabella of Villehardouin]], heiress of the [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]], and his line kept the title princes of [[e:achaea|Achaea]] even after losing [[e:greece|Greece]].
lordship-of-piedmont.r: Philip and his heirs ruled from [[e:pinerolo|Pinerolo]] over [[e:turin|Turin]] and the towns of the upper Po plain, as [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the counts of [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]]. They fought the [[s:march-of-montferrat|March of Montferrat]] and the [[s:marquisate-of-saluzzo|Marquisate of Saluzzo]] for control of [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]] and held assemblies of nobles and towns. Prince Louis founded the [[e:university-of-turin|University of Turin]] in 1404.
lordship-of-piedmont.e: Louis died without a legitimate heir in 1418, and his lands returned to his cousin [[e:amadeus-viii-duke-of-savoy|Amadeus VIII]] of the [[s:duchy-of-savoy|Duchy of Savoy]], uniting [[e:piedmont|Piedmont]] with [[s:county-of-savoy|Savoy]]. The heir to the Savoy throne was later styled Prince of Piedmont.

later-qin.t: The Qiang-ruled state of the Yao family at Chang'an, whose ruler Yao Xing brought Kumarajiva to translate the Buddhist scriptures into Chinese.
later-qin.o: [[e:yao-chang|Yao Chang]], a [[e:qiang-historical-people|Qiang]] general of [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]], rebelled after the [[e:battle-of-fei-river|Fei River]] defeat in 383, captured and killed the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] ruler [[e:fu-jian-337-385|Fu Jian]] in 385 and proclaimed himself emperor of Qin in 386, with his capital at [[e:changan|Chang'an]].
later-qin.r: [[e:yao-chang|Yao Chang's]] son [[e:yao-xing|Yao Xing]] defeated [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]] remnants and [[s:western-qin|Western Qin]], made [[s:later-liang-386-403|Later Liang]] submit and ruled much of north-western [[e:china|China]]. A devout Buddhist, he brought the Kuchean monk [[e:kumarajiva|Kumarajiva]] to [[e:changan|Chang'an]] in 401 and gave him a translation bureau with hundreds of assistants; their versions of the [[e:lotus-sutra|Lotus Sutra]] and other texts became standard in [[e:east-asia|East Asia]].
later-qin.e: Later [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] was weakened by the rise of [[s:helian-xia|Helian Xia]], a former [[e:vassal|vassal]], and by succession disputes. In 417 the [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]] general [[e:emperor-wu-of-liu-song|Liu Yu]] captured [[e:changan|Chang'an]], and the last ruler, [[e:yao-hong|Yao Hong]], was executed at [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]].

lordship-of-carpi.t: The Pio family's small Emilian lordship, whose humanist prince Alberto III Pio made Carpi a Renaissance showpiece.
lordship-of-carpi.o: In 1319 the Pio family, local nobles, took control of [[s:carpi|Carpi]], a town between [[e:modena|Modena]] and [[s:duchy-of-mantua|Mantua]], with the support of the Bonacolsi. They ruled it as imperial vicars, with the [[e:house-of-este|Este]] and [[e:house-of-gonzaga|Gonzaga]] as powerful neighbours.
lordship-of-carpi.r: The Pio governed a small farming territory and its walled town. [[e:alberto-iii-pio|Alberto III Pio]], pupil and patron of the printer [[e:aldus-manutius|Aldus Manutius]], rebuilt [[s:carpi|Carpi]] around a huge new square with the castle, a new cathedral and porticoes. A diplomat at [[e:rome|Rome]], he sided with [[e:france|France]] in the [[e:social-war-91-87-bce|Italian Wars]] and quarrelled with [[e:erasmus|Erasmus]]. The family often divided the lordship among relatives.
lordship-of-carpi.e: Alberto's support for [[e:france|France]] cost him his state: [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V's]] forces occupied [[s:carpi|Carpi]], and in 1527 the emperor gave it to Alfonso I d'[[e:house-of-este|Este]]. Carpi then became part of the Este lands of the [[s:duchy-of-modena-and-reggio|Duchy of Modena and Reggio]].

lao-peoples-democratic-republic.t: Communist Laos, a one-party state led by the Lao People's Revolutionary Party since the abolition of the monarchy in 1975.
lao-peoples-democratic-republic.o: After the [[e:pathet-lao|Pathet Lao]] gained control of the coalition government formed under the 1973 accords, [[e:savang-vatthana|King Savang Vatthana]] abdicated, and on 2 December 1975 the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed in [[s:kingdom-of-vientiane|Vientiane]], with Prince [[e:souphanouvong|Souphanouvong]] as president and [[e:kaysone-phomvihane|Kaysone Phomvihane]] as prime minister.
lao-peoples-democratic-republic.r: The [[e:lao-peoples-revolutionary-party|Lao People's Revolutionary Party]] rules as the only legal party, closely allied with [[s:socialist-republic-of-vietnam|Vietnam]]. Early policies of collectivisation, re-education camps and suppression of [[e:hmong-people|Hmong]] resistance drove many to flee. From 1986 the [[e:new-economic-mechanism|New Economic Mechanism]] opened the economy to markets and foreign investment. Unexploded ordnance from the US bombing campaign still kills and injures people.
lao-peoples-democratic-republic.e: The Lao PDR continues today, joining [[e:association-of-southeast-asian-nations|ASEAN]] in 1997. Growth from hydropower dams and mining, and the Chinese-built [[e:boten-vientiane-railway|Laos-China railway]] opened in 2021, have deepened ties with [[e:china|China]], alongside heavy public debt.

later-han.t: The shortest of the Five Dynasties, set up at Kaifeng by the Shatuo general Liu Zhiyuan after the Khitan withdrew from northern China in 947.
later-han.o: When the Khitan army of the [[s:liao-dynasty|Liao dynasty]] took [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]] and ended the [[s:later-jin-936-947|Later Jin]] (936-947) at the start of 947, [[e:liu-zhiyuan|Liu Zhiyuan]], [[e:shatuo|Shatuo]] governor of [[e:hedong-shanxi|Hedong]] at [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]], proclaimed himself emperor. As the Khitan withdrew north under popular resistance, he entered Kaifeng and took over the old court.
later-han.r: Later Han relied on the palace army and on ruthless ministers, and its tax collectors and courts were notorious for harshness. [[e:liu-zhiyuan|Liu Zhiyuan]] died in 948, leaving his young son [[e:liu-chengyou|Liu Chengyou]] under a group of senior ministers and generals.
later-han.e: In 950 [[e:liu-chengyou|Liu Chengyou]] had leading ministers killed and plotted against the general [[e:guo-wei|Guo Wei]], who marched on [[e:kaifeng|Kaifeng]]. The emperor was killed in the fighting, and early in 951 Guo Wei founded the [[s:later-zhou|Later Zhou]]. [[e:liu-zhiyuan|Liu Zhiyuan's]] brother [[e:liu-chong|Liu Chong]] held [[e:taiyuan|Taiyuan]] as the [[s:northern-han|Northern Han]].

lordship-of-pesaro.t: An Adriatic lordship held by the Malatesta and then the Sforza, before passing to the della Rovere dukes of Urbino in 1512.
lordship-of-pesaro.o: A branch of [[e:malatesta-family|the Malatesta]] of [[s:lordship-of-rimini|Rimini]] took control of Pesaro in 1285 and ruled it as lords and papal vicars. In 1445 [[e:galeazzo-malatesta|Galeazzo Malatesta]] sold Pesaro to [[e:alessandro-sforza|Alessandro Sforza]], brother of [[e:francesco-sforza|Francesco Sforza]], who had married his granddaughter [[e:costanza-da-varano|Costanza da Varano]].
lordship-of-pesaro.r: Under [[e:malatesta-family|the Malatesta]] and then the [[e:house-of-sforza|Sforza]], Pesaro was a small Adriatic court state living from farming, fishing and maiolica pottery. [[e:alessandro-sforza|Alessandro Sforza]] patronised artists, and his son [[e:costanzo-i-sforza|Costanzo]] began the [[e:rocca-costanza|Rocca Costanza]] fortress. [[e:giovanni-sforza|Giovanni Sforza]], Costanzo's son, married [[e:lucrezia-borgia|Lucrezia Borgia]], but the marriage was annulled and [[e:cesare-borgia|Cesare Borgia]] expelled him in 1500. He returned after [[e:pope-alexander-vi|Pope Alexander VI's]] death in 1503.
lordship-of-pesaro.e: After Giovanni's son died young, [[e:pope-julius-ii|Pope Julius II]] granted Pesaro in 1512 to his nephew [[e:francesco-maria-i-della-rovere|Francesco Maria I della Rovere]], joining it to the [[s:duchy-of-urbino|Duchy of Urbino]].

lugasi-state.t: A minor principality of the Bundelkhand Agency, one of many small holdings left from the break-up of Bundela power.
lugasi-state.o: Lugasi became a separate chiefship in the mid-18th century during the fragmentation of the [[e:bundelas|Bundela]] kingdoms, and its holder received a British sanad in the early 19th century.
lugasi-state.r: Little is recorded of its history. It was a small non-salute state of a few villages, supervised by the political agent in [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]].
lugasi-state.e: After independence Lugasi was merged with the other [[e:bundelkhand|Bundelkhand]] states into [[s:vindhya-pradesh|Vindhya Pradesh]], and its lands were absorbed into the Indian administration by 1950.

la-corona.t: A small Maya kingdom in north-western Petén, the long-sought 'Site Q', whose panels illuminate its close ties with the Kingdom of Kaan.
la-corona.o: For decades looted carved panels from an unknown 'Site Q' circulated on the art market. In 2005 the site was identified as La Corona, a modest centre in north-western [[e:peten|Petén]] whose rulers used the title of Sak Nikte'. Its dynasty is attested from the [[e:early-classic-period|Early Classic]], around 500 CE.
la-corona.r: La Corona lay on a route between [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Calakmul]] and the south, and its kings were loyal [[e:vassal|vassals]] of the Kingdom of Kaan, receiving Kaan princesses as royal brides. Its panels record journeys of local lords to Calakmul and ballgame rituals. In 2012 archaeologists found a stairway block that mentions the bak'tun ending of 2012 in a text about a visit by the Kaan king [[e:yuknoom-yichaak-kahk|Yuknoom Yich'aak K'ahk']] in 696.
la-corona.e: With Kaan's decline in the 8th century, La Corona's power waned, and it was abandoned around 800 CE. It shows how the [[s:kingdom-of-kaan|Snake Kingdom]] held its network together through marriage and patronage.

landgraviate-of-hesse-marburg.t: A Hessian landgraviate centred on the university town of Marburg, whose division in 1604 set off decades of conflict between Kassel and Darmstadt.
landgraviate-of-hesse-marburg.o: The 1567 division of the [[s:landgraviate-of-hesse|Landgraviate of Hesse]] gave [[e:louis-iv-landgrave-of-hesse-marburg|Louis IV]], second son of [[e:philip-i-landgrave-of-hesse|Philip the Magnanimous]], about a quarter of the land, centred on [[e:marburg|Marburg]] and its university, founded by his father in 1527 as the first Protestant university.
landgraviate-of-hesse-marburg.r: [[e:louis-iv-landgrave-of-hesse-marburg|Louis IV]] was a strict Lutheran who defended orthodoxy against the Calvinist leanings of his brother in [[e:kassel|Kassel]]. His land was largely agrarian, with [[e:marburg|Marburg's]] castle and university at its centre. He married twice but had no children, and his will required that his heirs keep the Lutheran faith.
landgraviate-of-hesse-marburg.e: When [[e:louis-iv-landgrave-of-hesse-marburg|Louis IV]] died in 1604, his lands were divided between [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]]. [[e:maurice-landgrave-of-hesse-kassel|Maurice of Hesse-Kassel]]'s introduction of [[e:calvinism|Calvinism]] in [[e:marburg|Marburg]] broke the will's terms and started a long dispute that culminated in the Hessian War of 1645 to 1648.

langkasuka.t: An early Malay port kingdom on the Kra Isthmus near modern Pattani, linking Indian Ocean and South China Sea trade for over a thousand years.
langkasuka.o: Chinese annals of the [[s:liang-dynasty|Liang dynasty]] say the kingdom of Lang-ya-xiu was founded around the 2nd century, more than 400 years before their own time. It grew up on the eastern side of the [[e:malay-peninsula|Malay Peninsula]], where traders crossed the narrow isthmus by land to avoid the long voyage round the peninsula. Excavations at [[e:yarang|Yarang]], near [[s:pattani-kingdom|Pattani]], have revealed brick religious buildings of the period.
langkasuka.r: Chinese sources describe a walled city, a king who rode an elephant under a white canopy, and a court that followed [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] and Buddhist practice. In 515 King [[e:bhagadatta|Bhagadatta]] sent envoys to the [[s:liang-liang-shidu|Liang]] court. Its wealth came from transit trade and forest goods such as aloeswood and [[e:camphor|camphor]], and for long periods it fell within the orbit of [[e:srivijaya|Srivijaya]].
langkasuka.e: [[e:rajendra-chola-i|Rajendra Chola]]'s [[s:thanjavur-maratha-kingdom|Tanjore]] inscription of about 1030 lists Ilangasogam among the places his fleet attacked in 1025. The kingdom faded in later centuries, and its name survived in the [[s:kedah-sultanate|Kedah]] chronicle [[e:hikayat-merong-mahawangsa|Hikayat Merong Mahawangsa]]. The Muslim [[s:pattani-kingdom|Pattani Kingdom]], which arose in the same area, is generally seen as its successor.
