landgraviate-of-thuringia.t: The principality of the Ludowingian landgraves at the Wartburg, a centre of courtly poetry and the home of Saint Elizabeth of Hungary.
landgraviate-of-thuringia.o: The [[e:ludowingians|Ludowingian]] family, founded by [[e:louis-vii-duke-of-bavaria|Louis the Bearded]], built up lands in [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] in the 11th century, building the [[e:wartburg|Wartburg]] near [[e:eisenach|Eisenach]] around 1067. In 1131 Emperor [[e:lothair-i|Lothair]] III raised Louis I to landgrave, giving him comital rights over Thuringia, and in 1180 they also gained the [[e:county-palatine-of-saxony|County Palatine of Saxony]].
landgraviate-of-thuringia.r: Landgrave Hermann I made the [[e:wartburg|Wartburg]] a centre of [[e:minnesang|Minnesang]], hosting poets such as [[e:walther-von-der-vogelweide|Walther von der Vogelweide]] and [[e:wolfram-von-eschenbach|Wolfram von Eschenbach]]; this was later remembered as the Wartburg contest of song. His son [[e:louis-iv-landgrave-of-thuringia|Louis IV]] married [[e:elizabeth-of-hungary|Elizabeth of Hungary]], canonised in 1235 for her charity. The landgraves governed from [[e:eisenach|Eisenach]] and the Wartburg.
landgraviate-of-thuringia.e: After the [[e:ludowingians|Ludowingians]] died out with [[e:henry-raspe|Henry Raspe]] in 1247, the [[e:war-of-the-thuringian-succession|War of the Thuringian Succession]] gave [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] to the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettin]] [[e:henry-iii-margrave-of-meissen|Henry the Illustrious]] of [[e:meissen|Meissen]] in 1264, while [[e:hesse|Hesse]] broke away. The landgraviate merged with Wettin lands, ending as a separate unit in 1440.

liu-song.t: The first of the Southern Dynasties, founded by the general Liu Yu, whose Yuanjia era was a southern golden age before family murders tore the dynasty apart.
liu-song.o: [[e:emperor-wu-of-liu-song|Liu Yu]], a commander of humble origins, defeated [[s:huan-chu|Huan Chu]], the rebel [[e:sun-en|Sun En]] and the northern states of [[s:southern-yan|Southern Yan]] and [[s:later-qin|Later Qin]]. In 420 he forced the last [[s:eastern-jin|Eastern Jin]] emperor to abdicate and proclaimed the [[e:song-dynasty|Song dynasty]], with its capital at [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]]. Historians call it Liu Song to distinguish it from the later [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]].
liu-song.r: [[e:emperor-wu-of-liu-song|Liu Yu]] relied on military men and curbed the great aristocratic clans. Under his son [[e:emperor-wen-of-liu-song|Emperor Wen]], the Yuanjia era (424 to 453) brought prosperity and cultural achievement, including Fan Ye's [[e:book-of-the-later-han|History of the Later Han]] and [[e:xie-lingyun|Xie Lingyun's]] landscape poetry; [[e:zu-chongzhi|Zu Chongzhi's]] calendar followed under [[e:emperor-xiaowu-of-liu-song|Emperor Xiaowu]]. A northern offensive in 450 provoked a [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] counterattack to the [[e:yangtze-river|Yangtze]].
liu-song.e: [[e:emperor-wen-of-liu-song|Emperor Wen]] was murdered by his heir in 453, and later rulers, such as [[e:liu-ziye|Liu Ziye]] and [[e:emperor-ming-of-liu-song|Emperor Ming]], massacred their own relatives. The general [[e:xiao-daocheng|Xiao Daocheng]] gained control and in 479 forced [[e:emperor-shun-of-liu-song|Emperor Shun]] to abdicate, founding the [[s:southern-qi|Southern Qi]].

liang-dynasty.t: The southern dynasty of Emperor Wu of Liang, the great Buddhist patron whose half-century of cultural brilliance ended in the catastrophe of Hou Jing's rebellion.
liang-dynasty.o: [[e:emperor-wu-of-liang|Xiao Yan]], a member of the [[s:southern-qi|Southern Qi]] imperial clan and a noted poet, rebelled against the murderous [[e:xiao-baojuan|Xiao Baojuan]] in 501, captured [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]] and in 502 founded the Liang dynasty as [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]].
liang-dynasty.r: [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] reigned for 47 years, reforming examinations for officials and promoting learning. A devout Buddhist, he offered himself as a servant to the [[e:tongtai-temple|Tongtai Temple]] several times, so that ministers had to ransom him back, and his court encouraged vegetarianism among monks. His son [[e:xiao-tong|Xiao Tong]] compiled the [[e:wen-xuan|Wenxuan]], the classic anthology of Chinese literature. [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]] was among the largest cities in the world.
liang-dynasty.e: In 548 the defecting general [[e:hou-jing|Hou Jing]] rebelled and besieged [[e:jiankang|Jiankang]]; [[e:emperor-wu-of-han|Emperor Wu]] died a captive in 549. [[s:western-wei|Western Wei]] sacked [[e:jiangling|Jiangling]] in 554 and set up [[s:western-liang-555-587|Western Liang]] (555-587) as a puppet. In 557 [[e:emperor-wu-of-chen|Chen Baxian]] deposed the last emperor and founded the [[s:chen-dynasty|Chen dynasty]].

lobedu-kingdom.t: The Limpopo kingdom of the Rain Queens, the Modjadji, whose rainmaking power was respected far beyond its small territory.
lobedu-kingdom.o: Lobedu tradition traces the royal line to a princess who fled from the [[e:karanga|Karanga]] lands of present-day [[e:zimbabwe|Zimbabwe]] with rain medicines, settling in the Molototsi valley in the north-eastern [[s:south-african-republic|Transvaal]] by the 17th century. The kingdom was ruled by kings until around 1800, when the first queen, [[e:maselekwane-modjadji-i|Maselekwane Modjadji I]], came to power.
lobedu-kingdom.r: The Rain Queen ruled through district heads and councillors and was believed to control rain. She did not marry but received wives from subject districts, and her daughters by them formed political ties across the kingdom. Rulers as distant as the [[e:zulu-kingdom|Zulu]] and Swazi kings sent gifts to seek rain, and the Lobedu were spared by many invaders.
lobedu-kingdom.e: The kingdom resisted [[s:south-african-republic|Transvaal]] [[e:boers|Boer]] authority until a campaign in 1894 brought it under the South African Republic. The Rain Queen survived as a traditional office, and the Lobedu inspired [[e:h-rider-haggard|H. Rider Haggard's]] novel She.

lebanese-republic.t: The republic of Lebanon, founded under French mandate in 1926, whose sharing of power among religious communities defines its politics.
lebanese-republic.o: On 23 May 1926 the constitution adopted by the representative council turned [[s:greater-lebanon|Greater Lebanon]] into the Lebanese Republic, with [[e:charles-debbas|Charles Debbas]] as first president, still under the [[s:french-mandate-for-syria-and-the-lebanon|French Mandate for Syria and the Lebanon]].
lebanese-republic.r: The unwritten [[e:national-pact|National Pact]] of 1943, agreed by [[e:bechara-el-khoury|Bechara El Khoury]] and [[e:riad-al-solh|Riad Al Solh]], reserved the presidency for a Maronite, the premiership for a [[e:sunni-islam|Sunni]] and the speakership for a Shia. Independence was won in November 1943. [[s:beirut|Beirut]] became a banking, trade and cultural centre, but sectarian and social tensions, the 1958 crisis and the presence of Palestinian armed groups led to the civil war of 1975-1990.
lebanese-republic.e: The [[e:taif-agreement|Taif Agreement]] of 1989 ended the war, though Syrian troops stayed until 2005, leaving after the assassination of [[e:rafic-hariri|Rafic Hariri]]. [[e:lebanon|Lebanon]] then suffered the 2006 war, the 2019 financial collapse, the 2020 [[s:beirut|Beirut]] port explosion and the 2024 war between [[s:kingdom-of-israel|Israel]] and [[e:hezbollah|Hezbollah]]; [[e:joseph-aoun|Joseph Aoun]] became president in 2025.
lebanese-republic.re: Christianity, Sunni and Shia Islam, Druze

lordship-of-cortona.t: The Casali family's lordship over the Tuscan hill town of Cortona, which ended when the king of Naples sold it to Florence.
lordship-of-cortona.o: [[s:cortona|Cortona]], an Etruscan hill town above the [[e:val-di-chiana|Valdichiana]], had long been a self-governing commune and gained its own [[e:bishop|bishop]] in 1325. That year [[e:ranieri-casali|Ranieri Casali]], head of a leading local family, became lord of the city, which the Casali then ruled as a hereditary lordship.
lordship-of-cortona.r: The Casali governed a small territory of hill and plain between [[s:commune-of-arezzo|Arezzo]], [[s:republic-of-siena|Siena]] and [[s:commune-of-perugia|Perugia]], balancing between these neighbours and seeking imperial and papal recognition. Family murders over the succession were common. Little is known of their administration beyond the town's walls and the fortress they built.
lordship-of-cortona.e: In 1409 King [[e:ladislaus-of-naples|Ladislaus of Naples]] captured [[s:cortona|Cortona]] from the last Casali lord during his wars in central [[e:italy|Italy]]. In 1411 he sold the town to the [[s:republic-of-florence|Republic of Florence]].

league-of-prizren.t: Albanian political and military league formed in 1878 to defend Albanian-inhabited lands from partition, and the starting point of the Albanian national movement.
league-of-prizren.o: The treaties of [[e:treaty-of-san-stefano|San Stefano]] and [[e:berlin|Berlin]] in 1878 assigned Albanian-inhabited districts to [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]], [[s:serbia|Serbia]] and [[e:greece|Greece]]. On 10 June 1878 Albanian notables met in [[e:prizren|Prizren]] and formed a league to resist the partition, at first with tacit Ottoman approval, under leaders such as [[e:ymer-prizreni|Ymer Prizreni]], [[e:abdyl-frasheri|Abdyl Frashëri]] and [[e:sulejman-vokshi|Sulejman Vokshi]].
league-of-prizren.r: The league raised armed volunteers and set up local committees, mainly among Muslim landowners and highland clans, though Catholic [[e:albanians|Albanians]] also took part. It fought [[s:montenegro|Montenegro]] over [[e:plav|Plav]] and [[e:gusinje|Gusinje]] and [[e:ulcinj|Ulcinj]]. Under [[e:abdyl-frasheri|Abdyl Frashëri]] it moved from defending Ottoman territory to demanding a single autonomous Albanian province, and in 1880 it took over administration in [[e:kosovo|Kosovo]].
league-of-prizren.e: Alarmed by the league's autonomy demands and under European pressure, the Ottoman government sent Dervish Pasha's army, which crushed it in 1881. Its leaders were imprisoned or exiled, but its programme inspired Albanian nationalists until independence in 1912.

liberia.t: Africa's oldest republic, founded by settlers from the United States, which escaped European colonisation but was long ruled by a narrow settler elite.
liberia.o: Liberia declared independence on 26 July 1847, when the [[s:colony-of-liberia|Colony of Liberia]], founded by the [[e:american-colonization-society|American Colonization Society]], became a republic under President [[e:joseph-jenkins-roberts|Joseph Jenkins Roberts]]. Its constitution was modelled on that of the [[s:united-states|United States]], and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:france|France]] recognised it within a few years. The [[s:republic-of-maryland|Republic of Maryland]] was annexed in 1857.
liberia.r: [[e:americo-liberians|Americo-Liberian]] settlers and their descendants dominated politics through the [[e:true-whig-party|True Whig Party]], in power from 1878 to 1980, while indigenous peoples were long excluded from citizenship and power. Liberia lost territory to British and French colonies, and depended on loans and on the [[e:firestone-tire-and-rubber-company|Firestone]] [[e:rubber|rubber]] concession of 1926. A [[e:league-of-nations|League of Nations]] inquiry into forced labour forced President [[e:charles-d-b-king|Charles King]] to resign in 1930. [[e:william-tubman|William Tubman]] (1944-1971) opened the economy to foreign investment in iron ore and rubber.
liberia.e: A coup led by [[e:samuel-doe|Samuel Doe]] ended settler rule in 1980, and civil wars from 1989 to 2003, involving [[e:charles-taylor-liberia|Charles Taylor]], devastated the country. Elections in 2005 made [[e:ellen-johnson-sirleaf|Ellen Johnson Sirleaf]] the first elected woman head of state in [[e:africa|Africa]].

lordship-of-mecklenburg.t: The Christian lordship founded by the Obotrite prince Pribislav, whose dynasty ruled Mecklenburg from 1167 to 1918.
lordship-of-mecklenburg.o: After [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion's]] campaigns destroyed Obotrite power and killed [[e:niklot|Prince Niklot]] in 1160, his son [[e:pribislav-of-mecklenburg|Pribislav]] accepted [[e:christianity|Christianity]] and [[e:saxons|Saxon]] overlordship. In 1167 Henry restored most of his father's lands to him, except the [[s:county-of-schwerin|County of Schwerin]]. Pribislav's descendants took their title from the old stronghold of Mecklenburg near [[s:swedish-wismar|Wismar]].
lordship-of-mecklenburg.r: The lords encouraged German settlement, founding towns such as [[s:lordship-of-rostock|Rostock]], [[s:swedish-wismar|Wismar]] and [[e:gustrow|Güstrow]], several of which joined the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]]. [[e:doberan-abbey|Doberan Abbey]], founded in 1171, became the family burial place. After 1229 the lands divided into Mecklenburg, [[s:lordship-of-werle|Werle]], Rostock and Parchim-Richenberg, each with its own branch.
lordship-of-mecklenburg.e: In 1348 [[e:charles-iv|Emperor Charles IV]] raised [[e:albert-ii-duke-of-mecklenburg|Albert II of Mecklenburg]] to duke. His son Albert became King of [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in 1364. Mecklenburg remained ruled by the same dynasty, divided into [[s:duchy-of-mecklenburg|Mecklenburg-Schwerin]] and Mecklenburg-[[e:strelitz|Strelitz]], until 1918, the only Slavic-origin ruling house in [[e:germany|Germany]].

lordship-of-schellenberg.t: A small Rhine-valley lordship that the princes of Liechtenstein bought in 1699 and joined with Vaduz to create their principality.
lordship-of-schellenberg.o: The lordship took its name from the Schellenberg family, Bavarian ministeriales who settled in the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] valley in the 13th century and built castles on the [[e:eschnerberg|Eschnerberg]] ridge. After they sold their rights in the early 14th century, the lordship passed to other houses, among them the barons of Brandis, the counts of Sulz and the [[s:county-of-hohenems|County of Hohenems]].
lordship-of-schellenberg.r: Schellenberg was a rural district of a few villages, including [[e:eschen|Eschen]], [[e:mauren|Mauren]] and [[e:gamprin|Gamprin]], ruled by distant lords through a bailiff. Its peasants lived from farming and livestock and kept local assemblies. It was usually held together with the neighbouring [[s:county-of-vaduz|County of Vaduz]], and both were direct fiefs of the empire, a status that later proved valuable.
lordship-of-schellenberg.e: The heavily indebted counts of [[s:county-of-hohenems|Hohenems]] sold Schellenberg in 1699 to [[e:hans-adam-i-prince-of-liechtenstein|Prince Johann Adam Andreas of Liechtenstein]], who wanted an imperial territory to win a seat in the [[e:imperial-diet|Imperial Diet]]. In 1719 [[e:charles-vi-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Charles VI]] united Schellenberg and [[s:county-of-vaduz|Vaduz]] as the [[s:principality-of-liechtenstein|Principality of Liechtenstein]], where it survives as the [[e:unterland-liechtenstein|Unterland]].

landgraviate-of-hesse.t: Central German landgraviate that broke away from Thuringia in 1264 and, under Philip the Magnanimous, became a leading Protestant power.
landgraviate-of-hesse.o: When the Ludowingian landgraves of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] died out in 1247, [[e:sophie-of-brabant|Sophie of Brabant]] fought the [[e:house-of-wettin|Wettins]] in the [[e:war-of-the-thuringian-succession|War of the Thuringian Succession]] to secure [[e:hesse|Hesse]] for her son Henry I the Child. The settlement of 1264 separated Hesse from Thuringia, and in 1292 Henry was made an imperial prince.
landgraviate-of-hesse.r: The landgraves ruled from [[e:marburg|Marburg]] and [[e:kassel|Kassel]], expanding by acquiring the [[s:county-of-katzenelnbogen|County of Katzenelnbogen]] in 1479. [[e:philip-i-landgrave-of-hesse|Philip I the Magnanimous]] introduced the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1526, founded the [[e:university-of-marburg|University of Marburg]] in 1527, hosted the [[e:marburg-colloquy|Marburg Colloquy]] between [[e:martin-luther|Luther]] and Zwingli in 1529 and co-led the [[e:schmalkaldic-league|Schmalkaldic League]]. His bigamous second marriage weakened the Protestant cause.
landgraviate-of-hesse.e: After Philip's death in 1567, [[e:hesse|Hesse]] was divided among his four sons into [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]], Hesse-[[e:marburg|Marburg]], Hesse-Rheinfels and [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]]. [[e:kassel|Kassel]] and [[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] became the main successors, later the Electorate of Hesse and the Grand Duchy of Hesse.

liao-dynasty.t: The empire of the Khitan people, which ruled Mongolia, Manchuria and the far north of China for two centuries and gave China its medieval name, Cathay.
liao-dynasty.o: [[e:emperor-taizu-of-liao|Abaoji]] of the Yila clan united the Khitan tribes of the [[e:liao-river|Liao river]] basin and in 916 proclaimed himself emperor. In 926 he destroyed [[s:balhae|Balhae]], setting up the client kingdom of [[s:dongdan|Dongdan]]. His son [[e:yelu-deguang|Yelü Deguang]] gained the [[e:sixteen-prefectures|Sixteen Prefectures]] around modern [[e:beijing|Beijing]] from [[s:later-jin-936-947|Later Jin]] (936-947) in 938 and adopted the dynastic name Liao in 947.
liao-dynasty.r: Liao governed with a dual system: a Northern Administration for the Khitan and other nomads under tribal law, and a Southern Administration on [[s:later-tang|Tang]] lines for Chinese farmers. It had five capitals, two Khitan scripts created in the 920s, and a court that migrated between seasonal camps. [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]] flourished, as the wooden pagoda at Yingxian shows. The [[e:chanyuan-treaty|Treaty of Chanyuan]] of 1005 brought annual payments of [[e:silver|silver]] and [[e:silk|silk]] from the [[s:song-dynasty|Song Dynasty]].
liao-dynasty.e: The [[e:jurchens|Jurchen]] under [[e:emperor-taizu-of-jin|Aguda]] rebelled in 1114 and founded the [[s:jin-dynasty-1115-1234|Jin dynasty]] (1115-1234), which captured the last emperor, [[e:emperor-tianzuo-of-liao|Tianzuo]], in 1125. [[e:yelu-dashi|Yelü Dashi]] led survivors west to found the [[s:qara-khitai|Qara Khitai]].

lordship-of-toron.t: A Crusader lordship in the hills of southern Lebanon whose lords, the Humphreys of Toron, were among the great barons of Jerusalem.
lordship-of-toron.o: Around 1105 [[e:hugh-of-saint-omer|Hugh of Saint-Omer]], lord of the [[s:principality-of-galilee|Principality of Galilee]], built the castle of Toron at [[e:tibnin|Tibnin]] in the hills above [[s:tyre|Tyre]] to support raids on the city, which was still in Muslim hands. It became a lordship held by the Toron family.
lordship-of-toron.r: [[e:humphrey-ii-of-toron|Humphrey II of Toron]] was constable of the kingdom and a respected negotiator with the Muslims. His grandson [[e:humphrey-iv-of-toron|Humphrey IV]] married Isabella, heir to the throne, but refused to be made king in 1186 and later lost her when barons forced their divorce. The lordship controlled hill villages and the routes from [[s:tyre|Tyre]] to [[e:banias|Banyas]].
lordship-of-toron.e: [[e:saladin|Saladin]] took Toron in 1187, and German crusaders failed to retake it in 1197-1198. It was returned by the treaty of 1229 and passed to the [[s:county-of-montfort|Montfort]] family, but [[e:baybars|Baybars]] captured it in 1266. The castle site is still occupied by a later fortress in [[e:tibnin|Tibnin]].

cr.a: Charles William Meredith van de Velde

later-hojo-clan-domain.t: The Kanto domain of the Later Hojo, five generations of lords ruling from Odawara whose efficient administration made them the strongest power in eastern Japan.
later-hojo-clan-domain.o: [[e:hojo-soun|Ise Moritoki]], later called Hojo Soun, a minor official with ties to the [[e:imagawa-clan|Imagawa]], seized [[e:izu-province|Izu]] in the 1490s and took [[e:odawara|Odawara]] castle, traditionally in 1495. His son [[e:hojo-ujitsuna|Ujitsuna]] adopted the prestigious surname Hojo, recalling the [[e:kamakura|Kamakura]] regents, though the families were unrelated.
later-hojo-clan-domain.r: The Hojo carried out land surveys, registered [[e:vassal|vassals]] by their military obligations and simplified taxes, building one of the most systematic [[e:sengoku-period|Sengoku]] administrations. [[e:hojo-ujiyasu|Hojo Ujiyasu]] won a celebrated victory at [[e:siege-of-kawagoe-castle|Kawagoe]] in 1546 and expanded across the [[e:kanto-region|Kanto]], resisting attacks by [[e:uesugi-kenshin|Uesugi Kenshin]] and [[e:takeda-shingen|Takeda Shingen]]. [[e:odawara|Odawara]] grew into a large walled castle town.
later-hojo-clan-domain.e: [[e:hojo-ujimasa|Hojo Ujimasa]] and [[e:hojo-ujinao|Ujinao]] refused to submit to [[e:toyotomi-hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi]], who besieged [[e:odawara|Odawara]] with an immense army in 1590. After its surrender Ujimasa was ordered to kill himself and Ujinao was exiled; their lands went to [[e:tokugawa-ieyasu|Tokugawa Ieyasu]], who made [[e:edo-tokyo|Edo]] his base.

lagash.t: The best-documented Sumerian city-state, famed for the reforms of Urukagina and the statues and temple hymns of Gudea.
lagash.o: Lagash was a state of several cities, chiefly [[e:girsu|Girsu]] (modern Telloh), Lagash and Nigin, in south-eastern [[e:sumer|Sumer]]. Around 2500 BCE [[e:ur-nanshe|Ur-Nanshe]] founded a dynasty whose inscriptions record temple building and trade with [[s:dilmun|Dilmun]]. The excavations of [[e:ernest-de-sarzec|Ernest de Sarzec]] at Telloh from 1877 first revealed Sumerian civilisation to modern scholars.
lagash.r: The patron god was [[e:ningirsu|Ningirsu]], and temple estates dominated the economy. [[e:eannatum|Eannatum]] defeated [[s:umma|Umma]], as shown on the [[e:stele-of-the-vultures|Stele of the Vultures]], and his nephew [[e:enmetena|Enmetena]] recorded the first known peace treaty. Around 2350 BCE [[e:urukagina|Urukagina]] (Uru-inimgina) proclaimed reforms against abuses by officials and priests, the earliest known legal reform. After the Akkadian period a Second Dynasty flourished, and [[e:gudea|Gudea]] filled [[e:girsu|Girsu]] with diorite statues and the [[e:gudea-cylinders|Gudea Cylinders]], a long hymn on building Ningirsu's E-ninnu temple.
lagash.e: [[e:lugal-zage-si|Lugal-zage-si of Umma]] sacked Lagash, which then passed under the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]]. The Second Dynasty ended around 2110 BCE when [[e:ur-nammu|Ur-Nammu]] incorporated Lagash into the [[s:neo-sumerian-empire|Neo-Sumerian Empire]], where it remained a large province.

lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia.t: Frankish lordship of the Argolid, held by the lords of Athens and their heirs, which ended when its last lady sold it to Venice in 1388.
lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia.o: After the death of [[e:leo-sgouros|Leo Sgouros]], his last strongholds, [[e:argos|Argos]] and [[e:nafplio|Nauplia]], fell to the [[s:franks|Franks]] in 1212. The [[s:principality-of-achaea|Principality of Achaea]] granted them to [[e:otho-de-la-roche|Otho de la Roche]], lord of the [[s:duchy-of-athens|Duchy of Athens]], who held them as a fief of the prince.
lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia.r: For a century the lordship was held by the dukes of [[s:athens|Athens]], giving them a foothold in the [[e:peloponnese|Peloponnese]] and a port at [[e:nafplio|Nauplia]]. When the [[e:catalan-company|Catalans]] conquered [[e:athens|Athens]] in 1311, [[e:argo|Argos]] and Nauplia stayed loyal to the [[e:house-of-brienne|Brienne]] heirs of [[e:walter-v-of-brienne|Walter of Brienne]] and later passed to the Enghien family. Greek and Albanian farmers worked the fertile Argive plain.
lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia.e: Pressed by the [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantines]] of the [[s:despotate-of-the-morea|Despotate of the Morea]] and the Turks, the heiress [[e:marie-of-enghien|Marie of Enghien]] sold the lordship to [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1388. The Despot [[e:theodore-i-palaiologos|Theodore I]] seized [[s:argos|Argos]] first, but Venice took control, creating [[s:venetian-nauplia|Venetian Nauplia]].

lordship-of-forli.t: The Ordelaffi lordship of Forlì in Romagna, a Ghibelline house that hosted Dante and long defied papal armies.
lordship-of-forli.o: The Ordelaffi family led Forlì's Ghibellines, and in 1315 they became lords of the city. They ruled, sometimes as papal vicars and sometimes in open rebellion, over Forlì and at times [[e:cesena|Cesena]] and other [[e:romagna|Romagna]] towns.
lordship-of-forli.r: [[e:scarpetta-ordelaffi|Scarpetta Ordelaffi]] hosted the exiled [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante]] around 1303. [[e:francesco-ii-ordelaffi|Francesco II Ordelaffi]] resisted [[e:gil-alvarez-carrillo-de-albornoz|Cardinal Albornoz's]] campaign to restore papal rule for years; his wife [[e:cia-degli-ubaldini|Cia degli Ubaldini]] defended [[e:cesena|Cesena]] in 1357 until forced to surrender, and Forlì fell in 1359. The family regained the city in 1376. Forlì lived from farming the [[e:romagna|Romagna]] plain and from the condottiere careers of its lords.
lordship-of-forli.e: [[e:pino-iii-ordelaffi|Pino III Ordelaffi]] died in 1480, and [[e:pope-sixtus-iv|Pope Sixtus IV]] granted Forlì to his nephew [[e:girolamo-riario|Girolamo Riario]], joining it to the [[s:lordship-of-imola-and-forli|Lordship of Imola and Forli]].

landgraviate-of-hesse-darmstadt.t: The youngest of the Hessian landgraviates, ruled from Darmstadt, which grew into the Grand Duchy of Hesse.
landgraviate-of-hesse-darmstadt.o: The 1567 division of the [[s:landgraviate-of-hesse|Landgraviate of Hesse]] gave [[e:george-i-landgrave-of-hesse-darmstadt|George I]], youngest son of [[e:philip-i-landgrave-of-hesse|Philip the Magnanimous]], the Upper [[s:county-of-katzenelnbogen|County of Katzenelnbogen]], about an eighth of the land, with [[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] as capital. Shares of Hesse-Rheinfels in 1583 and of Hesse-[[e:marburg|Marburg]] in 1604 enlarged it.
landgraviate-of-hesse-darmstadt.r: The landgraves remained Lutheran and loyal to the emperor, unlike Calvinist [[e:kassel|Kassel]]. Louis V founded the [[e:university-of-giessen|University of Giessen]] in 1607, and in 1622 a cadet line was established as the [[s:landgraviate-of-hesse-homburg|Landgraviate of Hesse-Homburg]]. The landgraves inherited the [[s:county-of-hanau-lichtenberg|County of Hanau-Lichtenberg]] in 1736, and [[e:caroline-of-zweibrucken|Landgravine Caroline]] made the [[e:darmstadt|Darmstadt]] court a meeting place for writers, including [[e:johann-wolfgang-von-goethe|Goethe]] and [[e:johann-gottfried-herder|Herder]].
landgraviate-of-hesse-darmstadt.e: Allied with [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]], [[e:louis-i-grand-duke-of-hesse|Landgrave Louis X]] joined the [[s:confederation-of-the-rhine|Confederation of the Rhine]] in 1806 and became Grand Duke Louis I of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Grand Duchy of Hesse]], which lasted until 1918.

lordship-of-albarracin.t: A tiny independent Christian lordship in the mountains of Teruel, whose Azagra lords refused to be vassals of either Castile or Aragon.
lordship-of-albarracin.o: Around 1170 the Navarrese noble [[e:pedro-ruiz-de-azagra|Pedro Ruiz de Azagra]] obtained [[e:albarracin|Albarracín]] from [[e:ibn-mardanish|Ibn Mardanish]] of the [[s:second-taifa-of-murcia|Second Taifa of Murcia]], whom he had served. He resettled the town with Christians and declared that he held it as a [[e:vassal|vassal]] of the [[e:mary-mother-of-jesus|Virgin Mary]] alone.
lordship-of-albarracin.r: The lords of [[e:albarracin|Albarracín]] ruled a mountain territory of pasture and forest, granted a fuero to settlers and created a bishopric. Their autonomy rested on balancing between the [[s:crown-of-castile|Crown of Castile]] and the [[s:crown-of-aragon|Crown of Aragon]], and the family kept it for over a century.
lordship-of-albarracin.e: The lordship passed by marriage to [[e:juan-nunez-i-de-lara|Juan Núñez de Lara]]. In 1284 [[e:peter-iii-of-aragon|Peter III of Aragon]] besieged and captured [[e:albarracin|Albarracín]], and it was incorporated into the [[s:kingdom-of-aragon|Kingdom of Aragon]] in 1300.

lindos.t: The greatest of the three old cities of Rhodes, crowned by the sanctuary of Athena Lindia and ruled by the sage Cleobulus.
lindos.o: [[e:dorians|Dorian Greeks]] settled [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]] in the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], forming three cities, Lindos, [[s:ialysos|Ialysos]] and [[s:kamiros|Kamiros]]. Lindos, on the east coast with the island's best natural harbours, grew around its acropolis sanctuary of [[e:athena|Athena]], and joined the [[e:dorian-hexapolis|Dorian Hexapolis]] with [[s:knidos|Knidos]], Kos and [[s:halicarnassus|Halicarnassus]].
lindos.r: Lindian sailors founded [[s:gela|Gela]] in [[e:sicily|Sicily]] with Cretans in 688 BCE and traded with [[e:egypt|Egypt]] and the [[e:levant|Levant]]. In the 6th century BCE [[e:cleobulus|Cleobulus]], counted among the [[e:seven-sages-of-greece|Seven Sages]], ruled as tyrant and rebuilt the temple of [[e:athena|Athena]]. Lindos later fell under the [[s:achaemenid-empire|Achaemenid Empire]] and then belonged to the [[s:delian-league|Delian League]].
lindos.e: In 408 BCE Lindos joined [[s:ialysos|Ialysos]] and [[s:kamiros|Kamiros]] to found the new city of [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]], which became the island's capital. Lindos remained a religious centre: the Lindian Chronicle of 99 BCE lists famous offerings to [[e:athena|Athena]], and the acropolis is still a landmark.
lindos.re: Greek religion; cult of Athena Lindia

lakhmid-kingdom.t: The Arab client kingdom of the Sasanians at al-Hira, a centre of early Arabic poetry and Christianity on the Euphrates.
lakhmid-kingdom.o: The Lakhmids, or Nasrids, established themselves at [[e:al-hira|al-Hira]] near the [[e:euphrates|Euphrates]] in the late 3rd century as allies of the [[s:sasanian-empire|Sasanian Empire]]. The [[e:namara-inscription|Namara inscription]] of 328 commemorates [[e:imru-al-qays-ibn-amr|Imru al-Qays]], son of Amr, as king of all the [[e:arabs|Arabs]]; he is usually counted as an early Lakhmid ruler.
lakhmid-kingdom.r: From [[e:al-hira|al-Hira]] the kings controlled the Arab tribes of the desert fringe for [[e:persia|Persia]] and fought the [[s:ghassanid-kingdom|Ghassanid Kingdom]] on [[e:byzantine-empire|Byzantium's]] behalf. al-[[e:al-mundhir-iii|Mundhir III]] raided [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]] repeatedly in the 6th century. al-Hira was a cosmopolitan town with a large [[e:church-of-the-east|Church of the East]] community, monasteries and a court that drew poets such as [[e:tarafa|Tarafa]] and [[e:al-nabigha-al-dhubyani|al-Nabigha]], helping shape classical Arabic.
lakhmid-kingdom.e: In 602 [[e:khosrow-ii|Khosrow II]] deposed and executed al-[[e:al-numan-iii-ibn-al-mundhir|Nu'man III]], the last Lakhmid king, and replaced the dynasty with Persian governors. The loss of this buffer contributed to the Arab victory over Persian forces at [[e:battle-of-dhi-qar|Dhi Qar]] and left the frontier open to the armies of the [[s:rashidun-caliphate|Rashidun Caliphate]], which took [[e:al-hira|al-Hira]] in 633.
lakhmid-kingdom.re: Arabian polytheism, later Church of the East

lullubi.t: A people and kingdom of the central Zagros, immortalised as the defeated enemy on Naram-Sin's victory stele and on the rock reliefs of Sar-e Pol-e Zahab.
lullubi.o: The Lullubi lived in the mountains around the [[e:shahrizor|Shahrizor]] plain and the upper [[e:diyala-river|Diyala]], on the borders of modern [[e:iraq|Iraq]] and [[e:iran|Iran]]. They first appear in the late third millennium BCE as opponents of the [[s:akkadian-empire|Akkadian Empire]], whose king [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin]] defeated their ruler Satuni around 2250 BCE.
lullubi.r: The Lullubi were organised in highland chiefdoms that at times united under kings. [[e:naram-sin|Naram-Sin's]] stele, later carried off to [[e:susa|Susa]] and now in the [[e:louvre|Louvre]], shows him trampling Lullubi warriors on a mountain slope. At [[e:sar-e-pol-e-zahab|Sar-e Pol-e Zahab]] a Lullubi king, [[e:anubanini|Anubanini]], carved his own relief with the goddess [[e:inanna|Inanna]], imitating Akkadian royal art. Lowland rulers prized their lands for livestock and slaves.
lullubi.e: The Lullubi remained a frontier people for over a millennium, campaigned against by [[e:shulgi|Shulgi]], Hurrian rulers and the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]]. By the 9th century BCE their land was called [[s:zamua|Zamua]], and they fade from the record by the 7th century, absorbed into Assyrian provinces and later the Median world.

langkat-sultanate.t: A Malay sultanate of North Sumatra that grew rich from tobacco and oil under Dutch rule, and ended in the social revolution of 1946.
langkat-sultanate.o: Langkat was one of the Malay states of the east coast of [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]], between [[e:aceh|Aceh]] and the [[s:deli-sultanate|Deli Sultanate]]. Local tradition traces its royal line to the 16th century, and the register dates it from 1568. For long it was subject to Aceh and Siak. Its seat was [[e:tanjung-pura|Tanjung Pura]] on the Batang Serangan River.
langkat-sultanate.r: In the 19th century the [[e:dutch|Dutch]] recognised its rulers, who leased land for tobacco plantations. Oil was found at [[e:telaga-said|Telaga Said]] in 1885, the field that launched the Royal Dutch company. [[e:sultan|Sultan]] Musa and his son Abdul Aziz grew wealthy and built the [[e:azizi-mosque|Azizi Great Mosque]] at [[e:tanjung-pura|Tanjung Pura]]. The court was also a centre of Malay letters.
langkat-sultanate.e: In March 1946, during the social revolution in [[e:east-sumatra|East Sumatra]], armed groups attacked the Malay aristocracy. Members of the royal family were killed, among them the poet [[e:amir-hamzah|Tengku Amir Hamzah]], and the sultanate ended. Langkat is now a regency of North [[e:sumatra|Sumatra]].
ru: Abdul Aziz Abdul Jalil Rahmat Shah

lingones.t: Gallic people of the Langres plateau around the sources of the Seine and Marne, who stayed loyal to Rome during the great revolt of 52 BCE.
lingones.o: The Lingones held the uplands around [[e:langres|Andematunnum]] (Langres), between the [[s:sequani|Sequani]], the [[s:aedui|Aedui]] and the [[s:leuci|Leuci]], astride the watershed between the [[e:seine|Seine]] and [[e:saone|Saône]] basins. [[e:livy|Livy]] and [[e:polybius|Polybius]] record that part of the people joined the Celtic migrations into [[e:italy|Italy]] around 400 BCE and settled near the Adriatic coast south of the Po.
lingones.r: Like their neighbours they lived in fortified oppida, struck their own coins and profited from the routes linking the [[e:saone|Saône]] with the [[e:seine|Seine]]. Little is known of their institutions, but they were large enough to supply [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]]'s armies with grain.
lingones.e: The Lingones refused to join [[e:vercingetorix|Vercingetorix]] in 52 BCE and were rewarded with the status of an allied civitas under [[e:rome|Rome]]. In 70 CE their nobleman [[e:julius-sabinus|Julius Sabinus]] joined the revolt of the [[s:batavi|Batavi]] and proclaimed himself [[e:julius-caesar|Caesar]]; after its failure his wife [[e:epponina|Epponina]] hid him for nine years before both were executed.

ligurian-republic.t: The French-sponsored republic that replaced the old Republic of Genoa in 1797 and was annexed to Napoleon's empire in 1805.
ligurian-republic.o: In May 1797 a democratic rising in [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], supported by [[e:france|France]], overthrew the old aristocratic Republic of [[e:genoa|Genoa]]. By the [[e:convention-of-mombello|Convention of Mombello]] in June 1797 [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] reorganised it as the Ligurian Republic, with a constitution on the French model.
ligurian-republic.r: The new republic abolished noble privilege, but the French controlled its policy and took its resources. In 1800 the Austrians and British besieged [[s:republic-of-genoa|Genoa]], held by General [[e:andre-massena|Masséna]], causing terrible famine before the city surrendered shortly before [[e:battle-of-marengo|Marengo]] restored French dominance. A new constitution of 1802 restored the title of doge, held by [[e:girolamo-durazzo|Girolamo Durazzo]].
ligurian-republic.e: In June 1805 the Ligurian Republic was annexed to the [[s:french-empire|French Empire]]. After [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] fall the [[s:republic-of-genoa|Republic of Genoa]] (1814) was briefly restored before [[e:genoa|Genoa]] passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]].

cr.a: See File history below for details.

lordship-of-padua.t: The Carrara lordship of Padua, patrons of Petrarch and rivals of Venice, whose last lords were strangled in a Venetian prison.
lordship-of-padua.o: Threatened by [[e:cangrande-i-della-scala|Cangrande della Scala]], the [[s:commune-of-padua|Commune of Padua]] in 1318 elected [[e:jacopo-i-da-carrara|Jacopo I da Carrara]] as its lord. The [[e:carraresi|Carrara]] lost [[e:padua|Padua]] to the [[s:lordship-of-verona|Lordship of Verona]] from 1328 to 1337 but then returned, ruling as hereditary lords.
lordship-of-padua.r: The [[e:carraresi|Carraresi]] governed from the [[e:reggia-carrarese|Reggia Carrarese]] palace and controlled [[e:padua|Padua's]] university, which flourished. Francesco I, called the Elder, ruled from 1350, welcomed [[e:petrarch|Petrarch]] and expanded the state towards [[s:commune-of-treviso|Treviso]] and [[e:friuli|Friuli]], making him a rival of [[e:venice|Venice]]. [[e:giusto-de-menabuoi|Giusto de' Menabuoi]] frescoed the baptistery for the family. [[e:gian-galeazzo-visconti|Gian Galeazzo Visconti]] took [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]] in 1388, but [[e:francesco-novello-da-carrara|Francesco Novello]] regained it in 1390.
lordship-of-padua.e: After a long war, the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] captured [[s:commune-of-padua|Padua]] in 1405. [[e:francesco-novello-da-carrara|Francesco Novello]] and two of his sons were strangled in prison in [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1406, and [[e:padua|Padua]] remained Venetian until 1797.

luash.t: Lu'ash, an Iron Age kingdom of inner Syria centred on Hatarikka, united with Hamath under King Zakkur.
luash.o: Lu'ash occupied the land between [[s:hamath|Hamath]] and [[e:aleppo|Aleppo]], the former [[s:nuhashshe|Nuhashshe]] of the [[e:bronze-age|Bronze Age]]. Its capital [[e:tell-afis|Hatarikka]], the biblical Hadrach, is identified with Tell Afis. It emerged as an Aramaean kingdom in the 9th century BCE.
luash.r: Around 800 BCE [[e:zakkur|Zakkur]], king of [[s:hamath|Hamath and Lu'ash]], was besieged in [[e:tell-afis|Hatarikka]] by a coalition led by [[e:ben-hadad-iii|Bar-Hadad]] of [[s:aram-damascus|Aram-Damascus]]. His [[e:aramaic|Aramaic]] stele, found at Tell Afis, thanks the god [[e:baalshamin|Baalshamin]] for deliverance. The kingdom lived from grain farming and the routes of inner [[s:syrian-arab-republic|Syria]].
luash.e: Tiglath-Pileser III of the [[s:assyrian-empire|Assyrian Empire]] annexed Lu'ash in 738 BCE, making [[e:tell-afis|Hatarikka]] the capital of a province.

lordship-of-montpellier.t: The merchant town of Languedoc whose Guilhem lords founded a dynasty, whose university taught medicine, and where King James I of Aragon was born.
lordship-of-montpellier.o: In 985 the count of Melgueil granted lands at Montpellier to a man named Guilhem, whose descendants, all named William, ruled the growing town as lords. Montpellier rose quickly in the 11th and 12th centuries as a market and staging post on the road from [[e:italy|Italy]] to [[e:spain|Spain]].
lordship-of-montpellier.r: The lords governed with an active merchant community and a strong consulate. Montpellier traded [[e:spice-trade|spices]], cloth and dyes across the [[e:mediterranean|Mediterranean]], and its medical school, recognised as a faculty in 1220, became one of the most famous in [[e:europe|Europe]]. In 1204 the heiress [[e:marie-of-montpellier|Marie of Montpellier]] married [[e:peter-ii-of-aragon|Peter II of Aragon]]; their son James I was born there in 1208.
lordship-of-montpellier.e: The lordship passed to the Aragonese crown and then to the [[s:kingdom-of-majorca|Kingdom of Majorca]]. In 1349 the hard-pressed [[e:james-iii-of-majorca|James III of Majorca]] sold Montpellier to [[e:philip-vi-of-france|Philip VI]], and it joined the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]].

lordship-of-frisia.t: Friesland west of the Ems under foreign lords after the end of the Frisian Freedom, passing from Saxony to Charles V and then into the Dutch Revolt.
lordship-of-frisia.o: In 1498 [[e:maximilian-i-holy-roman-emperor|Emperor Maximilian]] named [[e:albert-iii-duke-of-saxony|Albert of Saxony]] hereditary governor of [[s:frisian-freedom|Friesland]], ending the Frisian Freedom west of the Ems. [[e:saxons|Saxon]] troops imposed their rule with difficulty against Frisian resistance and the city of [[e:groningen|Groningen]].
lordship-of-frisia.r: [[e:saxons|Saxon]] government brought new courts, including the Hof van [[s:frisian-freedom|Friesland]] founded in 1499, and taxes, resented by many [[s:frisii|Frisians]]. [[e:charles-ii-duke-of-guelders|Charles of Egmond]] of [[s:duchy-of-guelders|Guelders]] encouraged revolt, and the rebel leader [[e:grutte-pier|Grutte Pier]] raided the coasts in the 1510s. [[e:george-of-saxony|George of Saxony]] sold his rights to the future [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] in 1515, and from 1524 [[s:county-of-habsburg|Habsburg]] stadtholders ruled from [[e:leeuwarden|Leeuwarden]].
lordship-of-frisia.e: [[s:frisian-freedom|Friesland]] joined the Revolt against [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]], signed the [[e:union-of-utrecht|Union of Utrecht]] in 1580, and after the [[e:act-of-abjuration|Act of Abjuration]] of 1581 became a province of the [[s:dutch-republic|Dutch Republic]], with its own stadtholders from the [[s:county-of-nassau|Nassau]] family.

lordship-of-glamorgan.t: The largest of the Welsh marcher lordships, seized from the last Welsh king of Morgannwg by Robert Fitzhamon and ruled from Cardiff Castle.
lordship-of-glamorgan.o: Around 1093 [[e:robert-fitzhamon|Robert Fitzhamon]] overthrew [[e:iestyn-ap-gwrgant|Iestyn ap Gwrgant]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-morgannwg|Kingdom of Morgannwg]] and built a castle at [[e:cardiff|Cardiff]] inside the old Roman fort. He granted manors in the fertile [[e:vale-of-glamorgan|Vale of Glamorgan]] to his knights, while Welsh lords kept the uplands.
lordship-of-glamorgan.r: Glamorgan was a marcher lordship, held outside the ordinary English shire system with its own courts and military power. Through inheritance it passed to the earls of [[e:gloucester|Gloucester]], notably the [[e:house-of-clare|Clare family]], who built the vast [[e:caerphilly-castle|Caerphilly Castle]] in the 1260s against [[e:llywelyn-ap-gruffudd|Llywelyn ap Gruffudd]]. It later passed to the [[e:despenser-family|Despensers]], [[e:beauchamp-family|Beauchamps]] and [[e:neville-family|Nevilles]].
lordship-of-glamorgan.e: The [[e:laws-in-wales-acts-1535-and-1542|Laws in Wales Act]] of 1536 abolished the marcher lordships, and Glamorgan became a shire of the [[s:kingdom-of-england|Kingdom of England]], with [[e:cardiff|Cardiff]] its county town.

later-yan.t: Murong Chui's restoration of the Yan state on the North China Plain, which dominated the east until the Northern Wei defeated it at Canhe Slope in 395.
later-yan.o: [[e:murong-chui|Murong Chui]], a [[s:former-yan|Former Yan]] prince who had served [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]], rebelled after the [[e:battle-of-fei-river|Fei River]] defeat, proclaimed himself King of Yan in 384 and emperor in 386, with his capital at [[s:zhongshan|Zhongshan]] (modern [[e:dingzhou|Dingzhou]], [[e:hebei|Hebei]]). He reconquered much of the [[e:former-yan|Former Yan]] heartland.
later-yan.r: Later Yan combined [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] military power with Chinese administration on the [[e:north-china-plain|North China Plain]]. [[e:murong-chui|Murong Chui]] destroyed the rival [[s:western-yan|Western Yan]] in 394. His son [[e:murong-bao|Murong Bao]], however, led an army against the rising [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] and was crushed at [[e:battle-of-canhe-slope|Canhe Slope]] in 395. [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong]] Chui died in 396 after a final campaign.
later-yan.e: [[s:northern-wei|Northern Wei]] took [[s:zhongshan|Zhongshan]] in 397, and the court retreated to [[e:chaoyang-liaoning|Longcheng]] in [[e:liaoning|Liaoning]]. A branch under [[e:murong-de|Murong De]] founded [[s:southern-yan|Southern Yan]]. The last emperor, the extravagant [[e:murong-xi|Murong Xi]], was killed in 407 by [[e:feng-ba|Feng Ba]] and [[e:gao-yun|Gao Yun]], who founded [[s:northern-yan|Northern Yan]].

league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions.t: The youngest of the Three Leagues of the Grisons, formed at Davos in 1436 when the last count of Toggenburg died without heirs.
league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions.o: When [[e:frederick-vii-count-of-toggenburg|Frederick VII]], last count of the [[s:county-of-toggenburg|County of Toggenburg]], died in 1436, the ten court districts (Gerichte) he had held in the [[e:prattigau|Prättigau]], around [[e:davos|Davos]] and in the [[e:schanfigg|Schanfigg]] formed a league at Davos to keep their rights and unity. Their lords remained, but the communes now acted together.
league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions.r: The league joined self-governing communes, each with its own court and assembly, and met at [[e:davos|Davos]]. The [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]] later acquired lordship over eight of the jurisdictions, causing friction until the communes bought out those rights between 1649 and 1652. The league allied with the [[s:league-of-gods-house|League of God's House]] in 1450 and the [[s:grey-league|Grey League]] in 1471, forming the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]]. Most communes became Reformed.
league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions.e: The league ended with the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]] when the [[e:graubunden|Grisons]] were attached to the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]] in 1799, and it became part of the canton of Graubünden in 1803.

landgraviate-of-leuchtenberg.t: Upper Palatinate landgraviate whose Catholic landgraves ruled from Pfreimd until 1646, a title later revived for Napoleon's stepson Eugène de Beauharnais.
landgraviate-of-leuchtenberg.o: The lords of Leuchtenberg held a castle above the [[e:naab|Naab]] valley in the [[s:upper-palatinate|Upper Palatinate]] and rose in the late 12th century, receiving the rank of landgrave in the 1190s. Their title gave them an unusual dignity for a modest territory between the [[e:house-of-wittelsbach|Wittelsbach]] lands and [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]].
landgraviate-of-leuchtenberg.r: The landgraves ruled a small, rural territory and from 1332 resided at Pfreimd, where they later built a palace. They served the emperors and the Bohemian kings and sold or pledged lands to [[s:kingdom-of-bohemia|Bohemia]] and the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]], so their domain shrank. The house remained Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], while much of the surrounding [[s:upper-palatinate|Upper Palatinate]] turned Protestant.
landgraviate-of-leuchtenberg.e: The last landgrave, Maximilian Adam, died in 1646, and Leuchtenberg passed to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]]. In 1817 the King of Bavaria created the title Duke of Leuchtenberg for [[e:eugene-de-beauharnais|Eugène de Beauharnais]], whose descendants married into the Swedish, Portuguese and Russian royal families.

langrin-state.t: A small Khasi chiefdom in the south-western Khasi Hills, bordering the plains of present-day Bangladesh.
langrin-state.o: Hima Langrin was one of the Khasi chiefdoms of the [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]] plateau; its origins are known only from oral tradition, and the register's start date is approximate.
langrin-state.r: Langrin was headed by a [[e:syiem|Syiem]] chosen from a royal clan, with succession through the female line. Its villages lay in hilly, forested country above the [[e:sylhet|Sylhet]] plains. Little written record of its history exists.
langrin-state.e: Langrin came under British supervision in the 19th century and acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1948, joining [[e:assam|Assam]]. It is now part of West Khasi Hills district, [[e:meghalaya|Meghalaya]].

lordship-of-leinster.t: The vast Anglo-Norman liberty in south-east Ireland won by Strongbow, whose division in 1247 created the counties of Leinster.
lordship-of-leinster.o: [[e:diarmait-mac-murchada|Diarmait Mac Murchada]], deposed king of [[s:kingdom-of-leinster|Leinster]], sought Norman help and promised his daughter [[e:aoife-macmurrough|Aoife]] and succession to [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Richard de Clare]], Strongbow. After Diarmait's death in 1171 Strongbow claimed Leinster, and [[e:henry-ii-of-england|Henry II]] granted it to him as a lordship under the crown in the [[s:lordship-of-ireland|Lordship of Ireland]].
lordship-of-leinster.r: [[e:richard-de-clare-2nd-earl-of-pembroke|Strongbow]] and his successors settled knights, founded towns and built castles such as [[e:kilkenny|Kilkenny]] and [[e:ferns|Ferns]]. [[e:william-marshal-1st-earl-of-pembroke|William Marshal]], who married Strongbow's daughter [[e:isabel-de-clare-4th-countess-of-pembroke|Isabel]], developed [[e:new-ross|New Ross]], Kilkenny and many abbeys, and granted Kilkenny its charter. The lordship had its own courts, exchequer and seneschal.
lordship-of-leinster.e: The five sons of [[e:william-marshal-1st-earl-of-pembroke|William Marshal]] all died without heirs, and in 1247 the liberty was divided among his daughters' heirs, forming [[e:county-carlow|Carlow]], [[e:kilkenny|Kilkenny]], [[e:county-wexford|Wexford]], [[e:kildare|Kildare]] and part of [[s:kingdom-of-loigis|Laois]]. The [[e:butler-dynasty|Butler]] earls of Ormond later held much of it.

lordship-of-the-isles.t: The MacDonald sea lordship of the Hebrides and western Highlands, a Gaelic power so strong its lords negotiated with England as near-independent princes.
lordship-of-the-isles.o: [[e:john-of-islay|John of Islay]], a descendant of [[e:somerled|Somerled]] of the [[s:kingdom-of-argyll-and-the-isles|Kingdom of Argyll and the Isles]], styled himself [[e:lord-of-the-isles|Dominus Insularum]], Lord of the Isles, from 1336. Through marriage and royal favour he united most of the [[e:hebrides|Hebrides]] and much of the western mainland under [[e:clan-donald|Clan Donald]].
lordship-of-the-isles.r: The lords held council at [[e:finlaggan|Finlaggan]] on [[e:islay|Islay]], with a council of the isles, and patronised the [[e:iona|Iona]] abbey, galley-building, Gaelic poets and physicians. [[e:donald-lord-of-the-isles|Donald of the Isles]] fought the [[e:battle-of-harlaw|Battle of Harlaw]] in 1411 over the earldom of [[e:ross-scotland|Ross]]. [[e:john-of-islay-earl-of-ross|John MacDonald II's]] secret [[e:treaty-of-westminster-ardtornish|Treaty of Westminster-Ardtornish]] with [[e:edward-iv-of-england|Edward IV]] in 1462 planned to partition [[e:scotland|Scotland]].
lordship-of-the-isles.e: When the treaty was discovered, John lost [[e:ross-scotland|Ross]] in 1475. In 1493 [[e:james-iv-of-scotland|James IV]] forfeited the lordship, and the title was later annexed to the heir of the Scottish crown in the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]].

loharu-state.t: A small Muslim-ruled state on the edge of the Thar, granted in 1806 to the family into which the poet Ghalib married.
loharu-state.o: [[e:ahmad-bakhsh-khan|Ahmad Bakhsh Khan]], an agent who helped negotiate between the British and the ruler of [[s:alwar-state|Alwar State]] during the war of 1803, received Loharu from Alwar and [[e:firozpur-jhirka|Firozpur Jhirka]] from the British in 1806 as a reward.
loharu-state.r: His son [[e:shamsuddin-ahmad-khan|Shamsuddin Ahmad Khan]] was hanged in 1835 for arranging the murder of [[e:william-fraser-delhi|William Fraser]], the British Resident at [[e:delhi|Delhi]], and [[e:firozpur-jhirka|Firozpur Jhirka]] was confiscated, leaving the family only Loharu. The Nawabs ruled a small dry territory with a mostly [[e:hinduism|Hindu]] peasantry. The poet [[e:mirza-ghalib|Mirza Ghalib]] married into the family and was closely tied to its Delhi household.
loharu-state.e: Loharu acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947 and was merged into [[e:east-punjab|East Punjab]]; it is now in Bhiwani district of [[e:haryana|Haryana]].

lucanians.t: Oscan-speaking people who took over much of southern Italy in the 5th and 4th centuries BCE, conquering Greek Poseidonia and defeating Thurii.
lucanians.o: The Lucanians formed in the 5th century BCE from Samnite groups moving south into the mountains of modern [[e:basilicata|Basilicata]] and the [[e:cilento|Cilento]]. They absorbed or displaced earlier peoples, the [[e:oenotrians|Oenotrians]] and [[e:chones|Chones]], and pressed the Greek cities of the coast, capturing [[s:poseidonia|Poseidonia]] around 410 BCE.
lucanians.r: They lived in fortified hill settlements such as [[e:serra-di-vaglio|Serra di Vaglio]] and [[e:roccagloriosa|Roccagloriosa]], and were led in war by elected kings. Their federal sanctuary of the goddess [[e:mefitis|Mefitis]] at [[e:rossano-di-vaglio|Rossano di Vaglio]] has yielded [[e:oscan-language|Oscan]] inscriptions in Greek letters. Painted tombs at [[s:poseidonia|Paestum]] show armoured horsemen and funeral games. They defeated [[s:thurii|Thurii]] near [[e:laus|Laus]] in 389 BCE and killed [[e:alexander-i-of-epirus|Alexander of Epirus]] at [[e:battle-of-pandosia|Pandosia]] in 331 BCE.
lucanians.e: The [[s:bruttii|Bruttii]] broke away from them in 356 BCE. The Lucanians allied with [[e:rome|Rome]] in 298 BCE, then turned against it with Pyrrhus and were subdued by 272 BCE. They later backed [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]] and the [[e:social-war-91-87-bce|Social War]] rebels, and their region became the [[e:lucania|Roman Lucania]].

lipara.t: Greek city on the Aeolian Islands, founded by Cnidians, whose citizens shared land in common and fought Etruscan pirates at sea.
lipara.o: Settlers from [[s:knidos|Cnidus]] and [[s:rhodes|Rhodes]], led by the family of [[e:pentathlus|Pentathlus]], settled on [[e:lipari|Lipari]], the largest of the Aeolian Islands north of [[e:sicily|Sicily]], around 580 BCE after failing to found a colony in western Sicily. The island had been inhabited since the [[e:neolithic|Neolithic]], when its obsidian was traded widely.
lipara.r: According to [[e:diodorus-siculus|Diodorus]], the Liparaeans at first held land in common, some farming while others manned the fleet against Etruscan [[e:piracy|pirates]], and their victories were celebrated with dedications at [[s:delphi|Delphi]]. The city prospered from its harbour, alum and sea trade, and its necropolis has yielded fine pottery and [[e:theatre|theatre]] masks.
lipara.e: Lipara came under Carthaginian control in the 4th century BCE and served as a Carthaginian naval base in the [[e:first-punic-war|First Punic War]]. [[e:rome|Rome]] captured it in 252 BCE. It remained a town of Roman [[e:sicily|Sicily]], today [[e:lipari|Lipari]].

land-of-punt.t: A fabled land of incense, ebony and gold on the southern Red Sea, reached by Egyptian trading fleets for over a thousand years.
land-of-punt.o: Punt is known almost entirely from Egyptian sources. The earliest recorded expedition went out under [[e:sahure|Sahure]] of the 5th Dynasty, c. 2450 BCE, and later voyages sailed from [[e:red-sea|Red Sea]] harbours such as [[e:mersa-gawasis|Mersa Gawasis]]. Its exact location is still debated, with proposals ranging from eastern [[e:sudan|Sudan]] and [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] to the [[e:somalis|Somali]] coast, while recent isotope studies of baboon mummies point to the [[e:eritrea|Eritrea]] and [[s:federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia|Ethiopia]] region.
land-of-punt.r: [[e:egyptians|Egyptians]] prized Punt for [[e:myrrh|myrrh]] and frankincense, [[e:ebony|ebony]], [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], gold, leopard skins and live baboons. The best-known record, the reliefs of [[e:hatshepsut|Hatshepsut's]] temple at [[e:deir-el-bahari|Deir el-Bahari]] (c. 1470 BCE), show houses on stilts, domed huts, a ruler called [[e:parahu|Parahu]] and his queen Ati, and myrrh trees being loaded in baskets for replanting in [[e:egypt|Egypt]]. Nothing is known of its own language or institutions.
land-of-punt.e: References fade after the [[e:new-kingdom-of-egypt|New Kingdom]], with the last expeditions recorded under [[e:ramesses-iii|Ramesses III]] in the 12th century BCE. Punt survived in Egyptian memory as a semi-mythical 'God's Land', and some historians see it as a forerunner of the trade networks later dominated by [[s:dmt|D'mt]] and the [[e:aksumite-empire|Kingdom of Aksum]].

lobetani.t: An obscure Iberian or Celtiberian people of the Teruel highlands, known almost only from the geographer Ptolemy.
lobetani.o: The Lobetani are recorded mainly by Ptolemy in the 2nd century CE, who places them in the mountains of eastern [[e:spain|Spain]] with a town called Lobeton, perhaps near [[e:albarracin|Albarracín]] in modern [[e:teruel|Teruel]]. Their origin and language are unknown.
lobetani.r: Nothing is known of their society beyond a probable highland economy of herding, and archaeology cannot securely identify their settlements.
lobetani.e: Their territory was absorbed into [[s:hispania-citerior|Hispania Citerior]] during the Roman conquest of the interior in the 2nd century BCE. They are remembered only as a name in the ancient geographies.

league-of-lezhe.t: Alliance of Albanian lords under Skanderbeg that resisted the Ottoman Empire for a quarter of a century and became a symbol of Albanian unity.
league-of-lezhe.o: On 2 March 1444, in the Venetian-held town of [[e:lezhe|Lezhë]], [[e:skanderbeg|Skanderbeg]] gathered the leading Albanian nobles, among them the Arianiti, Dukagjini, [[e:muzaka-family|Muzaka]], [[e:thopia-family|Thopia]], Zaharia and [[e:balsic-noble-family|Balšić]] families and [[e:stefan-crnojevic|Stefan Crnojević]] of [[e:zeta-region|Zeta]]. They agreed to pool troops and revenues under his command against the [[e:ottoman-empire|Ottomans]], with [[e:kruje|Krujë]] as the centre of resistance.
league-of-lezhe.r: The league was a military alliance rather than a unified state: each lord kept his own lands, while [[e:skanderbeg|Skanderbeg]] led a mobile army that used mountain terrain to defeat larger Ottoman forces, as at [[e:battle-of-torvioll|Torvioll]] in 1444 and [[e:battle-of-albulena|Albulena]] in 1457. [[e:kruje|Krujë]] withstood Ottoman sieges in 1450, 1466 and 1467. Skanderbeg sought support from [[e:naples|Naples]], [[e:venice|Venice]] and the [[e:papacy|papacy]].
league-of-lezhe.e: The alliance frayed early, through a war with [[e:venice|Venice]] in 1447 and defections of lords. After [[e:skanderbeg|Skanderbeg]] died at [[e:lezhe|Lezhë]] in 1468, [[e:leke-dukagjini|Lekë Dukagjini]] and Venice fought on, but [[e:kruje|Krujë]] fell in 1478 and [[e:shkoder|Shkodër]] in 1479. Skanderbeg's flag and memory became central to Albanian nationalism.

lagos-colony.t: The British colony formed when the island town of Lagos was annexed in 1861, which grew into the commercial heart of what became Nigeria.
lagos-colony.o: In 1851 British warships bombarded [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]], deposed King [[e:kosoko|Kosoko]] of the Kingdom of [[e:lagos|Lagos]] and restored [[e:akitoye|Akitoye]], ostensibly to end the [[e:atlantic-slave-trade|slave trade]]. A British consul then dominated affairs, and in August 1861 Akitoye's successor [[e:dosunmu|Dosunmu]] signed a treaty ceding Lagos to [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] under pressure. It was organised as a crown colony in 1862.
lagos-colony.r: [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]] became the chief port of the [[e:bight-of-benin|Bight of Benin]], exporting [[e:palm-oil|palm oil]] and later cocoa. Its society included [[e:yoruba|Yoruba]] townspeople, Saro from [[e:sierra-leone|Sierra Leone]] and [[e:agudas|Afro-Brazilian returnees]], who built churches, schools and newspapers. Administrator [[e:john-hawley-glover|John Hawley Glover]] extended influence inland in the 1860s. From 1874 to 1886 [[e:lagos|Lagos]] was governed as part of the [[s:gold-coast-colony|Gold Coast Colony]], then became separate, and from 1895 a railway was built towards [[s:ibadan|Ibadan]].
lagos-colony.e: In 1906 [[s:kingdom-of-lagos|Lagos]] was merged with the [[s:protectorate-of-southern-nigeria|Protectorate of Southern Nigeria]], and it became the capital of [[s:colonial-nigeria|Colonial Nigeria]] in 1914. [[e:lagos|Lagos]] remained the federal capital until 1991 and is now [[e:nigeria|Nigeria's]] largest city.

liburnians.t: Seafaring Illyrian people of the northern Dalmatian coast and islands whose fast galley, the liburna, was copied by the Roman navy.
liburnians.o: Their culture can be traced from the early [[e:iron-age|Iron Age]], and from the 6th century BCE Greek sources place the Liburnians on the coast and islands between the [[e:rasa-river|Raša]] and [[e:krka-river|Krka]] rivers in modern [[e:croatia|Croatia]]. Iron Age hillforts and cemeteries such as Nin show a distinct culture already formed, with wide maritime contacts. Before Corinthian settlers took [[s:corcyra|Corcyra]] in 733 BCE, Liburnians are said to have held the island.
liburnians.r: They lived in fortified hill settlements grouped around centres such as [[e:zadar|Iader]] (Zadar), [[e:nin|Aenona]] (Nin) and [[e:skradin|Scardona]], with no single king recorded. Sea trade and raiding made them a power on the Adriatic, and their light two-banked galley became a standard warship. Greek writers claimed women held unusual authority among them. [[s:jaipur-state|Amber]] and Italian goods passed through their ports.
liburnians.e: Greek colonies such as [[e:issa-dalmatia|Issa]] and the rise of the [[s:illyrian-kingdom|Illyrian Kingdom]] cut back their sea power. They came under Roman control in the 2nd and 1st centuries BCE and were finally subdued during [[e:octavians-illyrian-campaign|Octavian's Illyrian campaign]] of 35 BCE. Their towns became Roman municipia in [[e:dalmatia|Dalmatia]].

leucas.t: Corinthian colony on the Ionian island of Lefkada, which cut a canal through its isthmus and later became the capital of the Acarnanian League.
leucas.o: Corinthians led by a son of the tyrant [[e:cypselus|Cypselus]] founded Leucas c. 640 BCE on what was then a peninsula of [[e:acarnania|Acarnania]]. The colonists dug a canal through the isthmus, making it an island. Its white cliffs at [[e:cape-lefkatas|Cape Leucatas]] were linked with the legend of [[e:sappho|Sappho's]] leap.
leucas.r: Leucas stayed close to [[s:corinth|Corinth]], fighting at Salamis in 480 BCE and with Corinth at [[e:battle-of-sybota|Sybota]] in 433 BCE, and was a member of the [[s:peloponnesian-league|Peloponnesian League]]. It was an oligarchy living from trade along the route to [[e:italy|Italy]]. In the [[e:hellenistic-period|Hellenistic period]] it joined the [[s:acarnanian-league|Acarnanian League]] and became its meeting place.
leucas.e: After the [[e:third-macedonian-war|Third Macedonian War]] [[e:rome|Rome]] separated Leucas from [[e:acarnania|Acarnania]] in 167 BCE, and it came under Roman control. The island is today's Lefkada.
leucas.re: Greek religion; cult of Apollo Leucatas

lexovii.t: Gallic people of the Pays d'Auge in Normandy, whose name survives in the town of Lisieux.
lexovii.o: The Lexovii lived between the [[e:seine|Seine]] estuary and the [[e:orne-river|Orne]], with a coastline on the [[e:english-channel|Channel]]. Caesar names them among the peoples of the Atlantic seaboard.
lexovii.r: Caesar records that in 56 BCE they killed their senators, who would not support war, and joined the coalition of [[e:viridovix|Viridovix]], showing a council of nobles similar to those of their neighbours.
lexovii.e: Defeated by [[e:quintus-titurius-sabinus|Quintus Titurius Sabinus]] in 56 BCE, they also sent troops to [[e:battle-of-alesia|Alesia]] in 52 BCE. Under [[e:rome|Rome]] their chief town was [[e:lisieux|Noviomagus Lexoviorum]], the origin of Lisieux, later a bishopric.

cr.a: Lexoviens (peuple celtique de Gaule). Autorité émettrice de monnaie

lordship-of-ravenna.t: The da Polenta lordship over the old imperial city of Ravenna, which sheltered Dante in his last years.
lordship-of-ravenna.o: In 1275 [[e:guido-i-da-polenta|Guido da Polenta]], called the Elder, took control of Ravenna, ancient capital of the [[s:roman-empire|Western Roman Empire]] and the Byzantine exarchate. His family ruled as lords and later as papal vicars within the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].
lordship-of-ravenna.r: The [[e:da-polenta-family|da Polenta]] ruled a city whose glory lay in the past, living from the farmland and salt pans of the [[e:romagna|Romagna]] coast. Guido's daughter [[e:francesca-da-rimini|Francesca]] married into the [[e:malatesta-family|Malatesta of Rimini]] and became the tragic heroine of [[e:inferno-dante|Dante's Inferno]]. [[e:guido-novello-da-polenta|Guido Novello da Polenta]] welcomed the exiled [[e:dante-alighieri|Dante]], who died in Ravenna in 1321 and is buried there. Later members of the family were often violent, and they grew dependent on [[e:venice|Venice]].
lordship-of-ravenna.e: In 1441 [[e:venice|Venice]] expelled the last lord, [[e:ostasio-iii-da-polenta|Ostasio III da Polenta]], and annexed Ravenna to the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]]. After 1509 the city returned to the [[s:papal-states|Papal States]].

league-of-gods-house.t: One of the Three Leagues of the Grisons, formed in 1367 by the bishop of Chur's subjects to stop him handing their land to the Habsburgs.
league-of-gods-house.o: In 1367 the cathedral chapter, the town of [[e:chur|Chur]] and the communes of the Engadine, [[e:bregaglia|Bergell]] and other valleys under the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-chur|Prince-Bishopric of Chur]] met to prevent [[e:bishop|Bishop]] Peter Gelyto from handing his temporal rule to the [[e:habsburg-dynasty|Habsburgs]]. Their pact became the League of God's House (Gotteshausbund), named after the cathedral.
league-of-gods-house.r: The league was a federation of self-governing communes, each with its own courts and assemblies, which sent envoys to a common diet. It allied with the [[s:grey-league|Grey League]] in 1406 and with the [[s:league-of-the-ten-jurisdictions|League of the Ten Jurisdictions]] in 1450, forming the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]], an associate of the Swiss. The [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] divided its communes, and much of the Engadine turned Reformed.
league-of-gods-house.e: The league remained part of the [[s:three-leagues|Three Leagues]] until 1799, when French forces attached the [[e:graubunden|Grisons]] to the [[s:helvetic-republic|Helvetic Republic]]. In 1803 the Grisons became a Swiss canton, and the old leagues' symbols survive in its coat of arms.

luvale-kingdom.t: A Lunda-derived kingdom of the upper Zambezi whose chiefs grew rich from the 19th-century trade in captives and beeswax before colonial partition.
luvale-kingdom.o: The [[e:lwena|Luvale]] (Lovale) trace their ruling line to [[e:lunda-empire|Lunda]] emigrants who settled along the upper [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]] in present-day [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]] and [[e:zambia|Zambia]] in the 17th century. The senior chief, Kakenge, held ritual primacy over other Luvale chiefs.
luvale-kingdom.r: [[e:lwena|Luvale]] chiefs ruled riverine villages of farmers and fishermen, and initiation and masking ceremonies, such as the makishi, were central to social life. In the 19th century [[e:ovimbundu|Ovimbundu]] traders and Portuguese-linked merchants from [[s:portuguese-angola|Angola]] bought slaves, [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]] and beeswax, and the Luvale became active raiders and middlemen, often in conflict with [[s:barotseland|Barotseland]].
luvale-kingdom.e: In 1905 an arbitration by the King of [[e:italy|Italy]] divided the [[e:lwena|Luvale]] lands between [[s:portuguese-angola|Portuguese Angola]] and British [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]]. The Luvale remain a people of both [[e:zambia|Zambia]] and [[e:angola|Angola]], and the makishi masquerade is listed by [[e:unesco|UNESCO]].

livonian-confederation.t: Loose league of the Livonian Order, bishops, nobles and towns of medieval Livonia, bound together by a common diet from 1435 until the Livonian War.
livonian-confederation.o: [[s:terra-mariana|Terra Mariana]] had long been divided among quarrelling powers. After the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]]'s crushing defeat by [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]] at [[e:battle-of-wilkomierz|Wiłkomierz]] in 1435, the Order, the archbishop of Riga, the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:tartu|Dorpat]], [[e:bishopric-of-osel-wiek|Ösel-Wiek]] and [[e:courland|Courland]], the [[e:vassal|vassal]] knighthoods and the towns agreed at [[e:valga|Walk]] (Valga) to settle disputes peacefully and defend one another.
livonian-confederation.r: The confederation had no single ruler or treasury. Its main institution was the Landtag, a diet usually held at [[e:valga|Walk]] or [[e:valmiera|Wolmar]], where the territorial lords and estates met to decide on war, peace, coinage and trade. The [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]]'s master, especially [[e:wolter-von-plettenberg|Wolter von Plettenberg]], was the leading military figure, and the Hanseatic towns of Riga, [[s:reval|Reval]] and [[e:tartu|Dorpat]] had great weight.
livonian-confederation.e: Weakened by the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and internal rivalries, the confederation could not withstand [[e:ivan-iv-of-russia|Ivan IV's]] invasion in 1558. Its members sought protection from Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]], [[e:sweden|Sweden]] and [[e:denmark|Denmark]], and in 1561 it dissolved, giving way to the [[s:duchy-of-courland-and-semigallia|Duchy of Courland and Semigallia]], the [[s:duchy-of-livonia|Duchy of Livonia]] and the [[e:swedish-estonia|Swedish Duchy of Estonia]] (1561-1721).

lower-aulaqi-sultanate.t: A coastal sultanate of the Aulaqi tribes, centred on Ahwar on the Arabian Sea, within the British Aden Protectorate.
lower-aulaqi-sultanate.o: The Lower Aulaqi Sultanate, the coastal member of the Aulaqi states, held the plain around [[e:ahwar|Ahwar]] on the [[e:gulf-of-aden|Gulf of Aden]]. It emerged as a separate polity around 1800, alongside the [[s:upper-aulaqi-sultanate|Upper Aulaqi Sultanate]] and the [[s:upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom|Upper Aulaqi Sheikhdom]] inland.
lower-aulaqi-sultanate.r: The sultans governed farming and fishing communities on the coastal plain and [[e:bedouin|Bedouin]] in the hills. The sultanate signed protection treaties with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and was part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. In the early 1960s it joined the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]], which became the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]].
lower-aulaqi-sultanate.e: In 1967 the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took control and the sultanate was abolished and incorporated into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].
